job.title: Manager, Public Relations Strategy
job.description:
The Manager, Public Relations Strategy will lead and execute proactive and strategic media relations efforts that elevate AccuWeather’s global brand, reinforce our position as the most accurate and most used source of weather forecasts and warnings in the world, and amplify our mission of saving lives and protecting property. Manager, Public Relations Strategy will report directly to the Vice President of Corporate Communications and will have direct involvement with the Director of Corporate Communications and the Media Relations Supervisor, as well as lead and mentor the corporate communications interns.

This role is responsible for developing and maintaining strong relationships with national, regional, and trade media; providing strategic guidance to secure high-impact coverage of AccuWeather's news and content; shaping compelling narratives around AccuWeather’s Superior Accuracy™, products, innovation, leadership, and enterprise solutions; and supporting executive visibility. Manager, Public Relations Strategy will serve as a key strategic advisor, ensuring consistent, timely, and accurate messaging across earned media channels in a fast-paced, high-visibility environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop and execute comprehensive media relations strategies aligned with corporate priorities, product launches, major weather events, research releases, partnerships, and company milestones
  • Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with reporters, editors, producers, and influencers across national, business, technology, science, trade, and broadcast media
  • Draft, edit, and oversee the distribution of press releases, media advisories, statements, talking points, FAQs, and executive messaging
  • Lead proactive media outreach strategy to secure coverage highlighting AccuWeather’s Superior Accuracy™, innovation, thought leadership, AccuWeather For Business solutions, and the AccuWeather Network
  • Serve as a primary media contact; manage inbound inquiries and coordinate interviews with executives, meteorologists, and subject matter experts
  • Partner cross-functionally to ensure message alignment and maximize media impact
  • Manage communications during significant weather events and time-sensitive situations
  • Monitor media coverage, analyze results, and provide reporting and insights to leadership
  • Support executive visibility initiatives and thought leadership opportunities
  • Maintain organized media lists, press materials, messaging documents, and coverage archives
  • Work with external PR agencies or vendors as needed
  • Be available to work outside of normal business hours, including nights and weekends, as needed based on company needs and events
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field
  • 2-4+ years of progressive experience in media relations, public relations, or corporate communications
  • Proven track record of securing national and top-tier media coverage
  • Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills
  • Experience serving as a spokesperson and managing media inquiries
  • Strong understanding of AP Style and media best practices
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, particularly during high-profile weather events

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Experience in broadcast, science, technology, or weather-related communications
  • Familiarity with media monitoring and distribution tools
  • Experience supporting executive communications and thought leadership platforms
  • Background working with B2B and B2C brands

Skills & Competencies:

  • Strategic thinker able to translate complex scientific and technical information into compelling media narratives
  • Strong relationship-building and interpersonal skills
  • Excellent organizational and project management abilities
  • Calm, decisive, and solutions-oriented under pressure
  • Collaborative team player with the ability to work independently
  • High level of professionalism and sound judgment
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and digital collaboration tools

 

About AccuWeather and Dr. Joel N. Myers

AccuWeather, recognized and documented as the most accurate and most used source of weather forecasts and warnings in the world, has saved over 12,000 lives, prevented injury to over 100,000 people, and saved companies tens of billions of dollars through better planning and decision-making. Over one billion people around the world rely on AccuWeather’s proven Superior Accuracy™. AccuWeather.com is the #1 weather destination globally and one of the top 100 most-visited websites in the world, and our award-winning AccuWeather app delivers detailed real-time forecasts to tens of millions of smartphones.

AccuWeather forecasts also appear on digital signage, in 700 newspapers, are heard on over 400 radio stations, and viewed on 100 television stations. The AccuWeather Network and AccuWeather NOW® reach an audience of over 250 million on cable and streaming platforms including DirecTV, Charter Communications - Spectrum, Verizon, Philo, Frndly TV, Comcast’s Xfinity X1 and Xfinity Stream, Roku, Xumo, Rockbot, Samsung, LG, and Amazon Freevee.

AccuWeather For Business serves more than half of the Fortune 500 companies and thousands of other businesses and government agencies globally.

Dr. Joel Myers, Founder and Executive Chair, established AccuWeather in 1962 and is considered the “father of modern commercial meteorology.” Myers, a leading creative thinker and visionary, has been called “the most accurate man in weather” by The New York Times and has been recognized as one of the top entrepreneurs in American history by Entrepreneur’s Encyclopedia of Entrepreneurs. Dr. Myers was inducted into the Broadcasting+Cable Hall of Fame, Class of 2026, in recognition of his role in revolutionizing weather forecasting through teaching, research, and building AccuWeather into one of the world’s major sources of weather data, forecasts, and warnings.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

To help us do this work, The Times is hiring a Director of Media Relations & Communications to support rapid response and issues management communications throughout the organization. You will advance and defend the reputation of the New York Times and its employees by creating and executing media relations strategies during emerging issues and high-stakes situations. You will be part of a team that develops and executes comprehensive rapid response strategies, handles complex media inquiries, and provides expert counsel to senior leadership on sensitive communications matters. The ideal candidate possesses exceptional judgment, a deep understanding of the media landscape, strong writing and communication skills, and the ability to thrive under pressure in a fast-paced environment.

This is a hybrid role based either in our New York City headquarters or our Washington, San Francisco or Los Angeles bureaus, reporting to the Executive Director of Media Relations and Communications. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week. This position requires regular after hours, weekend and on-call work.

Responsibilities:

Rapid Response & Media Relations: As a senior spokesperson for The New York Times, you will act as a primary media contact for urgent inquiries, implementing a robust rapid response framework and protocols to manage breaking news and critical issues across all media channels (traditional, digital, social). You will draft and rapidly disseminate accurate, consistent, and impactful statements, Q&As, talking points, and other communications materials under tight deadlines.

Issues Management: Working with colleagues across the communications team, you will develop and execute comprehensive issues management communications plans, collaborating with internal subject matter experts to gather accurate information and develop informed responses to complex issues.

You will also be responsible for reporting on your efforts in collaboration with the communications operations team. 

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree and 10+ years of increasing experience in media relations, public affairs, or corporate communications, with a significant focus on rapid response and issues management. 
  • Proven track record of successfully managing high-profile, sensitive, and complex media situations, with a strong understanding of the evolving media landscape, including traditional, digital, and social media platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to think strategically and critically under pressure, making sound judgments and rapid decisions, with experience advising and collaborating with senior executives on communications strategy.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders. 
  • Experience managing a team of seasoned crisis communicators, helping them make decisions and guiding their strategic approach.

Reporting to Operations Leadership, the Project Manager (PM) leads complex digital signage, audio, and technology deployment projects from initial handoff through final sign-off. This is a strategic, high-ownership role requiring strong governance, budget oversight, and proactive risk mitigation.

We are looking for a candidate with a strong entrepreneurial spirit—someone who takes full ownership of their projects, thrives in a fast-paced environment, thinks resourcefully when faced with unexpected hurdles, and drives continuous innovation within our operations. ABOUT HALLMARK’S INTERNSHIP PROGRAM  

We're looking for curious, creative, and consumer-focused interns who are passionate about storytelling, trends, culture, creativity, and human connection. 

This posting includes two distinct Creative Internship opportunities within Hallmark Greetings Creative .

 

Writing Studio & Greetings Editorial Intern 

This internship provides hands-on experience in creative writing, content development, editorial planning, trend research, and greeting card product strategy. Interns will partner with writers, editors, and product teams to develop consumer-focused content and concepts that help Hallmark create meaningful connections through greeting cards and related products.  

 

What you'll do 

  • Create original writing for greeting cards and related Hallmark products. 
  • Explore emerging trends, voices, and cultural insights relevant to Gen Z and Gen Alpha consumers. 
  • Learn how Hallmark plans, develops, and curates greeting card programs. 
  • Conduct editorial analysis and consumer research to identify future content opportunities. 
  • Develop concepts and editorial content that authentically connect with consumers. 
  • Partner with writers, editors, designers, and product teams throughout the creative process. 
  • Present recommendations and creative concepts to business and creative leaders. 

               

              BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 

              The following is required to be considered for this role: 

              • Pursuing a bachelor's degree in English, Journalism, Communications, Creative Writing, Advertising, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field 
              • A graduation date of December 2027, May 2028, December 2028, May 2029, December 2029, or May 2030.  

                 

                PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

                Your resume and application will stand out if you are: 

                • Demonstrated interest in writing, content creation, publishing, media, advertising, or product development 
                • Strong writing and editing skills 
                • Familiarity with social, cultural, and consumer trends relevant to Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences 
                • Experience through coursework, publications, student organizations, freelance work, or personal creative projects is a plus 

                        

                      ADDITIONAL DETAILS 

                      • A portfolio is required for this position. Your portfolio should be compiled into one PDF document that is no larger than 5 MB. If your portfolio file size is above the 5MB limit, you can submit a one-page overview of your work (see example). You can also submit a link to a personal portfolio website to supplement your uploaded portfolio. Applicants who do not upload a portfolio or one-page overview will not be considered.
                      •  Candidates selected to move forward in the interview process will be asked to complete a few brief exercises later in the process.
                      • Our internship program is 12 weeks long, starting in late May and ending in early August. 
                      • This summer internship is a hybrid position, with the flexibility to work from both our recently renovated headquarters building in Kansas City, MO, and from your summer residence within the KC metro area. 
                      • Some relocation and housing assistance is provided for interns whose permanent address is outside of the KC metro area. Relocation is required for this role. 

                             

                            Interested? Follow the application instructions below to apply. 

                             

                            APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS  

                            Along with your resume and application, please provide up to 10 samples of your own writing that demonstrate:

                            • Your unique voice
                            • A range of content types (academic, creative, journalistic, prose, verse, etc.)
                            • Ability to edit for clarity / conciseness (for example, a piece of writing that shows before and after edits)
                            • Success in writing for a variety of audiences

                             

                            You must show how you meet the basic qualifications in a resume or document you upload, or by completing the work experience and education application fields. Accepted file types are Microsoft Word (DOC or DOCX), PDF, HTML, or TXT.  

                             

                            In compliance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, Hallmark Cards, Inc. and its subsidiary companies will hire only individuals lawfully authorized to work in the United States. Hallmark does not generally provide sponsorship for employment. Employment by Hallmark is contingent upon the signing of the Employment Agreement, signing of an agreement to arbitrate in connection with the Hallmark Dispute Resolution Program, completing Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification, passing the urinalysis drug screen, education verification and satisfactory reference and background checks. 

                             

                            ABOUT HALLMARK – Because Connecting With Each Other Has Never Been More Important  

                             

                            For more than a century, Hallmark has been bringing people together and improving the relationships that matter most. That’s why millions of people all over the world connect with the Hallmark brand. It has always been a mission so much bigger than any one of us who work here. Today, we need empathetic learners, strategic thinkers, and enthusiastic visionaries with diverse experiences and skills to help us create the rest of Hallmark’s second century as we shift to a more digitally savvy, unified approach that combines the best of brick-and-mortar retail with the efficiency of dot-com spaces. Help us imagine what our next hundred years could look like!  

                            When you join Hallmark, we will go out of our way to make you feel like part of the team, even in a remote/hybrid work environment. In the day-to-day, we’ll make the best use of the skills and talents you already have. We’ll also give you leadership opportunities and show you multiple potential pathways to future success.  

                            Our culture of care for our consumers and for one another shows in the way we embrace different backgrounds, identities, and working styles, deliberately seeking out ways to be more inclusive both internally among our work groups and externally through the ings we make and sell to our retail partners and consumers. We believe that a broadly inclusive, equitable approach is also our best path to future success. We’re seeking out those who can bring a fresh perspective to our business and would love your input as someone new to our team! We can only change and grow when we intentionally include new perspectives–like yours.

job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

21GRAMS, a Real Chemistry subsidiary, is an advertising agency born to make healthcare more human. Not just in our work, but in how we conduct business, approach client relationships, and treat each other. We believe in being good to each other and hard on the work, and in creating work that makes a meaningful difference for patients, caregivers, healthcare professionals, and brands.

Job Summary

The Director, Product Design is a senior design leader responsible for setting the product design vision, raising the quality of the work, and building the conditions for teams to deliver cohesive, accessible, and effective digital experiences. This role leads complex engagements across websites, platforms, products, services, and connected ecosystems, translating user needs, brand strategy, business goals, technology constraints, and healthcare requirements into clear experience direction.

This is not solely an execution role. The Director is accountable for design strategy, client leadership, team development, resourcing, design operations, and measurable experience outcomes. They remain close enough to the work to guide critical decisions, facilitate discovery, critique design, and step into high-impact moments while enabling senior designers to lead day to day.

What You Will Do

Design Vision and Product Strategy

  • Own the product design vision and experience strategy across a portfolio of complex client engagements, connecting user needs, brand intent, business objectives, and technical feasibility.
  • Partner with Experience Strategy, UX, Product Management, Creative, Technology, Data, Medical, Strategy, and Account leadership to frame opportunities, define roadmaps, and establish measurable outcomes.
  • Lead discovery and definition activities, including stakeholder alignment, experience principles, journey framing, service blueprints, value propositions, prioritization, and product or platform planning.
  • Identify opportunities that extend beyond the immediate brief and turn them into clear, decision-ready recommendations for clients and agency leadership.

Design Excellence and Delivery

  • Set and uphold a high bar for interaction design, visual design, responsive behavior, content hierarchy, prototyping, motion, and end-to-end experience coherence.
  • Guide teams from early concepts through detailed design, validation, launch, and optimization, ensuring that strategic intent is maintained through implementation.
  • Oversee scalable design systems, component libraries, pattern governance, and documentation in Figma, working with engineering partners to improve quality and delivery efficiency.
  • Build accessibility into the work from the start, applying WCAG 2.2 AA principles and inclusive design practices rather than treating compliance as a final review step.
  • Use qualitative research, analytics, usability findings, and business measures to evaluate design decisions and recommend iteration.

Client and Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Act as a trusted senior design partner to clients, clearly articulating experience strategy, design rationale, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations to executive and working teams.
  • Lead high-stakes presentations, workshops, critiques, and decision-making sessions, creating alignment across internal and external stakeholders.
  • Partner with project and account leadership on scope, staffing, schedules, assumptions, and change management; surface delivery risks early and propose practical solutions.
  • Represent Product Design in new-business opportunities, estimates, proposals, capability presentations, and pitch work.

People Leadership and Practice Development

  • Manage, coach, and develop product designers across levels through clear expectations, actionable feedback, growth plans, and regular career conversations.
  • Create an environment where designers can do their best work, with strong critique, psychological safety, accountability, and thoughtful delegation.
  • Partner with Experience leadership on hiring, staffing, performance management, succession planning, and capability development.
  • Improve the Product Design practice through reusable methods, templates, standards, training, and responsible adoption of emerging tools, including AI-enabled workflows.
  • Contribute to a culture of collaboration across Product Design, UX, Creative, Technology, and Strategy, reducing silos and improving continuity from concept through launch.

What Success Looks Like

  • Clients see Product Design as a strategic partner, not only a production capability.
  • Teams have clear experience direction, decision criteria, and an appropriate level of design leadership from discovery through delivery.
  • Creates a more consistent, accessible, and high-quality experience across the portfolio.

Job Description:

POLITICO is looking for a Team Manager, Customer Success to manage a team of 10 Customer Engagement Specialists and develop scalable customer engagement practices that drive product adoption, customer value, Wallet Retention Rate, and retention rate across the US Professional Subscriptions business. This senior manager level role will focus on coaching and developing team members, driving team performance, and executing strategies that strengthen customer engagement and retention.


POLITICO's mission from the very beginning was to win the audience. We dedicate ourselves to providing accurate, non-partisan, impactful information to the right people at the right time so that they can act with confidence and speed. We experiment to avoid being disrupted and we have fun disrupting others. And we are not afraid to risk failure if it means being the best at what we do.


What You’ll Do:

  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of 10 Customer Engagement Specialists, fostering a high-performing team culture focused on growth, accountability, and results.
  • Partner with the Managing Director, Customer Success to develop and execute strategies that drive customer engagement, product adoption, Wallet Retention Rate, and overall retention.

  • Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, and professional development to strengthen individual and team performance.
  • Leverage customer health, usage, and engagement data to identify opportunities, address risks, and improve the customer experience.
  • Collaborate with Account Management and Customer Success leadership to align customer engagement efforts with broader business goals.
  • Partner with Product, Marketing, Technology, and Data teams to share customer insights and drive improvements across the business.

What You’ll Need:

  • Experience in Customer Success, Account Management, client services, customer engagement, or a related field, preferably within SaaS, subscription, or information services.
  • Proven experience managing, coaching, and developing customer-facing teams, with a track record of driving performance and results.
  • Ability to build and improve scalable processes that strengthen customer engagement, product adoption, and retention.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills, with a passion for developing people.
  • Analytical mindset with experience using customer data and performance metrics to identify opportunities and drive decisions.
  • Ability to collaborate across departments, manage competing priorities, and adapt in a fast-paced environment.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

COMPENSATION: $85,000 - $100,000 annual salary. This role is also eligible to participate in POLITICO’s commission plan, with a target incentive opportunity of $35,000 - $50,000, resulting in an on-target earnings (OTE) potential of approximately $120,000 - $150,000. Commission payments are variable and are based on achievement against applicable performance goals and the terms of the commission plan. Actual compensation will depend on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and other job-related considerations.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO.

Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here and email us careers@politico.com. We hope to see your application soon!

 

About Us. 

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital. 

Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes. 

Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist. 

Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself. 

These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization. 

POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. The company’s guiding principles - first articulated as  The Essentials by founder Axel Springer in the aftermath of World War II - remain a cornerstone of the company’s foundation today. Learn more about Axel Springer.

job.title: The FT World Desk Fellowship
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to inclusion and fairness

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

The Financial Times has an exciting opportunity for aspiring Black foreign correspondents.

Are you keen to report on the world at this time of tumult? Are you excited by international news and do you want a hand in interpreting and explaining it to a global audience? Are you tempted by the idea of a wide-ranging career in journalism reporting on dramatic events from across the globe? If so, then our new six-month World Desk fellowship would suit you well.   

The FT’s global, award-winning editorial team represents the gold standard in journalism, seeking depth, originality and balance that differentiates the FT from the pack and engages subscribers.

The Fellowship is a six-month, paid fellowship in the heart of the FT’s London newsroom. You will join the World News Desk, where a dozen-strong team of accomplished journalists commission and edit our global coverage.   

You will work with the editors to help deliver ground-breaking coverage. You will also work closely with our London-based regional editors, the Africa Editor, Europe Editor, Latin America Editor and Middle East Editor, helping them with their coverage.

You will support the global network of correspondents with research and ideas for how to complement their stories with the right data and visual elements. You will be encouraged to write your own stories and will have mentoring from senior FT editors, in particular the foreign editor, in how to conceive and craft an “FT story”.

 

What You Will Learn 

You will be part of a team of experienced journalists covering the world, and there may also be opportunities for short-term stints on other editorial desks. You will learn the timeless arts of writing clear crisp copy and reporting on complex and sensitive stories. 

You will also gain insight into the essential skills of cutting-edge digital journalism and story-telling. The overarching ambition of the fellowship is to help to equip you one day to be a foreign correspondent, hopefully for the FT.

 

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

The successful candidate will:

  • Display a keen interest in international affairs
  • Want to pursue a career in journalism covering global news
  • Be capable of keeping a cool head under deadline pressure
  • Care deeply about writing accurately and objectively

Some experience in journalism is preferable but not essential. Career change applications are also welcome.

This opportunity is designed for Black candidates to help to address historical under-representation in the media, and to support greater diversity.

 

How to apply

All applicants must have the right to work in the United Kingdom.

Please upload three documents:

  • CV
  • A Cover Letter detailing what you will bring to the role and why you think you are suitable
  • An unpublished article on an international story (600 words max)

 

The deadline for applications is 8pm on Sunday 15th November 2026.

 

Further information

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview and to take a short writing test. The successful applicant will join the World News Desk and report to the FT’s Foreign Editor, Alec Russell.  

This 6-month fellowship is for 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, starting in Spring 2027.

The fellow will receive a monthly bursary of £2,500.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism.  Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

 

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

job.title: Multiskilled Journalist
job.description:
About TEGNA

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news.

 

WWL WUPL-TV New Orleans, the CBS/MNTV TEGNA affiliate,  is looking for an experienced Multi-Skilled Journalist to help maintain our tradition of superior reporting and newsgathering. We are interested in finding a journalist who can create unique, memorable and well written stories, who can share them on all platforms with a mix of outstanding photography and unforgettable editing. If you're a creative storyteller who understands true multi-platform journalism and who is not bound by the methods of traditional TV news – we want to hear from you! 

Current driver's license and ability to operate news gathering vehicle to and from various locations is required.

Responsibilities: 

  • Perform authoritative, compelling live shots in a developing story or in breaking news situations
  • Develop story ideas
  • Mine the community to find sources who will keep you informed about events and ideas in their areas of expertise
  • Ability to identify, write and produce stories within a specific framework.
  • Research for facts and credibility.
  • Maintain and develop sources who will help bring our reporting to the next level.
  • Shoot, write, produce and edit on air and online content within deadlines.
  • Use creative production techniques such as graphics and new forms of media (viewer pictures, webcam interviews, etc.) to enhance stories.
  • Use social media and digital tools to research, discover and distribute content.
  • Attend editorial meetings and offer story ideas daily.
  • Write in an exciting, captivating and authentic manner.

Requirements: 

  • 1-3 years reporting experience preferred.
  • Must possess solid news judgment, display strong communication skills, creativity, and ethical decision-making skills.
  • Strong writing skills, production skills and tease writing abilities.
  • ENPS, EDIUS and Axis graphics experience is preferred.
  • Must be organized with the ability to work under constant deadlines.
  • Must be able to calmly handle live breaking news situations and changing events.
  • Proven social and digital content creation ability.
  • Knowledge of New Orleans a plus ​

Benefits: 

TEGNA offers comprehensive benefits designed to safeguard the physical, mental and financial health of our employees and their families. TEGNA offers two medical plan options for full and part-time employees through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, as well as access to dental and eye care coverage; fertility, surrogacy and adoption assistance; disability and life insurance.

Our 401(k) program offers full, part-time and temporary employees the opportunity to contribute 1% - 80% of their pay on a pre-tax basis to TEGNA’s 401(k). Contributions made up to the first 4% of pay are eligible for a 100% match from the company and are 100% vested from day one.

Regardless of participation in TEGNA medical plans, ALL employees and their eligible family members receive nine free virtual doctor’s appointments with a physician through Teladoc, and 12 free annual therapy sessions with a licensed clinician through Spring Health.

TEGNA offers a generous Paid Time Off (PTO) benefit as well as nine paid holidays per year.

job.title: Senior Vice President, Audience Development & Content Distribution
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

We are seeking an experienced, strategic, and mission-aligned executive to serve as Senior Vice President (SVP), Audience Development & Content Distribution. Reporting directly to the Chief Content Officer (CCO), this executive will bridge enterprise editorial vision with multi-platform publishing, network syndication, and station distribution strategy. While our newsroom leadership focuses on the stories we tell, you will lead how, when, where, and to whom public media journalism is delivered and experienced across our nationwide network.

The ideal candidate sits at the intersection of executive media leadership, digital strategy, and network operations—scaling quality, editorial integrity, and audience reach by building a collaborative publishing framework that aligns, empowers, and coordinates NPR, Member stations, and affiliate partners. You will oversee enterprise content roadmaps and channel distribution strategies to maximize audience acquisition, reader/listener retention, and civic impact across owned properties, third-party platforms, and member newsrooms.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.    

Responsibilities

Multi-Platform Distribution & Ecosystem Growth

  • Drive Enterprise Content Planning: Build and manage the enterprise-wide content roadmap, aligning daily news flow, major investigative series, podcasts, newsletters, and special projects across all publishing platforms to optimize newsroom capacity and audience engagement.
  • Execute Channel & Syndication Strategy: Oversee multi-platform distribution across owned digital properties (apps, web, newsletters) and third-party networks (search, social platforms, news aggregators, streaming platforms) while adapting to media consumption trends and algorithm shifts.
  • Lead Ecosystem Relationships: Build, maintain, and expand long-term executive relationships with publishers, digital-native media outlets, radio/TV syndicators, and non-profit journalism networks.
  • Optimize Audience Growth & Impact: Direct cross-functional initiatives with SEO, social media, and newsletter teams to boost discovery, retention, and measurable civic and journalistic impact.

Member Network Strategy

  • Architect Station Network Publishing: Design, govern, and scale the operational framework for network syndication, content sharing, joint reporting initiatives, and affiliate publishing across Member stations and affiliate newsrooms.
  • Cultivate Member Relationships: Serve as the central executive partner to station managers, news directors, and affiliate leaders, establishing partner advisory cadences and service standards that deliver maximum strategic value to Member stations.
  • Establish Impact & Performance Metrics: Partner with data and analytics teams to define network operational KPIs, content adoption metrics, and ROI frameworks, translating audience data into actionable strategic recommendations for editorial leadership.

Enterprise Infrastructure & Strategic Leadership

  • Modernize Publishing Workflows: Architect technology-enabled distribution workflows, enterprise CMS stacks, asset management repositories (DAM/MAM), and ethical AI tools designed for distributed network environments.
  • Manage Budget & Executive Alignment: Oversee the content operations and distribution budget, manage strategic resource allocation, and collaborate with Legal, Product, Tech, and Revenue leadership to preserve brand safety and organizational alignment.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in media strategy, content operations, audience development, or network distribution—ideally within a major newsroom, public broadcasting network, or federated media alliance.
  • Demonstrated expertise managing complex editorial calendars, media partner relationships, and multi-channel digital distribution mechanics (SEO, news aggregators, newsletters, social platforms, and streaming syndication).
  • Proven experience designing, scaling, and managing complex affiliate syndication systems, content-sharing networks, or federated member-station alliances.
  • Executive-level familiarity with enterprise publishing architecture, distributed CMS stacks, media asset management systems (MAM/DAM), and workflow automation.
  • Exceptional executive presence with a track record of building consensus, inspiring collaboration, and aligning independent station partners and cross-functional leaders around shared strategic goals.
  • Strong operational budget management experience with familiarity with network economics, membership models, or syndication structures.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep operational understanding of public radio, member-station governance, and federated media fundraising/licensing models.
  • Direct experience evaluating and implementing ethical AI, automated distribution tools, or next-generation media delivery frameworks within distributed media environments.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Strategic Publishing Vision: Ability to bridge high-level editorial vision with operational execution, aligning enterprise storytelling with multi-platform delivery mechanics.
  • Federated Stakeholder Diplomacy: Exceptional interpersonal and negotiation skills to build trust, navigate federated governance structures, and align independent partners.
  • Data-Informed Editorial Judgment: Strong competency in translating quantitative audience analytics and qualitative metrics into strategic publishing decisions.
  • Executive Change Leadership: Proven capacity to guide teams through digital transformation, process modernization, and evolving media landscapes.
  • Mission-Driven Commitment: Passion for public-interest journalism, editorial integrity, and the vital role of news in a healthy democracy.

Education Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communications, Media Studies, Business Administration, or a related field, OR equivalent practical work experience demonstrating equivalent executive capability.

Work Location & Requirements

NPR and SAG-AFTRA Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. The employee will be required to be in the Washington, D.C. office at least 3 days a week. The employee must also reside in Washington, D.C. / Maryland / Virginia.

Job Type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The anticipated U.S.-based salary range for this opportunity is $290,000 - $ 350,000 plus benefits. The displayed range reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to offer new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

 

The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.NPR Pay Range$290,000—$350,000 USD

NPR is committed to being an inclusive workplace that welcomes diverse and unique perspectives, all working toward the same goal – to create a more informed public. Qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, ancestry, age, religion, religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, lactation, and reproductive health decisions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, transgender status, gender non-conforming status, intersex status, sexual stereotypes, nationality, citizenship status, personal appearance, marital status, family status, family responsibilities, military status, veteran status, mental and physical disability, medical condition, genetic information, genetic characteristics of yourself or a family member, political views and affiliation, unemployment status, protective order status, status as a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking, or any other basis prohibited under applicable law.

job.title: Senior Staff Editor, Off Platform Graphics
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Graphics department at The New York Times seeks to hire an experienced and versatile senior visual editor to manage and execute the presentation of our graphics journalism in formats beyond nytimes.com, including social media, email newsletters and the print newspaper. This is a high-impact role designed for a senior journalist who wants to pioneer best practices and drive our off-platform visual storytelling.

You will guide the adaptation of complex graphics for audiences on social media, including Instagram, Facebook, X and other emerging surfaces. You will be responsible for coordinating strategy with the Social Visuals team and for assigning, editing and in some cases crafting graphics to meet that strategy, and help to do the same for Times newsletters, including The Morning and On Politics. And you will work with the Print Hub to coordinate production and edit graphics for the Times print edition.

You possess impeccable news judgment and have extensive experience creating and editing a wide range of types of information graphics. You operate with autonomy to proactively identify new opportunities to extend the reach of our journalism.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceptualize and execute unified visual styles that can effectively translate complex data, maps and diagrams into digestible, high-impact visual assets to fit a variety of formats.
  • Produce and edit news graphics under tight deadlines during breaking news environments.
  • Guide and edit the work of other visual journalists who translate interactives, spatial models and breaking news graphics into these formats.
  • Expertly and independently carry out all aspects of visual production, serving as the primary leader of all off-platform displays.
  • Work with the Social Visuals and Audience teams to direct the packaging of graphics journalism off-platform.
  • Maintain strong relationships and coordinate across other multidisciplinary desks (Graphics, Design, Video and the Print Hub) to track projects and establish publishing workflows.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a deputy graphics editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of professional experience producing and editing visual journalism or multimedia graphics at a major news organization.
  • Deep familiarity with visual storytelling devices, including a strong portfolio demonstrating hands-on execution of maps, charts, diagrams, 3-D modeling or motion graphics.
  • Expert proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite (specifically Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects) and Figma.
  • Experience with creating, editing or art directing graphics for a print publication.
  • Strong writing and editing skills and experience synthesizing complex information and work on strict deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with reading and editing code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).
  • Familiarity with tracking off-platform traffic trends and optimizing display assets (headlines, thumbnails, custom visual cards) to maximize audience engagement.
  • Experience managing or guiding visual journalists.

job.title: Technical Product Manager II, Data Platforms
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Mission Overview & Responsibilities:

The Data Platform mission is to help us use data to answer important questions, power user experiences, and inform strategic decisions.

The New York Times is looking for a Technical Product Manager II to shape product direction for Data Platform's Compute and Storage team. The team builds shared compute engines, lakehouse storage, and connective infrastructure so engineers can publish and own data products without managing the underlying platform.

You will partner with engineering, machine learning, analytics, and others across the company to deliver reliable, scalable, easy-to-use capabilities. You will make data infrastructure more accessible and efficient through reusable products for diverse workloads.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters in Times Square, with an expectation of working onsite 3+ days per week. You will report to the Technical Product Director of Data Platforms.

Responsibilities

  • Own the strategy for shared compute and storage capabilities, including compute engines, streaming, orchestration, lakehouse storage, and connective infrastructure.

  • Understand platform users' workflows and translate their needs into clear outcomes, requirements, and priorities.

  • Partner with engineering leaders to scope initiatives, define milestones, manage dependencies and delivery risks, and keep execution aligned with product priorities.

  • Deliver self-service capabilities that help teams build, publish, and operate data products without managing underlying infrastructure; favor reusable solutions.

  • Communicate roadmap progress, risks, and tradeoffs to stakeholders.

Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry is looking for a Group Copy Supervisor to join our growing team!  

The Group Copy Supervisor is a brand steward and category champion, responsible for having a deep understanding of the brand, its benefits, and competitive differentiation. Working with art partners and reporting to a Creative Director, the Group Copy Supervisor will own all day-to-day writing responsibilities for assigned healthcare/pharma-related HCP accounts. The ideal candidate will have the skills and experience to think strategically, supply creative ideas and concepts, and execute across a range of mediums.

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What you’ll do: 

  • Responsible for writing headlines and body copy for various types of digital tactics, including websites, interactive visual aids, videos, banners, landing pages, and emails, for branded and unbranded HCP clients
  • Convey scientific information into compelling and memorable messages for HCP campaigns
  • Champion creative thinking for campaigns and initiatives that advance creative strategy and brand personality
  • Prepare materials for client copy approval submissions, ensuring pieces are referenced and annotated according to AMA style, without supervision
  • Collaborate with Art Directors, Designers, and Developers from job initiation to digital deployment, and partner with Account and Strategy teams at all points
  • Ability to independently lead multiple projects, sometimes for different brands/industries
  • Clearly and expertly present work to clients and internal team members

This position is a perfect fit for you if: 

·  ​Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you. 

·  You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving. 

·  You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data. 

·  You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines. 

What you should have:  

  • 7+ years healthcare/pharmaceutical writing, preferably in an agency setting
  • College degree in a related field preferred
  • Experience writing for the healthcare/pharmaceutical industry
  • Portfolio or PDF of relevant work samples required

Pay Range: $135,000-$145,000
This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

Real Chemistry is proud to be Great Place to Work® certified; check out what our people shared about our culture and workplace on our Great Places to Work Profile here.

We believe we can do our best when feeling our best, which is why we’ve put together a benefits program designed to give you the support you and your family need at every stage of life. Real Chemistry offers a comprehensive benefit program and perks, tailored to your region. Globally, this includes offices in our key markets with free snacks to keep you running all day long, generous holiday and paid time off, options for private medical, dental, and vison plans, and support in saving for the future. Other perks include mental wellness coaching and support and access to more than 13,000 online classes with LinkedIn Learning.  Learn more about our great benefits and perks and search specific offerings in your region at: www.realchemistrybenefits.com.

At Real Chemistry, we believe we're at our best when we're connected. Our Real Hybrid and Regional Teams (Real HART) approach is designed to foster collaboration, learning, innovation, and meaningful relationships while providing flexibility where appropriate. Because our workforce spans multiple countries, regions, and client needs, work arrangements may vary by role and location. Some positions offer hybrid or remote flexibility, while others require regular in-office presence. For example, certain teams and regions, including some of our UK operations, have office-based requirements. Your recruiter will discuss the specific expectations for the role you're pursuing during the interview process and keep you informed throughout the hiring journey. For employees located within a one-hour commute of a Real Chemistry office, we require in-person attendance two days per week, either from a Real Chemistry office or when working onsite with clients. Employees in regions without a nearby office may work remotely and come together throughout the year for collaboration, culture-building, learning, and team connection opportunities. While these guidelines reflect our current workplace model, we understand that everyone’s circumstances are unique. If you require additional flexibility, we welcome an open conversation with your recruiter and our HR team to discuss your needs and determine what may be possible.

We continually strive to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable work environment where our employees feel empowered to leverage all they bring from their personal lived experience and professional expertise, to make our team the best in the industry. job.title: Junior Broadcast Technician - Melfort SK
job.description:
Junior Broadcast Technician

Melfort, Saskatchewan

After an incredible 51 years of service, our longtime Technical Manager in Melfort has recently retired. Pattison Media is now looking for a Junior Broadcast Technician to join our Technical Services team and help support our two radio stations in Melfort.

This is a great opportunity for someone early in their technical career who enjoys troubleshooting, working with technology and learning how things work. You don't need to arrive knowing everything about broadcast engineering. You'll be supported by Pattison Media's Technical Services team and will work closely with our Technical Services Manager in Prince Albert, who will provide ongoing technical support and mentorship.

If you have a background in electronics, IT, networking, telecommunications or broadcast technology and are interested in building a career in radio broadcast engineering, we'd like to hear from you.

What you’ll do:

  • Help maintain, troubleshoot and repair studio and broadcast equipment.
  • Assist with the operation and maintenance of radio transmission systems.
  • Support computers, servers, network equipment and other technology used by our Melfort stations.
  • Support broadcast systems including WideOrbit automation and other studio, newsroom and audio systems.
  • Assist with the installation and commissioning of new technical equipment and systems.
  • Maintain technical documentation, records and drawings.
  • Help troubleshoot technical issues affecting our on-air and business operations.
  • Work with the Pattison Media Technical Services team on technical projects and upgrades.
  • Provide day-to-day technical assistance to staff at our Melfort stations.

What we’re looking for:

  • A genuine interest in broadcasting, electronics and technology.
  • Education or experience in electronics, electrical technology, IT, networking, telecommunications, broadcast technology or a related technical field.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Basic knowledge of computers and networking.
  • Good organizational skills and an ability to follow tasks through to completion.
  • Comfortable working both independently and as part of a larger technical team.
  • Good communication skills and a willingness to learn.
  • A valid driver’s License.

Broadcast experience is an asset, not a requirement.

Previous experience working in radio or with broadcast equipment would certainly be an asset, but we're also interested in candidates with strong technical aptitude who are willing to learn.

You'll have the support of an experienced Technical Services team and the opportunity to develop hands-on experience with studio technology, radio automation, IT and networking, RF transmission systems and other broadcast infrastructure.

If you're technically curious, enjoy solving problems and are interested in building a career in broadcast technology, we'd like to hear from you.

Please apply below or submit a cover letter, resume and demo along with the completed Pattison Media Self ID Form before Friday, November 27th 2026 to:

Bill Stovold

Director, Technical Services

Pattison Media Ltd.

Bill.stovold@pattisonmedia.com

job.title: Associate, Post-Production Audio Mixer (External Agency Employee)
job.description:
NFL Films is seeking an experienced Associate, Post-Production Audio Mixer to play a critical role in bringing our stories to life through sound. This position is responsible for crafting immersive, broadcast-quality audio experiences across a wide range of NFL Films productions, including documentaries, feature programming, branded content, commercial projects, and digital media.

Working at the intersection of storytelling and technology, the Associate, Post-Production Audio Mixer will lead all aspects of audio post-production, including dialogue editing, sound design, restoration, re-recording mixing, and final delivery. The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise with strong creative instincts, understanding how sound enhances emotion, reinforces narrative, and elevates the viewer experience.

Success in this role requires exceptional attention to detail, the ability to thrive in a collaborative and deadline-driven environment, and a passion for producing world-class content that reflects the quality and legacy of NFL Films.

This role compensates at $53 to $63 per hour for this long term, benefited contract engagement.  

Essential Functions

  • Perform dialogue editing, sound effects editing, restoration, and cleanup for a variety of NFL Films productions.
  • Create original sound designs that support and enhance storytelling objectives.
  • Execute re-recording mixes for documentary, long-form, short-form, commercial, and digital content.
  • Deliver final mixes and mix stems in accordance with production, broadcast, and distribution specifications.
  • Mix and deliver content in stereo, surround sound, and Dolby Atmos formats.
  • Utilize DaVinci Resolve Fairlight and other industry-standard tools to manage audio post-production workflows.
  • Apply advanced audio restoration and repair techniques utilizing tools such as iZotope RX.
  • Collaborate closely with producers, editors, composers, and other creative stakeholders to ensure audio elements align with the creative vision.
  • Troubleshoot technical and workflow challenges while maintaining project schedules and quality standards.
  • Manage multiple projects simultaneously while meeting demanding production deadlines.

Required Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Communications, Audio Engineering, Recording Arts, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
  • Minimum of 10+ years of professional experience as a Sound Designer and/or Re-Recording Mixer in a post-production environment.
  • Demonstrated experience across documentary, sports, commercial, and long-form content production.
  • Advanced knowledge of mix stem creation and delivery workflows.
  • Extensive experience mixing in stereo, surround, and Dolby Atmos environments.
  • Strong understanding of digital audio workstations, audio signal flow, and contemporary post-production techniques.
  • Proficiency with audio restoration, repair, and cleanup tools, including iZotope RX.
  • Proven ability to maintain high-quality output while working under tight deadlines and shifting priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in sports, entertainment, or broadcast media environments.
  • Advanced proficiency with DaVinci Resolve Fairlight.
  • Familiarity with evolving audio standards and emerging post-production technologies.

Other Key Attributes

  • Strong creative instincts and a passion for storytelling through sound.
  • Collaborative team player with the ability to build effective working relationships across production teams.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Solution-oriented mindset with the ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to remain composed and productive in fast-paced production environments.

Terms / Expected Hours of Work

  • In-office position.
  • Standard schedule averages 40 hours per week.
  • Must be available to work early mornings, evenings, weekends, extended hours, and other non-standard schedules as required by production demands and delivery deadlines.
  • This job posting is for a position with one of the NFL’s third-party agency partners that provides services to the NFL. The individual selected for this role will be an employee of that third-party agency and not the NFL. All compensation, benefits, and other terms and conditions of employment are handled by the agency. The assignment to provide services to the NFL will be limited in duration but may be extended for an additional period by agreement between the NFL and the agency.

Salary / Pay Range

This job posting contains a pay range, which represents the range of salaries or hourly rates that the NFL believes, in good faith, at the time of this posting that it might be willing to pay for the posted job. The NFL expects to hire for this position near the middle of the range. Only in truly rare and exceptional circumstances, where an external candidate's experience, credentials, or expertise significantly exceed the qualifications required for the role, would the NFL consider compensation near the upper end of the range.

Salary $53—$63 USD

Benefits Information
To learn more about our comprehensive benefits offerings, please visit: NFL BENEFITS

At the NFL, in-person work at our offices is a top priority because it allows us to collaborate more effectively, build stronger connections, and maintain the culture that drives our success. This role requires onsite presence at an NFL office or stadium location, and remote and/or hybrid working options are not offered. 

NO RELOCATION ASSISTANCE WILL BE PROVIDED.

The NFL is committed to building an inclusive work environment that reflects our incredible fan base. We provide an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all employees and applicants without regard to status as protected by applicable federal, state, and local laws. 

WHO WE ARE:

NFL Core Values:

  • Respect: Everyone matters. We celebrate diverse opinions, honor hard work, and value every contribution.
  • Integrity: We do what's right, even when it's tough. We hold ourselves accountable and always follow through.
  • Team Responsibility: We support each other and our communities. No one is bigger than the game, and every action impacts others.
  • Resiliency: We set high standards, overcome adversity, and adapt to challenges, always striving for excellence.

NFL Leadership Attributes:

  • Build Talent: We develop and nurture potential, empowering individuals to grow and succeed.
  • Execute: We take action with precision, delivering results that drive our goals forward.
  • Inspire: We motivate others through vision, energy, and a commitment to excellence.
  • Live Our Values: We embody our core principles in every decision and action.
  • Know the Business: We stay informed, understand our industry, and make decisions that strengthen our position.
  • Think Big: We challenge the status quo, envision bold possibilities, and strive for transformative impact

WHO YOU ARE:

Talent Attributes:   What we expect for our employees:

  • Embody an enthusiastic, proactive can-do attitude 
  • Embrace grit, free from ego or entitlement
  • Excel as a relationship builder, with the ability to influence
  • Eager learner, driven by passion rather than just ambition
  • Encompasses an incredible work ethic with an agile mindset

The Digital Strategist will assist and strategize with key members of the sales staff including Account Executives, Account Managers, and sales leaders, to build digital solutions by leveraging ad-serving interfaces and other operational platforms. The Digital Sales Strategist’s primary responsibility is revenue generation and campaign success through pre-sales strategy, efficient campaign execution, and optimization of Digital Media campaigns in partnership with the Account Managers and Digital Fulfillment Specialists.

•    Assist in quarterly business reviews and execute strategic key digital accounts reviews.
•    Proactively monitor and analyze digital campaigns to create solutions to retain and grow our digital revenue.
•    Create case studies and communicate successful digital campaign results to the sales team.

Attending client calls if needed, as the subject matter expert on our digital product offerings.

job.title: Senior Vice President, NPR Content Strategy & Business Development
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

We are seeking a strategic, deal-driven SVP of Content Strategy & Business Development to lead the strategic expansion of our editorial reach and enterprise distribution. Reporting directly to the Chief Content Officer, this executive will serve as the primary architect and operator of our external partnership strategy. You will bridge the gap between our content production and revenue growth—identifying, negotiating, and executing strategic alliances with digital platforms, streaming networks, audio networks, and mission-aligned distribution partners.

In addition to structuring external partnerships, you will collaborate closely with enterprise stakeholders across the organization to standardize operational frameworks, direct the division’s OKR planning, and align resource allocation directly with Content’s overarching strategic objectives.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.    

Responsibilities

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Reporting directly to the Chief Content Officer (CCO), the Vice President of Talent Strategy serves as the principal architect, relationship builder, and strategic scout for creative, journalistic, and host talent across NPR. job.title: Editor, Cannonball
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company.
