The New York Times is looking for an experienced, imaginative senior editor to lead Wesley Morris's weekly culture show, Cannonball, which debuted in 2025. This role is fundamentally about partnership: working closely with one of the great cultural critics of our time to keep developing the show and reaching new heights; and leading a small team of producers to translate Wesley's critical voice, instincts, and curiosity into a show that feels as engaging as it is intellectually sharp.

The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work.

This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. You are an experienced and accomplished culture editor/writer/producer/thinker in your own right, someone with ideas about what's going on in the world of movies, TV, books, music, art and more. You have a keen sense of who the interesting critical voices in this landscape are, and a sense of how to program great guests each week. You are well-organized, someone capable of leading a multidisciplinary team through the many overlapping stages of development and production on multiple episodes at a time. You're adept at working within a larger editorial system, taking notes and other input. You have an understanding of YouTube and other social platforms where the show may travel. You have a feel for the right way to use audience data to inform editorial decision-making. You're adaptable, friendly, creative, and discerning. And above all, you're interested in and capable of doing all the work—both the glamorous and exciting stuff and the basic but necessary stuff—to build a successful show.

As senior editor of Cannonball, you will also be part of the staff of The New York Times Magazine, where Wesley is a staff writer and where the show is based. You will draw on and be part of the magazine's cultural coverage.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as an editorial partner to Wesley Morris, shaping episode ideas, refining arguments, and helping translate his voice and sensibility into a compelling episode.
  • Come up with interesting ideas for guests and manage the process of bringing them in and staging successful conversations with Wesley.
  • Lead the editorial process from pitch through final cut, including story development, scripting, structural editing, and post-production feedback.
  • Collaborate with producers, editors, and Magazine and Shows leadership to ensure editorial clarity, creative ambition, and high production quality across every episode.
  • Manage and mentor a multidisciplinary team, setting clear expectations, providing feedback, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing culture.
  • Oversee production timelines and workflows, ensuring deadlines are met without compromising quality or ambition.
  • Maintain a strong, consistent editorial voice while pushing the show to expand creatively and reach new audiences.
  • Develop new formats and concepts for a show that's still evolving.
  • Work with Magazine leadership to integrate the show into the Magazine's editorial plans, voice and design, helping the show grow into a recurring, high‑impact Magazine franchise.
  • Partner with audience, analytics, and platform teams to understand viewer and listener behavior and refine the show's format, distribution, and growth strategy.
  • Work cross-functionally with other newsroom desks and teams to identify opportunities for collaboration, guest booking, and editorial alignment.
  • Work proactively with Legal and Standards departments to keep the show free of corrections and/or legal challenges.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Magazine's Deputy Editor overseeing Culture.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience editing/producing cultural coverage—criticism, cultural reporting, and storytelling in a variety of formats.
  • 5+ years experience in audio and/or video production and editing, including managing soup‑to‑nuts production of long‑form, conversational shows.
  • Deep interest in movies, TV, books, music, art, and all forms of culture (both rarefied/literary and pop).
  • Sophisticated sense of how criticism can work to open up, explore and define a work of art by reading it closely, putting it in larger context, and registering a personal response to it.
  • Sharp instincts for the ways that ideas about culture intersect with everything else: politics, history, technology, identity, business, and everyday life.
  • Familiarity with digital storytelling formats.
  • Experience working with talent.
  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing — from structuring episodes and pacing to line editing and shaping host conversations to guiding group edits and editorial brainstorms.
  • Belief in The New York Times's mission and a strong commitment to journalistic independence, fairness and accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience with a weekly publishing cadence and in managing teams under deadline.
  • 5+ years experience managing teams, including setting expectations, giving feedback and supporting people's growth.
  • Proven ability to foster an inclusive, diverse and innovative environment, both on‑air and within the team.
  • Deep familiarity with vertical video platforms and the changing social media landscape.
  • Knowledge of YouTube and social video strategy, or a demonstrated ability to learn and apply platform best practices in partnership with audience and video colleagues.
  • Experience in Adobe Premiere.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Over the past two years, “The Interview” has made itself a trustworthy New York Times brand and a destination, where artists (Mick Jagger, Nicolas Cage, Charlize Theron), politicians (Zohran Mamdani, Chuck Schumer), athletes (Karl-Anthony Towns), influential figures in the media (Megyn Kelly, Andrew Schulz, Tucker Carlson), at the center of a story (Scott Pelley, Gisele Pelicot) and beyond sit down for thoughtful, wide-ranging, challenging, fun, news-making conversations about their lives and ideas. And now we are looking for the next Executive Producer to lead the show.

We're looking for a senior editorial leader with strong, relevant experience running a video show, working with hosts (we have two great ones: Lulu Garcia-Navarro and David Marchese) and leading show teams made up of talented staffers with audio and video backgrounds. You will drive the show's creative and editorial direction, and work to grow The Interview's already considerable audience across Times-owned platforms, YouTube and social media. You will be responsible for setting the editorial priorities, managing the production team that delivers the show each week and communicating with stakeholders across the newsroom on timely, impactful conversations. Because you will work closely with the staff of the New York Times Magazine, having experience in an ideas-driven magazine environment is a plus.

You are a curious, creative thinker, a stylish editor, a decisive and compassionate manager, and an excellent communicator. You should be comfortable working in video, excited by an evolving media landscape and motivated by booking big guests in important moments, whether that's the the definitive conversation with a Hollywood icon, a rising political star or a newsmaker at the center of a breaking story. You should be a fan of what The Interview has built, and excited to keep building and growing and evolving the show. You will report to the editor-in-chief of the New York Times Magazine.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the overall editorial and creative strategy for The Interview, setting the editorial goals and guiding the coverage for the show

  • Oversee the editorial quality of each episode, ensuring strong structure, pacing, framing and tone that aligns with the overall strategic goals of the franchise and the standards of the Times

  • Oversee workflow to ensure that several episodes at various stages of production are being made in the smartest, most efficient and sustainable way possible

  • Work closely with the hosts, booker and editor to solicit and field pitches and book a compelling mix of guests

  • Own all expressions of the show, including onsite and off-platform, all mediums (video, audio, digital), episode packaging, titles and thumbnails, in coordination with the Audience team

  • Collaborate with video operations and the Shows team to shape the visual identity of The Interview, including set design, camera approach, clips and other media to enhance each episode

  • Collaborate with the Magazine's photo, fact-checking and copy departments

  • Cultivate relationships with Times journalists across the newsroom whose valuable perspectives can be invaluable during the prep phase for any given interview

  • Lead communication with and seek feedback from the masthead on high-profile interviews

  • Manage and mentor a team of producers (some with audio backgrounds, some with video backgrounds), setting clear expectations, supporting their growth, assessing performance and providing regular feedback

  • Work with the audience team to understand audience trends and performance analysis, translating insights into recommendations

  • Create a culture of productive experimentation, because the show should never get stuck in its ways and the environment we are publishing into is always changing

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand

Basic Qualifications:

  • 15 years of experience leading editorial teams, including significant experience running a host-driven conversational audio or video show

  • Strong experience working on high profile interviews in culture and politics

  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing at the show level, from structuring episodes (both before and after the interview) and pacing to line editing and reviewing cuts

  • Experience managing and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, including hosts, audio or video producers, audience strategists and others

  • Comfortable interpreting platform analytics and audience insights to inform editorial decisions

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. The New York Times is looking for a FOIA editor to oversee and guide our strategy of using the Freedom of Information Act and other local, state and federal public records laws to obtain information from governmental and public entities.

You will serve as a hub for the newsroom’s public records requests, helping provide resources and guidance to journalists across The Times about how to maximize our ability to obtain information in the public’s interest. You will serve as a consultant to teams on effective tactics, working with reporters and editors at the inception of stories and projects to help integrate FOIA requests early in the process. You will also be responsible for developing story ideas and original coverage through the FOIA process, identifying opportunities to obtain public records that will generate news. You are excited to experiment with new technology and formats and collaborate with our data, visual and product teams to tell stories that resonate with our audience.

You will help track and expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals, and will work closely with the Legal department to identify efforts that merit litigation support.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office each week. The person will also work closely with our bureau in Washington and make periodic visits there. 

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and refine FOIA requests in partnership with internal stakeholders for submission

  • Serve as a consultant for teams as they design public records requests to bolster their reporting, with a priority on integrating such requests early into the process of developing stories.

  • Propose and drive story ideas based on FOIA requests and coordinate coverage across multiple desks 

  • Consult with desks to understand when and how to augment ongoing themes with FOIA requests

  • Advise journalists across the newsroom about the most effective approaches to obtain information through public records laws.

  • Develop and maintain training materials and deliver training about what information can be obtained through the federal Freedom of Information Act and similar state and local statutes.

  • Coordinate, track and help expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals.

  • Partner with the Legal department in identifying efforts to seek public information that merit litigation support.

  • Represent the Newsroom in partnership with Legal on FOIA matters

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the enterprise OR news research team.

  • 5+ years’ experience at a journalism or media company or other relevant organization.

  • Demonstrated success navigating and resolving legal issues related to public records laws. 

  • A record of collaborating and partnering with colleagues to find innovative storytelling approaches through the use of public records and other legal strategies. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in shaping the public records strategy of a news organization.

  • Conversant in local and state public records laws and practices in addition to the federal statute.

  • Deep familiarity with media law or a law degree

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters in local newsrooms or freelancers.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  1. What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  2. Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  3. Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  4. What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  5. What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  6. Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  • What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  • Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  • Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  • What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  • What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  • Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

job.description:

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Research Director, Content Insights will have a critical role informing the creation, iteration and measurement of video and video products at the New York Times. You will lead all video measurement research to inform our understanding of how video content performs across platforms, surfaces, and audience segments. You will oversee the end-to-end measurement of video effectiveness, from individual videos to longer-form recurring concepts, and translate data into relevant strategies that inform production, distribution, and editorial decisions. You will also work with product, design, and editorial teams to improve on-platform video experiences.

You will report to the Managing Director, News Products on the Audience Insights Team and will collaborate with partners across the Newsroom. You understand how to blend market research and user research methods and practices into actionable insights for an entire mission.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop audience research to support the creation and growth of video franchises and recurring shows. Drawing on research methods used by production studios and streaming networks, you'll conduct research that can inform greenlight decisions — including concept testing, pilot testing, audience appetite studies, and competitive landscape analysis.
  • Partner with video leadership to evaluate whether a format, host, or editorial premise has the demand to sustain an audience over time. For existing shows, help build longitudinal tracking that monitors audience health: loyalty, satisfaction, and reasons for churn.
  • Help build a video performance tracking program grounded in survey-based measurement, tracking metrics like awareness, recall, engagement, and sentiment among defined audience segments over time.
  • Working alongside analytics teams, you'll help establish benchmarks, monitor performance across all surfaces where video is published (owned and operated, social, streaming), and develop a consistent cadence of reporting that gives editorial, product, and business stakeholders a reliable read on how our videos are landing with audiences.
  • Lead quantitative and qualitative research among target audiences to support video strategy and format development (e.g., format preference studies, thumbnail and title concept tests, viewer satisfaction studies). Partner with video producers and editors to understand their needs and scope appropriate methodologies, from brief development through questionnaire design, survey launch, and insight delivery.
  • Manage multiple research projects and ad-hoc requests simultaneously, developing timelines and planning resources.
  • Partner or lead research on other editorial projects and franchises, such as newsletters, podcasts, or other emerging products
  • Collaborate with research partners, analytics teams, and company partners.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the quality, speed, and effect of video measurement, including recommending new vendors, tools, and methodologies.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in market research, user research, or consumer insights, with an emphasis on multimodal and product research.
  • Proficiency in both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies and experience with continuous improvement and new ideas.
  • Experience leading all facets of a tracking program, including vendor relationships, questionnaire development, data mining, and reporting.
  • Fluency in analyzing large datasets, identifying insights, and creating clear reports.
  • Experience developing timelines across multiple projects, applying project management skills.
  • Experience managing external research partners/vendors.

job.title: Technical Product Manager II, Content Data Products
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Publishing group at The New York Times builds and maintains the content management system powering all Times platforms. We empower engineering teams to evolve digital experiences while providing creators with interconnected tools to uphold our journalistic mission.

The Content Data Products team governs the centralized, compliance-cleared platform for all Times content data. Partnering closely with the New AI Products and Platforms (NAPP) team—whose Discovery Engine (search, knowledge graph, and AI) relies on our infrastructure—we ensure our rich archive is ingested, structured, attributed, and indexed across all brands (News, Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic, Games) and multimedia formats (articles, video, interactives).

  • Product Delivery: Guide the end-to-end product development lifecycle from concept to launch with high quality.

  • 3+ years of experience launching complex software products in close partnership with engineering teams.

job.title: Sr. Context Planner
job.description:
Who We Are

We are a well-established independent agency and thriving music business, built to help ambitious brands harness the power of culture to solve their biggest challenges. As a unique mix of experts in culture, technology, and storytelling, we are united by a passion to grow brands in ways that advertising alone can never do. 

We are an entrepreneurial business – not a traditional “ad agency.” That means we value resourcefulness and tenacity just as much as we value creativity and intelligence. In 2022, Translation was awarded the number three spot in Ad Age’s Agency A-List and AdWeek’s Multicultural Agency of the Year. One year before, Translation was awarded Ad Age’s Small Agency of the Year. We’re unapologetically ambitious, but we’re also a tight-knit crew.

We are looking for a Senior Context Planner to join Translation! Please note that this role is a Hybrid role: four days in office and one day remote. 

Summary

The Senior Context Planner leads integrated communications and go-to-market planning that turns brand strategy and creative ideas into audience participation. As a strategic partner to clients and colleagues across disciplines, you define where, when, with whom and why a brand should show up, giving every channel a clear role. You move quickly and independently, form and defend a clear point of view, and translate complex thinking into compelling stories, thoughtfully designed decks and actionable plans.

You pair that planning craft with cultural fluency across sports, music, entertainment and the worlds they intersect with, from creators and fandom to fashion, gaming and internet behavior. With strong social instincts and a sharp creative eye, you understand how ideas come to life in-feed, spot emerging behaviors and formats, and turn those insights into meaningful opportunities for brands.

What You'll Do

Comms Planning.

  • Translate cultural insights and creative platforms into campaign architecture, defining the role of messaging, channels, moments and partners.
  • Build phasing and sequencing that shows how the idea unfolds over time.
  • Communicate the approach clearly and visually, making complex ecosystems simple and actionable

Cultural Insights

  • Identify meaningful cultural shifts, behaviors and communities relevant to the audience and brand.
  • Frame those signals into clear implications and opportunities for strategy and creative.
  • Use research and cultural inputs to sharpen the comms approach, not just report what’s happening, and contribute insights to company thought leadership (e.g. newsletters, social, etc.) beyond client work.

Creative world-building

  • Maintain a clear narrative throughline as the idea extends across the campaign ecosystem.
  • Shape how the idea is expressed across different touchpoints while preserving what makes it distinctive.
  • Identify opportunities for participation and amplification that help the idea travel further.

Campaign casting

  • Synthesize best practices across the talent x brand landscape into clear POVs
  • Develop talent filters and casting recommendations for creators, artists and partners who credibly bring the idea to life.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Build trust through clear and persuasive presentations
  • Collaborate across departments including strategy, creative, business leadership and production, including risk assessments, case studies and awards.
  • Mentor associate and mid level Context Planners, delegating clearly and providing feedback that strengthens their craft.
  • Actively connect with the UnitedMasters team for an understanding of upcoming milestones and priority artists for casting consideration in Translation brand campaigns.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Comfortable working quickly and independently, owning deliverables with light oversight and adapting as priorities shift.
  • Able to form and defend a clear POV, using cultural insights and research to make actionable recommendations.
  • Strong comms planning instincts, connecting audience behavior, brand opportunity and campaign choreography.
  • Sharp information design and visual taste: build strong decks, shape a clear story and make complex ideas simple and actionable.
  • Cultural fluency across sports, music, entertainment and pop culture, including their intersections with creators, fandom, fashion, gaming and internet behavior.
  • A social-first thinker with a strong creative eye for how ideas work in-feed and an instinct for emerging behaviors and formats.
  • Strong collaborator across disciplines, receptive to feedback and confident presenting to internal teams and clients.
  • Resourceful in research, curious about new platforms and media opportunities, and committed to refining the work.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Possess excellent time management, organization and prioritization skills.
  • Have the proven ability to work under tight deadlines and handle pressure, while consistently paying attention to accuracy and quality of work.
  • Exercise the ability to quickly and effectively adapt to changing needs and expectations.                                                                                        

Preferred Qualifications

  • Minimum 4-7 years experience in a strategic position in an agency or brand environment
  • 4-year college degree in Marketing, Advertising or Business preferred.
  • Digitally savvy; MUST be proficient in Google Suite and Keynote (Mac preferred).

About UnitedMasters Inc.

UnitedMasters Inc. represents the creative solutions company, Translation, and the leading software and services platform for independent creators, UnitedMasters. UnitedMasters enables ownership, exposure, and new paths for financial return for independent creators, while Translation helps brands leverage the power of contemporary culture to achieve transformational growth. Combined, UnitedMasters, Inc. is the world’s leading marketplace for cultural capital, connecting independent artists and brands to realize a future in which all creators own their future. Backed by Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz, and Apple, UnitedMasters, Inc. is reimagining how brands and artists come together to tell their stories, build profitable growth, and push culture forward.

Salary Hiring Range: $93,000 - $110,000

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of many compensation, benefits and other reward opportunities we provide (e.g. bonus, stock options, 401(k) match, etc.)

Individual pay rate decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to peers at the company.  We expect the majority of the candidates who are offered roles at our company to fall healthily throughout the range based on these factors. 

The range above is for the expectations as laid out in the job description, however we are often open to a wide variety of profiles, and recognize that the person we hire may be less experienced (or more senior) than this job description as posted.  If that ends up being the case, the updated salary range will be communicated with you as a candidate.

The salary range above is for the NY/CA.  As a company, we have a location based strategy, which means the salary range could be lower or higher than this if the role is hired in another location.

The Senior Manager owns paid social strategy and execution for client projects of moderate scope with limited oversight. This person translates business objectives into effective channel approaches, solves complex activation challenges and develops compelling performance stories tied to client outcomes.

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. KPNX-TV Phoenix, the TEGNA NBC in Phoenix seeks a full-time Broadcast Engineer to join the Technology team. This position is responsible for the day-to-day hands-on maintenance of the station’s technical equipment including traditional broadcast hardware and industry specific software.

Current driver’s license and ability to operate news gathering vehicle to and from various locations required

job.title: Senior Manager, Evidence & Insights (RWE & HEOR)
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry is looking for an Senior Manager join our growing Evidence & Insights team! 

The Senior Manager, Evidence & Insights provides strategic and scientific support across real-world evidence (RWE), health economics and outcomes research (HEOR), and evidence generation. This role co-leads client engagements end-to-end, helping to shape evidence strategies, oversee analytics and deliverables, and advise biopharma and related stakeholders. 

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Indianapolis, or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What you'll do: 

  • Co-lead and support RWE and HEOR strategy across client programs, including evidence planning, study design, and interpretation of findings to inform value, access, and payer and health system decision-making. 
  • Design and support evidence generation plans (e.g., RWE studies, retrospective database studies, economic models) aligned to product lifecycle needs and client requirements. 
  • Develop and oversee the process for systematic literature reviews (SLRs), including the development of study protocols, execution of study searches, delegation of screening, and oversight of data extraction and reporting (leveraging the Nested Knowledge platform where possible).
  • Translate complex real-world datasets and outcomes evidence into clear, defensible insights and recommendations for clients (clinical, economic, and utilization outcomes). 
  • Serve as a client co-lead alongside Director and VP: build trusted relationships, guide strategic direction, and ensure work products meet scientific rigor, timelines, and client expectations. 
  • Directly manage staff planning, internal and external project timelines, internal and external communications, and budgets to ensure projects are adequately staffed, managed, and executed.
  • Stay current on evolving evidence standards and trends impacting access decisions, including: 
    • HTA requirements and value frameworks 
    • Payer evidence expectations and comparative effectiveness 
    • RWE guidance and regulatory considerations 
    • Measurement/reporting of quality, performance, and outcomes 
  • Co-lead scoping and resourcing for engagements: define scope of work, timelines, budgets, and staffing plans; proactively manage risks and changes. 
  • Partner cross-functionally to connect evidence strategy to broader client objectives and account growth. 

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.
  • You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines. 

What you should have: 

  • 3-5+ years of relevant experience in HEOR, RWE, SLR, epidemiology, outcomes research, market access strategy, or closely related fields (consulting and/or biopharma experience preferred). 
  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree strongly preferred (MPH, PhD, PharmD, MD, MS, or equivalent) in health economics, epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, health services research, or related discipline. 
  • Demonstrated expertise in HEOR/RWE study design and execution and ability to translate evidence into access-relevant strategy. 
  • Strong project/program leadership experience, including managing teams on complex, multi-workstream engagements and ensuring scientific and editorial quality. 
  • Excellent writing, editing, and executive communication skills; ability to craft clear narratives from technical analyses. 
  • Strong analytical fluency and comfort engaging with complex datasets and statistical outputs (hands-on analytics not required but highly valued). 
  • Client-service orientation, sound judgment, high attention to detail, and ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Outlook). 

 Pay Range: $90,000-$110,000

This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

job.title: Account Executive
job.description:
About TEGNA

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news.

 

WKYC-TV Cleveland, the TEGNA-owned NBC affiliate in Cleveland, is seeking a proven, results-driven Account Executive to grow new business and manage a book of advertising clients across one of the strongest cross-screen portfolios in the market. This is a seat for a closer who can walk into a business owner's office or an agency pitch, uncover what's really driving their marketing decisions, and build the multi-platform solution that wins the budget. 

You'll sell the full weight of TEGNA: the mass reach and trust of NBC broadcast television paired with the targeting and growth of streaming. On the linear side, you'll connect advertisers to the large, engaged local audiences that tune in to Cleveland's trusted news and programming. On the streaming side, you’ll leverage Premion, TEGNA’s streaming and CTV advertising business, to deliver premium, brand-safe connected-TV inventory. Premion’s curated marketplace includes 125+ OTT and CTV publishers, offering the same premium environments national buyers demand. Layered with digital video, display, and content solutions, it's a cross-screen story few competitors can match and in your hands, a clear advantage in every pitch. 

We give experienced sellers the portfolio, the autonomy, and the support to build something significant. Top performers grow their books, their earnings, and their careers. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Drive new business. Build and maintain a strong pipeline of local and regional advertisers, connect with key decision-makers and create opportunities across broadcast TV, Premion streaming/CTV and digital.
  • Sell strategically and consultatively. Uncover each client's real business goals, read the market and competitive landscape, and architect tailored, multi-platform solutions that tie directly to measurable outcomes. 
  • Own the full sales cycle. Prospect, qualify, present, negotiate and close business while consistently meeting activity and revenue targets.
  • Grow and defend the book. Turn accounts into long-term partnerships; expand them through smart upsell and cross-sell across the portfolio and stay close enough to results to renew and grow every cycle. 
  • Pitch with data. Build compelling, insight-driven proposals that show advertisers exactly how broadcast reach and connected-TV targeting combine to deliver ROI.

job.description:

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. We are interested in finding a journalist who can create unique, memorable and well written stories, who can share them on all platforms.
St. Louis is filled with incredible people, neighborhoods, restaurants, businesses, nonprofits, attractions and experiences, and we’re looking for someone who is excited to tell their stories.

•    Shoot, write, edit and report compelling lifestyle and community stories.
•    Conduct engaging interviews both in studio and in the field.
•    Develop original content showcasing the people, places, businesses, food, entertainment, nonprofits and experiences that make the St. Louis region unique.

job.title: Manager, Corporate Development, Asia
job.description:
Established in 1997, Sony Music Entertainment is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, Japan, with a presence in over 100 countries through our affiliates. We have nurtured some of music's most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Sony Music's Corporate Development team for Asia & the Middle East works across some of the highest-growth music markets in the world, and has been behind many of the region's most significant transactions. Our work spans M&A and minority investments in music and entertainment businesses, music IP catalogue acquisitions, and strategic joint ventures.

We're seeking a highly analytical Manager to join us, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development, Asia & Middle East. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in financial modeling, commercial analysis, and deal execution, with a genuine interest in music, entertainment, and media.

 

What you will do:

  • Financial Modeling: Build and own the financial models underpinning valuation and deal structuring.
  • Commercial Analysis: Conduct industry and competitor analysis to evaluate potential acquisition and investment targets, joint ventures, and strategic initiatives.
  • Due Diligence: Participate in all aspects of due diligence, including financial, tax, legal, and operational; coordinate with external advisors and cross-functional teams across Asia, London, and New York.
  • Deal Execution: Support the end-to-end deal process from initial assessment through closing.

  • Internal Reporting: Maintain the regional deal pipeline and report on the performance of completed investments against the original investment thesis.

 

Who you are:

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, business, economics, engineering, or a quantitative discipline. MBA, CFA, or an equivalent advanced credential is a plus.
  • Minimum of five years' experience in corporate development, deal advisory, investment banking, private equity, venture capital, or a similar analytical role.
  • Exceptional analytical skills, with strong proficiency in financial modeling and a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Comfortable working with large datasets, such as digital sales and streaming reports, to support deal analysis. Advanced Excel is essential; Python, SQL, or experience using AI/LLM tools to accelerate analysis is a plus.

job.title: Performance Marketing Manager
job.description:
Sony Music Entertainment är ett av världens ledande musikbolag med drygt 5 000 medarbetare globalt. På Sony Music Sverige arbetar ca 80 medarbetare med att dagligen skapa, utveckla, marknadsföra och distribuera våra artisters musik ur vårt breda urval av svensk och internationell repertoar. Vår vision är att vara Sveriges bästa musikbolag och arbetsplats inom branschen, kända för vår innovation, kreativitet och framgång, präglat av mångfald och passion för musik.

Sammanfattning av rollen
Brinner du för performance marketing och mäter du framgång i konverteringar snarare än räckvidd? Sony Music Sweden söker en datadriven, handlingskraftig och analytisk Performance Marketing Manager med gedigen erfarenhet av avancerad, konverteringsdriven digital annonsering. Du planerar, sätter självständigt upp och optimerar ett stort antal kampanjer – med ett tydligt mål; att driva konvertering och skapa långsiktiga resultat.

Du blir en del av vår Commercial-avdelning, där vi inte bara driver kampanjer för våra artister, utan framför allt marknadsför våra spellistor och artisternas största hits genom tiderna, både i Sverige och internationellt. Vi arbetar i grunden som en e-handlare: våra kampanjer optimeras mot konvertering och faktiska resultat snarare än traditionella räckviddsmål. Hos oss får du arbeta operativt med avancerade, datadrivna kampanjer och våra egenutvecklade marknadsföringsverktyg.

Rollen är baserad i Stockholm.

Vad kommer du att göra?
Som Performance Marketing Manager kommer du bland annat att:

  • Självständigt planera, sätta upp och optimera ett stort antal parallella kampanjer (ca 10–30 per vecka), med ansvar för budget, leverans och resultat.
  • Driva konverteringsfokuserade kampanjer för spellistor, artister, katalog och e-handel – från målgrupp och budskap till konvertering.
  • Granska och analysera kampanjdata över flera plattformar och löpande optimera mot konvertering, CPA och ROAS.
  • Säkerställa korrekt tracking och mätning – pixlar, Conversions API, UTM-struktur och förstapartsdata – i nära samarbete med våra analytiker och utvecklare.
  • Arbeta systematiskt med A/B-testning och konverteringsoptimering av annonser, målgrupper och landningssidor.
  • Bidra med ett varumärkesbyggande perspektiv och förståelse för vad som gör våra spellistor attraktiva och relevanta, med målet att skapa långsiktigt engagemang hos lyssnarna.
  • Samarbeta med teamet för att utveckla nya idéer, arbetssätt och lösningar som förbättrar våra resultat.

Vem är du?

  • Du har gedigen erfarenhet av performance marketing med fokus på konverteringsdriven annonsering, avancerad tracking och komplexa kampanjupplägg, gärna inom e-handel eller liknande digitala verksamheter.
  • Mycket goda praktiska kunskaper i Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads och TikTok Ads Manager. Du är van att självständigt sätta upp, hantera och optimera kampanjer.
  • Goda kunskaper om tracking och mätning, exempelvis spårningspixlar, Conversions API/server-side tracking, attribution och förstapartsdata.
  • Erfarenhet av konverteringsoptimering (CRO) och systematisk A/B-testning.
  • Förståelse för SEO, sökbeteenden och hur digital annonsering kan bidra till organisk tillväxt.
  • Förmåga att analysera och visualisera data samt presentera insikter som leder till konkreta förbättringar.
  • God förmåga att skriva engagerande och säljande texter för digitala kampanjer på svenska och/eller engelska.
  • Det är meriterande om du har erfarenhet av att driva försäljning i en webbshop samt grundläggande kunskaper i Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Premiere Pro, After Effects).

Personliga egenskaper

  • Du är kommersiellt driven och motiveras av mätbara resultat.
  • Du är analytisk, nyfiken och tycker om att testa, utvärdera och optimera för att ständigt förbättra resultaten.
  • Du är kreativ och har känsla för målgrupper, budskap och vad som skapar engagemang.
  • Du är strukturerad, organiserad och trivs med att hantera många parallella kampanjer.
  • Du är självgående, tar egna initiativ och trivs med att arbeta operativt och hands-on.
  • Du är kommunikativ, prestigelös och samarbetar gärna med andra.
  • Du är flexibel och har lätt för att anpassa dig till nya förutsättningar.

Vad erbjuder vi?

  • Som en del av Sony Music får du chans att vidga dina vyer och naturligt växa in i ett globalt nätverk.
  • Möjligheten att arbeta med avancerade, datadrivna kampanjupplägg i en miljö där vi ständigt utvecklar nya verktyg och arbetssätt.
  • Här får din kreativitet flöda fritt; vi uppmuntrar nya idéer som kan revolutionera hur vi skapar banbrytande kampanjer.
  • Ett team och en arbetsmiljö som genomsyras av kreativitet, engagemang och internationellt samarbete.
  • En konkurrenskraftig lön med förmåner och möjligheter till professionell utveckling.

Ansökan
Är detta rollen för dig? Skicka in din ansökan senast den 13 november 2026. Varmt välkommen med din ansökan!

Som en aktiv del i ett samhälle med kulturell och social mångfald är Sony Musics ambition att präglas av inkludering och bred representation, samt vara en arbetsplats med lika möjligheter för alla. Sony Music anställer, bibehåller, befordrar och i övrigt behandlar alla medarbetare och kandidater efter erfarenhet, kvalifikationer och kompetens, oavsett kön, religion, ursprung, ålder, sexuell läggning, könsidentitet eller funktionsvariationer.

job.title: Human Resources Intern
job.description:
AccuWeather is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented HR Intern to join our Human Resources team at our Corporate HR in State College, Pennsylvania for the spring semester. This internship provides an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience in HR practices, policies, and procedures. The HR Intern will support daily HR operations, recruitment, employee engagement activities, and administrative functions while learning about the overall employee lifecycle.

  • Assist with the recruitment process, including posting job ads, screening resumes, scheduling interviews, and coordinating with candidates.
  • Support onboarding and orientation for new hires.
  • Maintain and update HR records, databases, and employee files.
  • Assist with payroll and benefits administration as needed.
  • Help organize employee engagement initiatives, training sessions, and events.
  • Conduct research on HR trends, best practices, and compliance topics.
  • Provide general administrative support to the HR department.

  • Currently pursuing a degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology, or related field.

  • Excellent organizational and time management abilities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with professionalism.
  • Detail-oriented, proactive, and eager to learn.

  • Exposure to the full employee lifecycle (recruitment, onboarding, training, retention).

The AccuWeather Network and AccuWeather NOW® reach an audience of over 225 million on cable and streaming platforms including DirecTV, Charter Communications - Spectrum, Verizon, Samsung, Vizio, Philo, Frndly TV, Comcast’s Xfinity X1 and Xfinity Stream, Roku, Xumo, Rockbot, LG, and Amazon Freevee.   AccuWeather For Business serves more than half of the Fortune 500 companies and thousands of other businesses and government agencies globally.   Dr. Joel Myers, Founder and Executive Chairman, established AccuWeather in 1962 and is considered the “father of modern commercial meteorology.” Myers is a visionary entrepreneur and has been called “the most accurate man in weather” by The New York Times. He has been recognized in Entrepreneur Magazine’s Encyclopedia of Entrepreneurs as one of the greatest entrepreneurs in American history. Myers received the American Meteorological Society’s 2018 Award for Outstanding Contributions to the Advancement of Applied Meteorology and the National Weather Association’s 2017 Lifetime Achievement Award, in addition to numerous other accolades.   COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION   AccuWeather is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. job.title: Assistant White House Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Assistant White House Editor will play a central role in shaping the Washington Bureau report, supporting the White House editor and collaborating with other teams as news requires. This editor will manage reporters, help launch and edit news and enterprise stories focused on the President, and will help coordinate coverage across platforms. Operating in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment, this editor will help monitor ongoing developments on multiple fronts, and assist the White House editor in planning, making assignments, editing stories and thinking creatively about how to advance our report to serve our audiences.

The Assistant White House Editor also collaborates with other newsroom departments and stakeholders, monitoring daily and weekly priorities, helping to manage daily story planning and budgeting, getting reporters launched on stories and doing first or second-editing. This editor will manage the team when the White House editor is absent and shares responsibility for managing coverage of events on nights and weekends.

At a time when the news priorities can shift rapidly, this editor will sometimes be deployed to jump on other developments, work with other teams and support live coverage.

This editor should be able to move quickly across storylines without sacrificing accuracy and tone. Experience managing reporters or other editors is essential, as is a demonstrated ability to make thoughtful news judgements under pressure. Experience with White House coverage is a plus.

This position is based in Washington, D.C. and may include night and weekend coverage. It includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

You will report to the White House editor.

Responsibilities:

  • You will serve as a deputy first editor for the White House team, stepping in to support the White House editor. You will assign and cover first edits for breaking, live news and some enterprise stories, ensuring continuity of coverage and clear direction for reporters across beats.
  • You will handle edits of all sorts, including quick cuts, write-throughs, live stories, dailies and lead-alls as needed.
  • You will help set up weekend and off‑peak Washington coverage for these teams, including assigning, editing and coordinating with the News Director, editors managing live and breaking news stories as well as staff editors on key stories and providing additional support for stories that move or break at night, on weekends or holidays.
  • You will be nimble and flexible about being directed to other news developments and coverage teams as necessary and to work across platforms.
  • You will support live and alternative formats, helping decide when developments should go into live files versus traditional stories, and partnering with other news editors as needed.
  • You will be organized and work in close partnership with other editors on the bureau to build out the day's budget and update the week's budget, anticipating news needs and planning future coverage.
  • You will be skilled at anticipating potential problems, addressing unexpected issues and finding solutions.
  • You will help identify potential stories, including non-traditional story formats, visual stories, service and explanatory pieces.
  • You will coordinate with editors and the audience team on story publication and promotion plans and foster group headline brainstorming and promotion planning.
  • You will work in close partnership with the Weekend Editor on planning handoffs at the start and mid-points of the week so we have clarity and continuity in our storylines and with other editors on the team to help identify potential stories, assign and edit the daily report.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years' experience at a journalism or media company or other relevant organization
  • Editing skills that demonstrate mastery of journalistic style and standards, including ethical standards.
  • Proven news judgment.
  • Previous experience managing and editing reporters.
  • Previous experience juggling multiple storylines with rigor and judgment.
  • Experience with coverage of some combination of government, policy and politics.
  • Openness to and comfort with new story forms, live coverage and adopting new ways of working as the newsroom's needs evolve.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • People management experience
  • A willingness to be nimble and flexible in anticipating potential problems, addressing unexpected issues and finding solutions.
  • A strong understanding of Times style and standards
  • A willingness to collaborate and the ability to partner with colleagues across The New York Times newsroom.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive coverage across multiple topics.

Additional Compensation and Benefits:

For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.

For roles outside of the U.S., information on benefits will be provided during the interview process.

job.title: Senior Customer Service Agent, NYT Wirecutter (Temporary)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

Wirecutter, a New York Times company, is the premier product recommendation service dedicated to rigorously testing and reviewing products to help readers make the best decisions for their lives. Building on our mission of trust and utility, the Wirecutter Store (wirecutterstore.nytimes.com) is our dedicated e-commerce destination, offering our audience for purchase a highly-curated selection of the exceptional products we recommend.

 

As we approach our busiest time of the year (Q4/Holiday Season), we are looking for two experienced Senior Temporary Customer Service Agents to join our team. You will be the customer-facing voice of the Wirecutter Store. You will ensure that our customers receive the same level of care, clarity, and reliability that they expect from Wirecutter's editorial recommendations.

 

You will report directly to the Ecommerce Operations Director. You will work with our Customer Experience Manager to resolve inquiries, refine support processes, and improve our helpdesk operations during the peak holiday shopping rush.

 

Schedule and Hours:

  • Base Hours: Up to 40 hours per business week.

  • Peak Season: An additional 10 hours on weekends during peak periods.

  • Available Shifts (subject to change):

    • Shift A: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM

    • Shift B: 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM

 

Responsibilities:

  • You will provide customer support across our primary communication channels: email and chat.

  • You will manage inquiries coming through our email and AI chat systems, providing rapid, real-time responses to customers and take over complex issues that require a human touch.

  • You will resolve inquiries regarding order status, product information, shipping, and returns.

  • You will process returns using Loop Returns, ensuring accurate refunds and inventory tracking.

  • You will guide communication between the store and our external supply partners, investigating and escalating complex fulfillment, shipping, or product inquiries to ensure rapid resolution for the customer.

  • You will navigate and use our ecommerce tech platforms at an expert level, specifically Shopify, Gorgias (including live chat and AI automation features), and Loop Returns.

  • You will collaborate with the Customer Experience Manager to identify trending customer issues and suggest operational improvements.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • At least 5 years, as a senior or lead customer service representative.

  • Communication & Speed: at least 5 years of experience interpreting and responding to customer requests with impeccable grammar and empathy. Must respond quickly to live chat inquiries without sacrificing quality.

  • Technical Expertise: at least 2 years of experience with Shopify, Gorgias, and Loop Returns.

  • AI Chat & System Optimization: at least 1 year of experience working with AI chat tools, managing live chat queues, creating macros, configuring auto-responses, and performing advanced administrative tasks within Gorgias.

  • Work Environment: at least 3 years of experience in a high-volume retail environment, meeting strict response time expectations during peak season.

  • Location Flexibility: You will work in-office during the Monday–Friday business week, with the flexibility to work from home on weekends during peak volume weeks.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3 years of experience working with drop-ship retailers.

The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It's why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It's why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it's why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it's worth paying for.

 

About the position

To help us do this essential work, The New York Times is hiring a Senior Manager, Strategic Business Communications.

In this role, you'll be part of a team that leads internal communication on the business side of The Times, with a focus on XFun, our cross-functional product development organization. You'll partner closely with XFun leadership, their chiefs of staff, HR, Legal, Labor Relations and other stakeholders across the org — bringing our strategy, priorities and culture to life, and elevating the employee experience for our team. You're comfortable working in a highly matrixed organization, bringing together many voices and priorities in service of The Times's mission, and you take real pride in helping colleagues feel seen, connected and celebrated for their work.

We're looking for someone who can manage several projects at once — some you'll lead, some you'll support — with experience helping executives and leaders accomplish their communication goals, ideally within a tech company or similarly fast-moving environment. You're an impeccable writer and you know how to make communications break through the noise, including through audio, video and other formats. You come with big ideas, the drive to see them through, and a collaborative spirit that puts the team and the work first.

Responsibilities

  • Connect colleagues to strategy and culture through communications, events and experiences.

  • Support communications and planning for All Hands and other internal events for XFun, Wirecutter and The Athletic — including recurring programs like Maker Week (our annual hackathon), EngX (our annual engineering gathering), and Behind the Report (our monthly series designed to connect colleagues with our mission).

  • Develop All hands agendas, prepare presenters, and manage scheduling and event logistics, from invitations and calendars to space bookings and catering.

  • Own communications plans across a range of topics and issues, working closely with leaders to draft communications, facilitate cascades across the organization, and help leaders share timely, aligned updates with their teams in a highly matrixed organization.

  • Own internal communications for external product launches (e.g., Games, Cooking, News), partnering with Product, Marketing, and XFun Ops to ensure employees understand what's launching and why it matters.

  • Own the XFun-all Slack channel, ensuring information inclusive, and aligned with XFun priorities.

  • Experiment with new formats — short-form video, audio/podcast content, interactive posts — to keep communications and events dynamic and engaging.

  • Serve as the central point of contact for XFun managers, owning a yearly engagement plan (including the managers Slack channel and producing recurring manager meetings) and partnering with Labor and Legal on sensitive communications.

  • Elevate XFun's work through 3–4 stories a year with the Storytelling team and segments at company-wide meetings.

  • Own communications for core people programs (the performance cycle, required training, the employee survey and benefits updates), and partner with HR, Legal and leadership on personnel matters such as departures, org changes and executive hires.

  • Champion recognition across XFun, executing on existing plans, finding new ways to celebrate wins big and small, and spotlighting major moments like Publisher Awards and team milestones.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in communications in a Global organization.

  • Experience executing internal events, from All Hands to large-scale gatherings, including comfort managing both content and logistics.

  • Experience producing multimedia content — such as video, audio, or interactive formats.

  • Experience with project management tools and methodologies and managing concurrent workstreams.

  • Experience managing multiple stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in highly matrixed technology companies.

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
