job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KGUN
job.description:
KGUN, The E.W. Scripps station in Tucson, AZ is looking for a driven, versatile Multimedia Journalist to research, write, shoot, and edit compelling stories across multiple platforms. In this role, you won't just report the news — you'll be out in the community, uncovering the stories that matter most to our viewers, capturing them with your own lens, and delivering them with impact. If you're energized by tight deadlines, passionate about community journalism, and ready to bring authenticity to every story you tell, we want to hear from you.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Pitch and develop story ideas.
  • Gather and verify factual information regarding stories through interview, observation, and research.
  • Organize material, determine slant or emphasis, and write story according to prescribed editorial style and format standards.
  • Shoot video and still photos to illustrate stories.
  • Edit videos for all multimedia platforms.
  • Appear on-air and other online platforms
  • Give live reports from site of event or mobile broadcast unit.
  • Work cooperatively with photographer assigned to story, if one is assigned.

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 3+ years of experience in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Computer literacy required, including newsroom computer systems
  • Videography and non-linear editing experience preferred
  • Knowledge of broadcast quality camera equipment
  • Edit video on Final Cut Pro editing systems, or similar equipment
  • Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills
  • Proficient at posting content to various websites
  • Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced deadline-driven environment
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Tucson is a city where the desert comes alive — dramatic saguaro-studded landscapes, stunning sunsets, and a warm, welcoming culture that draws people in and keeps them here. Outdoor enthusiasts will love having Saguaro National Park split across both sides of the city, while Mount Lemmon offers hiking, skiing, and sweeping views that seem almost impossible given the desert below. The region's mild winters make year-round adventure the norm, not the exception. Beyond the outdoors, Tucson has a rich cultural identity rooted in its deep Native American, Spanish, and Mexican heritage. The vibrant Fourth Avenue district and downtown core are packed with independent restaurants, art galleries, live music venues, and local shops. Tucson's food scene earned it a spot as a UNESCO City of Gastronomy — the first in the United States — celebrated for its unique Sonoran cuisine and thriving farm-to-table movement. Home to the University of Arizona, Tucson pulses with youthful energy, sports fandom, and a growing tech and innovation sector. With a lower cost of living than many comparable cities and a tight-knit community feel, Tucson offers the perfect blend of big-city culture and laid-back desert living — an inspiring backdrop for any journalist ready to make their mark.

job.title: Meteorologist, WMAR
job.description:
WMAR, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC affiliate in Baltimore, Maryland, is seeking a Meteorologist to join our weather team. This is an exciting opportunity to deliver critical weather information to one of the Mid-Atlantic's most dynamic markets. You'll analyze meteorological data and prepare forecasts that help our community stay informed and safe, whether it's tracking severe weather or planning their week ahead.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Prepare and deliver daily weathercasts utilizing all available weather data and graphics computers.
  • Prepare and deliver urgent weather updates interrupting regular programming as necessary.
  • Prepare and deliver all weathercast materials over a variety of mediums, including, but not limited to: TV, Radio, Internet.
  • Assist management in evaluations of potential new weather data gathering and presentation computers.
  • Receive assignments or evaluate news leads and news tips to develop story ideas.
  • Report live from event sites or mobile broadcast unit.
  • May write and produce quality news and weather stories for multiple media platforms.
  • May report, write, capture visual content, edit and produce stories for multiple platforms on deadline, such as Internet and digital channels.
  • Work cooperatively with photographer assigned to story, if one is assigned.
  • Gather and verify factual information regarding stories through interview, observation, and research.
  • Perform other duties as needed and assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Bachelors degree in Meteorology preferred
  • Generally 3+ years experience in related field preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Computer literacy required, including weather and newsroom computer systems
  • Knowledge of broadcast quality camera equipment
  • Knowledge of editing systems
  • Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills
  • Proficient at posting content to various websites
  • Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY:

Baltimore, Maryland, is a vibrant city rich in history and culture, offering an exceptional quality of life on the Chesapeake Bay. Known as "Charm City," Baltimore boasts world-class attractions including the National Aquarium, historic Fort McHenry, and the iconic Inner Harbor. The city's diverse neighborhoods each have their own character, from the cobblestone streets of Fells Point to the artistic energy of Station North. Food lovers will appreciate Baltimore's famous crab cakes and thriving restaurant scene, while sports fans can cheer on the Orioles at Camden Yards or the Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. With easy access to Washington, D.C., Philadelphia, and the beaches of the Eastern Shore, Baltimore offers the perfect blend of urban excitement and coastal living. The city's affordable cost of living compared to other major East Coast metros, combined with its strong sense of community and rich cultural heritage, makes it an ideal place to call home.

job.title: Live Broadcast Engineer
job.description:
Do you thrive when the stakes are highest and the cameras are live? Operations Shared Services is looking for a driven, detail-obsessed Live Broadcast Engineer to manage and drive reliability within a fast-paced, multichannel on-air operations environment — maintaining optimal on-air availability and reliability for live events. This is a critical role at the heart of what we do: keeping our broadcasts on air, our audiences engaged, and our team performing at the highest level, 24/7.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Coordinate with other engineers and master control; provide guidance for the execution of master control functions pertaining to live-event execution.
  • Coordinate with master control supervisor to train operators in operational best practices, issue resolution, and recovery of live events.
  • Develop a deep knowledge of the operation's technical architecture and on-air systems.
  • Resolve issues quickly and effectively to prevent on-air discrepancies.
  • Manage the end-to-end execution of all live events including preparation, in-event execution, and off-air adjustments.
  • Actively participate in the operation's change control procedures by approving and maintaining awareness of all on-air maintenances and by managing critical components of maintenance operating procedures.
  • Assume transmission responsibilities as needed, including monitoring of uplinks, booking, QCing (monitoring for quality control) and occasional remotes.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Associates degree in a related discipline preferred or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally 2+ years of experience in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Ability to prioritize and adapt to changing scenarios preferred
  • Thorough understanding of television production, broadcast engineering operations, and/or news/sports/entertainment technical production requirements
  • Technological curiosity and an improvement-oriented approach
  • Unwavering composure in high-pressure situations
  • Demonstrated record of meeting or exceeding performance expectations preferred
  • Acute attention to detail
  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills
  • Willingness and availability to work flexible hours, including overnight shifts, weekends, and holidays is required to support 24x7 operation

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Clearwater, Florida is a sun-soaked Gulf Coast gem known for its strikingly clear turquoise waters and white-sand beaches — most notably Clearwater Beach, consistently ranked among the best beaches in the United States. The city offers an active, outdoor-forward lifestyle with year-round boating, kayaking, paddleboarding, and fishing right at your doorstep, along with easy access to dozens of parks and nature preserves throughout the region.

As part of the greater Tampa Bay area, Clearwater residents enjoy all the cultural amenities of a major metro while living at a more relaxed pace. The region is home to professional sports teams including the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Rays, and Lightning, as well as a thriving restaurant scene, live music venues, and world-class attractions like the Clearwater Marine Aquarium. Spring training baseball brings added energy each year, with the Philadelphia Phillies calling nearby Spectrum Field home.

Beyond the beach, Clearwater and the surrounding Tampa Bay area are experiencing exciting growth across the arts, tech, and culinary sectors. With a relatively affordable cost of living compared to other Florida metros, no state income tax, and a warm climate virtually year-round, Clearwater is a place where your career and your quality of life can both flourish.

job.title: Scheduling Coordinator
job.description:
TelevisaUnivision is seeking a detail-oriented Scheduling Coordinator to support Noticias 24/7, a News streaming channel on our streaming service, VIX. This position plays an essential role in ensuring the integrity of the streaming service to deliver viewer satisfaction.


The Scheduling Coordinator will accurately schedule content playlists, maintain program calendars, oversee playout, and manage all program data. Additionally, this role contributes to the execution of scheduling strategies and operations, including collaboration in the development of promotional materials, coordinating deliverables between multiple departments, and participating in the evaluation and implementation of workflows and systems.


ABOUT YOU:

The successful candidate will be organized, detail-oriented and deadline-driven, as well as very comfortable learning and using program scheduling and playout systems both on-site and remotely. As this is a 24-hour a day news service, this individual would be on-call to support breaking news or off-hour playlist changes as needed.

 

YOUR DAY-DAY: (aka Responsibilities)

  • Schedule all long-form programming for streaming news service based on strategic direction from supervisor.
  • Develop fluency in using the scheduling software and executing workflows for a flawless on-air experience.
  • Create, capture, and edit all content metadata in systems as needed.
  • Generate and maintain schedule grids (24 hour and weekly) for internal distribution and on Sharepoint.
  • Help prepare and distribute weekly programming notifications, such as premieres, TV listings and updates.
  • Maintain internal and external distribution lists for programming department.
  • Create, maintain, and set program formats on the grid level as well as live or server events. Review formats on a quarterly basis and make recommendations for revisions as needed to support business objectives.
  • Cutting clips from the programs to create segments for program reruns and preparing clips for social media distribution.
  • Monitor the Network Playout and adjust as needed for breaking news and content issues.
  • Be available on call after hours and weekends as necessary to revise playlist, trigger breaking news or support News team needs.
  • Produce work orders for promotional materials that communicate strategy, objectives and deadlines.
  • Schedule all short form elements including promos, graphics, news briefs and crawls.
  • Execute and track promotional and advertising campaigns for internal and external clients and generate reports (AS-RUNS).
  • Partner with News Production, Art Department, Ad Sales, Marketing, Business Affairs and Content Management.
  • Perform ad-hoc assignments as needed.

YOU HAVE: (aka Qualifications)

job.description:

You are highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple priorities at once. job.title: Account Director, Performance & Growth (San Francisco)
job.description:
NBCUniversal is one of the world's leading media and entertainment companies. We create world-class content, which we distribute across our portfolio of film, television, and streaming, and bring to life through our global theme park destinations, consumer products, and experiences. We own and operate leading entertainment and news brands, including NBC, NBC News, NBC Sports, Telemundo, NBC Local Stations, Bravo, and Peacock, our premium ad-supported streaming service. We produce and distribute premier filmed entertainment and programming through our powerhouse film and television studios, including Universal Pictures, DreamWorks Animation, and Focus Features, and the four global television studios under the Universal Studio Group banner, and operate industry-leading theme parks and experiences around the world through Universal Destinations & Experiences, including Universal Orlando Resort, home to Universal Epic Universe, and Universal Studios Hollywood. NBCUniversal is a subsidiary of Comcast Corporation. Visit www.nbcuniversal.com for more information.

Our impact is rooted in improving the communities where our employees, customers, and audiences live and work. We have a rich tradition of giving back and ensuring our employees have the opportunity to serve their communities. We champion an inclusive culture and strive to attract and develop a talented workforce to create and deliver a wide range of content reflecting our world.

The NBCU Account Director, Performance & Growth will focus exclusively on driving demand for performance brands across our suite of linear and digital products including all streaming products, with a focus on driving new and incremental revenue for the full NBCU portfolio (One Platform). This individual will play a critical role within our fast-paced advertising sales team, managing relationships across external clients and independent media agencies. The role requires building relationships with key internal stakeholders and collaborative partners across the NBCU organization. Expertise within the performance and digital landscape is a must. This person must have the ability to operate effectively at the cross-section of performance and digital media as these skills are critical to achieving success in this role. This role will report directly into to the Vice President, Performance & Growth. 

  • Drive linear and digital advertising demand of the NBCU Platform for specific performance brands and agencies in the direct-to-consumer category 
  • Be an expert across NBCU digital and streaming products and convey meaningful and sustainable opportunities to emerging brands 
  • Execute on day-to-day sales strategy; develop target lists, lead client outreach and be in market often with full NBCU opportunities 
  • Leverage prospecting software such as Linkedin Navigator, Media Radar and Zoom Info to identify, research and engage prospective clients and partners 
  • Understand customer needs and provide feedback and market input that will strengthen our NBCU opportunities and value proposition 
  • Field proactive requests: collect, manage, and route RFP requests to key stakeholders to ensure deadlines are met 
  • Track sales revenue and establish a regular cadence for reporting on progress 
  • Partner with internal teams (Digital and Linear sales leads, Client Strategy, Agency Partnerships, Marketing, Legal, Research, etc.) to develop proactive packages and drive creativity throughout the sales process 
  • Develop strong relationships throughout NBCU to ensure a unified and coordinated strategy is presented in the market 
  • Proven ability to prospect and identify new/incremental revenue opportunities beyond servicing an existing book of business
  • Growth-oriented/hunter mindset, with experience developing new opportunities, expanding client investment, and converting whitespace into revenue
  • Strong technical aptitude, including demonstrated experience leveraging AI, automation, data, or emerging technology to improve workflows, prospect more effectively, or solve business problems
  • Demonstrated expertise in performance advertising, with a strong understanding of performance-driven digital media concepts, measurement, attribution, optimization, and the key levers that drive business outcomes.
  • Confidently applies performance principles across the full client lifecycle, from developing data-driven media strategies and communicating measurement frameworks pre-sale to analyzing campaign performance, identifying optimization opportunities, and using results to drive account growth post-sale.
  • Advanced client-facing skills with the ability to articulate value propositions, influence investment, and present integrated marketing solutions
  • Analytical and strategic thinker with a track record of creative problem-solving and driving innovation
  • Self-starter who can operate independently and effectively navigate a large, cross-functional organization
  • 5+ years of relevant experience across advertising sales, business development, account management, programmatic/ad tech, or a related advanced media environment
  • Digital video experience required

Hybrid: This position currently has a hybrid schedule, which requires contributing from the office a minimum of four days per week. The Company reserves the right to change in-office requirements at any time. 

Location: This role is open to candidates based in Los Angeles or San Francisco.

This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website.

Salary range: $95,000 - $170,000 + sales compensation incentive eligible

  • Implement reactive, non-blocking architectures to support high concurrency and resilience. Create reusable streaming frameworks and libraries. These will help improve engineering efficiency and standardization across the platform.

Architect Scalable Distributed Systems

  • Design and optimize distributed streaming architectures. You will work with Kafka topics, partitioning strategies, consumer groups, schema management, and event lifecycle patterns.
  • Help make architecture decisions for the whole platform. This includes scalability, resiliency, high availability, disaster recovery, and deployments across multiple regions.
  • Drive best practices around event modeling, schema evolution, idempotency, replayability, and data consistency across streaming systems.

  • Build automated testing strategies for streaming workflows, including unit, integration, contract, chaos, and performance testing.
  • Participate in production support. Help with incident response and root-cause analysis. Work on initiatives to improve reliability continuously.

  • Deploy and manage containerized microservices within Kubernetes environments across GCP, AWS, or similar cloud platforms.
  • Define strategies for autoscaling, deployment, failover, and resource optimization. These strategies will focus on high-volume production systems.
  • Create and manage CI/CD pipelines. This includes Infrastructure-as-Code and workflows for automated deployment.
  • Collaborate with platform engineering teams to improve developer tooling, deployment automation, and runtime reliability.

  • Deep knowledge of asynchronous, non-blocking system design. Kafka & Event-Driven Architecture
  • Extensive experience with Apache Kafka (producers, consumers, streams, schema registry).

The Signal Intelligence (SigInt) team turns a high-volume, multi-source data ecosystem — operational systems, client-app event streams, ad-tech platforms, stitcher events, ad server logs, and telemetry — into the trusted data models, metrics, and dashboards that drive business, product, and ad-ops decisions.

We are hiring a Senior Data Engineer who is, in equal measure, a data modeler, a SQL craftsperson, and an analyst — not only a pipeline builder. You will own data end-to-end: modeling raw events into conformed, analytics-ready marts; writing the analytical SQL that answers hard business questions; defining the metrics leadership relies on; and building the pipelines that feed it all. Because we sit close to the business, translating ambiguous questions into durable models and clear insight matters as much as engineering the pipeline.

In practice, you will be the team's data sherpa — the person who knows the data terrain cold, guides analysts and business partners through it, and turns an ambiguous “can we find out X?” into a trusted, well-modeled answer. You own the map — the definitions, lineage, and the “why” behind the numbers — as much as the pipelines.

This is an analytics-engineering role on a semi-business team. It is not a pure platform / infrastructure position — if your passion is exclusively distributed-systems plumbing with little interest in modeling, analysis, or guiding the business, this will not be the right fit.

 

Responsibilities Include:

 

Modeling & architecture — the core of the role

• Design and own the dimensional and semantic models — conformed dimensions, facts, star/snowflake schemas, slowly changing dimensions (Type 2), and well-defined grain — that serve as the trusted source of truth.

• Architect data marts spanning operational, advertising, and telemetry domains for analytics, reporting, AI, and operational use.

• Establish shared definitions and a semantic / metrics layer so users, sessions, devices, content, campaigns, and impressions mean the same thing everywhere.

SQL & analysis

• Write and optimize sophisticated analytical SQL — window functions, cohort and funnel logic, sessionization, distributions — on large event-scale datasets.

• Analyze complex datasets to find patterns, quantify drivers, and produce actionable insight; define new metrics and KPIs (usage, revenue, etc.) and the logic behind them.

• Independently investigate variance across platforms and communicate findings clearly to peers and senior leadership.

Business partnership

• Be the go-to guide for the data — the person who knows where every number comes from, what it means, and its quirks and landmines.

• Own the institutional knowledge of the data — definitions, lineage, and the reasoning behind metrics — and make it legible so analysts, ad ops, product, and finance can self-serve with confidence.

• Partner with stakeholders and source-system owners to translate ambiguous business questions into durable data models and metrics, and support/conduct strategic investigations and analysis.

Pipelines, quality & delivery

• Build and harmonize the ingestion and transformation pipelines — event data from client apps, ad-tech platforms, stitchers, ad servers, and telemetry — that feed the models, handling deduplication, late-arriving data, sessionization, and schema evolution.

• Stitch identity and sessions across client, server, and ad-side events for accurate user, content, and revenue analytics.

• Establish data-quality standards (testing, monitoring, alerting, freshness and volume SLAs) and troubleshoot incidents end-to-end — from a dashboard anomaly back through marts, transformations, and raw logs.

• Support and improve BI dashboards; document datasets, lineage, and business logic so the data map stays trustworthy and current.

• Mentor engineers and analysts on SQL, modeling, event data, and engineering best practices.

 

Basic Qualifications

 

• Expert SQL, including analytical SQL craft (window functions, complex joins, cohort / funnel / sessionization logic) and performance tuning on large event-scale datasets.

• Deep data-modeling expertise — dimensional modeling, star/snowflake schemas, slowly changing dimensions, conformed dimensions, grain, and data-mart design; able to design a trusted source of truth from messy multi-source data.

• Strong data analysis and business translation — able to independently investigate data, define metrics and KPIs, and act as a trusted guide who turns ambiguous business questions into clear answers and enables others to self-serve.

• A guide’s temperament — curiosity to learn the data terrain deeply, patience to help non-technical partners, and communication that earns trust across the business.

• dbt (or an equivalent transformation / modeling framework).

• Cloud warehouse — BigQuery strongly preferred (our environment); Snowflake or Databricks acceptable with a fast ramp.

• Python for data processing and pipeline development.

• Orchestration experience (Airflow).

• High-volume event data — clickstream, telemetry, ad impressions, or similar — including deduplication, late-arriving data, sessionization, and schema evolution.

• Proven track record harmonizing data across multiple source systems with conflicting schemas, identifiers, or grain.

• BI tools (DOMO, Looker, Mode) — comfort both consuming and supporting their development.

• Experience debugging data-quality issues across the full stack — from BI tool to warehouse to raw event logs.

• BA/BS in Computer Science, Math, Physics, Engineering, Economics, Statistics, or a related quantitative field.

• Strong analytical, logical, and communication skills.

 

Preferred Qualifications

 

• Semantic-layer experience (LookML, dbt Semantic Layer, Cube).

• Streaming-media / ad-tech domain (ad servers, SSAI / stitchers, VAST/VMAP, impression and fill-rate metrics).

• Streaming ingestion (Kafka, Pub/Sub, Kinesis).

• Statistical analysis with R and predictive-analytics tooling; experimentation / A-B analysis.

• Master data management or entity resolution.

• MS in a quantitative discipline; experience mentoring or leading engineers/analysts.

 

How you will succeed in this role:

 

• You think in models and metrics, not just pipelines.

• You are the person others come to when they are lost in the data — and you like being that guide.

• You are as comfortable in a SQL console or a dashboard as in a DAG, and you move fluidly between business context and technical root cause.

• You treat data as a product — with users, definitions, SLAs, and documentation.

• You turn ambiguous business questions into clean models and clear answers.

  • Experience: 2+ years in an Accounts Receivable (AR), Master Data, or Corporate Customer Service role within a complex, multi-location organization.

  • Technical Proficiency: Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Excel skills (proficient with lookups, data validation, and pivot tables). Familiarity with major ERP platforms such as SAP or Oracle is a strong advantage.

  • Industry Acumen: Background in media, entertainment, or advertising/media-buying agencies is highly desirable.

The Associate Producer will play a key role in the day-to-day execution of the show by helping develop engaging content, coordinating guests, managing production logistics, and supporting broadcast, digital, and social media initiatives. The ideal candidate is a strong communicator, thrives under tight deadlines, embraces collaboration, and has a passion for storytelling, audience engagement, and creative content development. If this is you, apply today!


Responsibilities
•    Assist producers with the planning, coordination, and execution of daily LIVE broadcasts.
•    Research and develop segment ideas, trending topics, community stories, local events, and guest opportunities.
•    Coordinate and book guests for in-studio, remote, and pre-recorded segments.
•    Serve as a primary point of contact for guests, clients, and community partners before, during, and after their appearances.
•    Write and format segment scripts, teases, graphics information, and supporting show materials.
•    Assist with daily show rundowns and ensure all production elements are accurate, organized, and ready for air.
•    Support pre-show preparation, live production needs, and post-show follow-up.
•    Manage studio logistics, including set preparation, prop placement, display setup, and guest microphone coordination.
•    Collaborate closely with producers, hosts, editors, photographers, sales teams, and other members of the production staff.
•    Lead and manage Great Day SA's social media presence across multiple platforms.
•    Create, schedule, and publish engaging daily content that promotes upcoming segments, highlights memorable moments, and strengthens audience engagement.
•    Develop original digital content and innovative segment ideas that enhance and extend the Great Day SA brand.
•    Write compelling and accurate social media copy, website content, and promotional materials.
•    Monitor social media trends, audience analytics, and engagement metrics to identify growth opportunities and optimize performance.
•    Utilize Cuez to manage show rundowns, coordinate workflows, and facilitate communication across the production team.
•    Produce and manage original content for KENS 5 streaming platforms, including planning, writing, and executing recorded streaming shows.

Requirements
•    Bachelor's degree in Broadcast Journalism, Communications, Television Production, Film, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
•    Strong writing, communication, and organizational skills.
•    Ability to create and adapt content for broadcast, digital, web, and social media platforms.
•    Demonstrated ability to generate fresh, creative content ideas and proactively pitch segment and digital opportunities.
•    Strong understanding of social media platforms, content creation strategies, and audience engagement best practices.
•    Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.
•    Creative storyteller with strong editorial judgment and news awareness.
•    Self-starter who can work independently while contributing effectively in a collaborative team environment.
•    Positive, solution-oriented mindset and strong interpersonal skills.
•    Ability to adapt quickly and problem-solve in a fast-paced live television environment.
•    Working knowledge of Adobe Premiere Pro and Adobe Photoshop.
•    Experience with Cuez or similar newsroom and production workflow systems is preferred.
•    Prior television, digital media, or content production experience is a plus.


Work Environment
•    Primarily based in a television studio and office setting.
•    Requires occasional lifting of props and production materials, standing for extended periods, and assisting with studio setup and breakdown.
•    Must be comfortable working early morning hours and adapting to changing production needs.
•    Minimal travel required, generally less than 10%.

job.title: Client Success Manager
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team

Our team brings together the capabilities to position, commercialize, and grow Dow Jones’s B2B and enterprise portfolio. We translate customer needs, audience insight, and market intelligence into product strategy, clear value propositions, differentiated positioning, and relevant product and content experiences.


We enable commercial performance through sales operations, go-to-market enablement, and cross-functional coordination. We also help drive client outcomes across onboarding, adoption, engagement, and retention. Working in close partnership with Product, Editorial, Sales, and Client Success, we ensure Dow Jones’s enterprise solutions are compelling in the market, equipped for commercial success, and deliver sustained value to clients.


About the Role

We are seeking a Client Success Manager to own the post-sale client journey for assigned new business accounts-  from signed deal through launch, activation, early adoption, and handoff into ongoing account management. This role serves as the primary relationship owner and cross-functional coordinator during the early post-sale phase, working closely with Sales, Regional Sales Coordinators, Operations, Engagement, Customer Care, and Account Management.


The goal is a seamless transition from signed account to active, engaged client-  reducing friction, accelerating time to value, surfacing risk early, and bringing in the right resources at the right time.


The Client Success Manager is the primary post-sale relationship owner and "quarterback" across the early client lifecycle, accountable for client readiness, launch coordination, onboarding progress, standard-account adoption execution, early engagement, and risk management. The role doesn't personally own every specialist workstream, but ensures each one happens successfully.


This is not a quota-carrying role. Success is measured by how effectively clients launch, activate, adopt key products and workflows, engage early, and transition cleanly into ongoing account management.


You Will:

Own the post-sale relationship and launch orchestration

  • Serve as the primary point of contact from signed deal through onboarding and early adoption.
  • Lead the handoff from Sales, ensuring client goals, use cases, stakeholders, and launch priorities are clearly understood and documented.
  • Build 60–90 day onboarding milestones and success plans so clients know what success looks like and can achieve early wins.
  • Maintain proactive, coordinated communication with clients and internal stakeholders to keep launches on track.

Coordinate account setup with Regional Sales Coordinators and Operations

  • Partner with RSCs on order processing, account setup/changes, billing, CRM updates, and related handoffs.
  • Partner with Operations and Fulfillment on provisioning, entitlements, technical readiness, SLA readiness, and launch execution.
  • Own coordination and follow-through, while RSCs and Operations retain responsibility for their own administrative execution.

Drive onboarding and adoption for standard accounts

  • Execute onboarding using established playbooks, milestones, and training guidance.
  • Ensure clients understand activation steps and build early usage habits.
  • Support in designing and implementing playbooks and frameworks
  • Apply learnings and best practices across the client base.

Partner with Engagement and Lifecycle teams to deepen usage

  • Work with Engagement Strategy & Performance and Customer Lifecycle Marketing to ensure clients get the right communications, campaigns, and enablement programs.
  • Use engagement reporting and health signals to prioritize interventions.
  • Connect clients to the right in-life programs as they move from onboarding into sustained engagement.

Monitor account health and manage risk

  • Track usage, activation milestones, and health signals to catch stalled onboarding, weak adoption, or early churn risk.
  • Escalate early and coordinate support across Engagement, Customer Care, Operations, and Account Management.
  • Ensure critical issues stay owned and teams stay aligned on actions and timing.

Act as the voice of the client internally

  • Share feedback, adoption insights, and emerging needs with Product, Marketing, Sales, Customer Care, and Client Success leadership.
  • Partner with the Enterprise Customer Care & Voice of Customer Lead on escalations and service themes.

Support a clean handoff into ongoing account management

  • Ensure a clear transition from early post-sale ownership into the ongoing account management motion once onboarding and early adoption are complete.
  • Share account context, progress, risks, and adoption status with Account Managers so momentum carries through on high-value accounts.

Success Measures

Measured on adoption, engagement, readiness, and handoff outcomes rather than direct revenue. KPIs may include:

  • Account launch readiness and setup completion rate
  • Time to onboarding completion and time to first value
  • Activation and seat activation rate
  • Adoption of priority products, workflows, and features
  • Usage frequency, engagement depth, and health score movement
  • Participation in training, webinars, and lifecycle programs
  • Early identification and escalation of churn risk or stalled onboarding
  • Quality of handoff into ongoing account management

Cross-Functional Partnerships

  • Sales Account Executives — post-sale handoff and continuity from signed deal into launch
  • Regional Sales Coordinators — order processing, account setup/changes, billing coordination
  • Operations and Fulfillment — provisioning, entitlements, technical readiness, launch execution
  • Engagement Strategy & Performance / Customer Lifecycle Marketing — health monitoring, engagement plays, in-life programs
  • Enterprise Customer Care & Voice of Customer — escalations, white-glove service, feedback loops
  • Account Managers — transition planning and ongoing relationship continuity

You Have:

  • 7 years of experience in client success, onboarding, implementation, account coordination, or related post-sale roles in B2B, SaaS, media, or subscription environments
  • Strong cross-functional project management skills, able to coordinate multiple stakeholders through launch, onboarding, and adoption milestones
  • Excellent client communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills
  • Comfort using data and health indicators to monitor trends and flag risk early
  • A proactive, organized, solutions-oriented approach to client coordination
  • A client-first mindset focused on driving value through usage, adoption, and engagement — not transactional account support

  • Paid Time Off

  • Comprehensive Insurance Plans
  • Lifestyle Programs & Wellness Resources
  • Education Benefits
  • Family Care Benefits & Caregiving Support
  • Commuter Transit Program

  • Cybersecurity Protection

job.title: Manager, News Video
job.description:
Application Instructions

Please list all professional experience and explain any gaps in employment history. All of your application materials, which may include PDF files of work samples and/or links to audio, video, photography or graphics, must be uploaded to the field labeled Resume/Cover Letter/Work Samples to be considered for the position.


Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is seeking a strategic, creative and collaborative leader to serve as Manager, News Video, helping drive how our journalism reaches audiences across social and video platforms.


This role sits at the center of The Post's off-platform strategy, overseeing a team of social video editors responsible for producing engaging, platform-native journalism for YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and other emerging platforms. The Manager, News Video will lead editorial strategy, programming and execution, ensuring our video journalism reaches audiences wherever they consume news while upholding The Post's standards for accuracy, creativity and innovation.


We are looking for a leader who sees video as a core journalistic product—not simply a promotional tool—and who understands the rapidly evolving dynamics of social platforms and audience behavior. The ideal candidate combines editorial judgment, audience expertise and operational excellence with the ability to coach journalists, develop new formats and execute a clear vision for audience growth.

Working closely with the Head of Off-Platform Strategy and leaders across the newsroom, this manager will play a central role in shaping the future of The Post's digital video presence.


This position is based in our Washington, D.C., newsroom.


What Motivates You

  • You are passionate about bringing journalism to audiences wherever they are.
  • You thrive on building teams and helping journalists develop new storytelling skills.
  • You are fascinated by evolving video platforms, audience behavior and emerging formats.
  • You enjoy balancing editorial excellence with audience growth and innovation.
  • You are energized by experimentation, collaboration and continuous learning.

How You'll Support the Mission

  • Lead and develop a team of social video editors, fostering a collaborative culture centered on creativity, journalistic excellence and continuous improvement.
  • Manage daily video programming, staffing and production schedules to ensure the team is positioned to cover major news events and execute long-term priorities.
  • Develop quarterly and annual editorial strategies for news video in partnership with newsroom leadership, establishing clear goals and success metrics.
  • Identify opportunities for original news video coverage and oversee production from concept through publication, including editing and programming responsibilities when needed.
  • Own the editorial strategy and audience growth for The Post's YouTube channels, including news, topical and talent-driven programming.
  • Partner closely with Shows, Originals and other newsroom teams to develop and distribute original video journalism across platforms.
  • Coach editors and producers on platform-specific best practices, storytelling techniques and emerging video formats.
  • Monitor audience engagement and performance across platforms, using data and experimentation to continuously refine strategy and maximize reach.
  • Oversee operational aspects of news video production, including live video workflows, licensing resources and vendor relationships.
  • Collaborate across coverage desks and with Product and Design to identify new opportunities for video innovation and audience engagement.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • Significant experience leading digital video production or social video teams at a major news organization or media company.
  • Demonstrated success developing video strategies that grow audiences while maintaining high editorial standards.
  • Deep understanding of YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and other video platforms, including programming, audience development and platform best practices.
  • Strong editorial judgment and experience overseeing breaking news as well as longer-form and original video projects.
  • Experience managing and developing journalists or video creators in a collaborative newsroom environment.
  • Ability to interpret audience metrics and translate insights into editorial strategy and production decisions.
  • Excellent communication, organizational and project management skills.
  • A passion for experimentation, innovation and helping shape the future of digital journalism.

We will consider strong candidates who do not meet all of the qualifications above. Candidates should upload a résumé to our jobs portal and may include a cover letter to tell us about other skills and experience that you think would be valuable for this role. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled, but those received by Nov. 13 will be prioritized. The cover letter should be addressed to Department Head, Off-Platform Strategy Keely Diven and Managing Editor Bryan Flaherty.

The salary range for this role is $110,000 - $160,000. The actual starting salary within this range will depend on individual skills, experience and qualifications as they relate to specific job requirements. This position may be eligible for a bonus or incentive program, and a member of The Post’s recruiting team will discuss bonus payment terms and conditions during the interview process.

 

Collaboration makes us stronger. That’s why our offices are designed with open layouts, modern technology, and easy access to transportation. With certain exceptions for newsgathering and business travel, we work on-site five days a week.

Compensation and Benefits

Wherever you are in your life or career, The Washington Post offers comprehensive and inclusive benefits for every step of your journey:

  • Competitive medical, dental and vision coverage

  • Company-paid pension and 401(k) match

  • Three weeks of vacation and up to three weeks of paid sick leave

  • Nine paid holidays and two personal days

  • 20 weeks paid parental leave for any new parent

  • Robust mental health resources

  • Backup care and caregiver concierge services

  • Gender affirming services

  • Pet insurance

  • Free Post digital subscription

  • Leadership and career development programs

Benefits may vary based on the job, full-time or part-time schedule, location, and collectively bargained status.

  Your story awaits. Apply today!

Learn more about The Post at careers.washingtonpost.com.

job.title: Audience Development Executive
job.description:
The Audience Development Executive grows and deepens the audience for Sony Music's C-POP and J-POP repertoire across Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. You will own how fans find our artists, how they move from a first stream to a committed fan, and how we understand and act on what those audiences tell us. 

C-POP and J-POP are two of the fastest-moving parts of our regional business, with releases and campaigns increasingly running across several markets at once and audience behaviour that differs sharply between the two. This role is the connective tissue: setting audience strategy per artist and per release, coordinating rollout across markets, and turning streaming, social and first-party data into decisions the marketing teams can act on. Success looks like measurable audience growth market by market, a healthier conversion from casual listener to superfan, and a release calendar for both repertoires that runs as one regional plan rather than several disconnected ones. 

The role is based in Taiwan, and covers Hong Kong, Taiwan and Southeast Asia (SEA). You will sit within Hong Kong, Taiwan and Southeast Asia (SEA) International Marketing community, reporting to the Director, International Marketing in Hong Kong and working closely with the Head of Creative, Southeast Asia, ensuring regional creative alignment while executing tailored campaigns locally. 

 

What you'll do:

Own audience strategy for C-POP and J-POP repertoire 

  • Develop and deliver audience development plans for priority C-POP and J-POP artists, releases and catalogue across Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, with clear objectives for audience growth, retention and conversion. 
  • Segment and size audiences by market, identifying where an artist is over- or under-indexed and where the realistic growth is, then shape campaign priorities and budget recommendations around that. 
  • Build the discovery-to-superfan funnel for each project: map how listeners enter, what moves them deeper, and where they drop out, and design interventions at each stage. 
  • Own the audience narrative for both repertoires in regional planning sessions, bringing a clear point of view backed by data to marketing, creative, commercial and repertoire centre stakeholders. 
  • Recognise where C-POP and J-POP audiences behave differently, in discovery route, fandom structure, spending patterns and platform preference, and build strategies that reflect those differences rather than applying one regional template to both. 

Grow audiences on DSPs and across the streaming ecosystem 

  • Work with digital service partners including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, LINE MUSIC, JOOX, KKBOX and regional platforms on pitching, editorial support, on-platform programming and audience-growth opportunities across both repertoires. 
  • Drive playlist strategy across owned, editorial and algorithmic surfaces, including Filtr and other in-house playlist brands, and track how placement translates into sustained audience rather than a single-week spike. 
  • Partner with the digital marketing and media buying teams to align paid audience targeting with organic audience strategy, so spend is directed where it compounds. 
  • Monitor the creator and short-form ecosystem, identifying tracks and moments gaining traction and working with creative and digital teams to amplify them quickly. 
  • Track and act on the discovery routes specific to J-POP in this region, including anime, film and game sync, tour and event moments, and catalogue resurgence, and convert those spikes into retained audience. 

Build first-party data and superfan capability 

  • Grow first-party data capture across C-POP and J-POP campaigns, working with local teams to embed sign-up and data collection into releases, tours, fan events and D2C moments. 
  • Turn first-party data into usable audience segments for CRM, direct-to-consumer and superfan activity, and support markets in activating those segments responsibly. 
  • Identify and develop superfan opportunities that deepen the relationship with the most engaged part of each artist's audience, and support the commercial cases that sit behind them. 
  • Partner with Sony Music Japan and Greater China repertoire centre teams on first-party data and superfan initiatives, feeding regional audience insight back to them and translating their priorities into market-level plans. 
  • Work within local data protection and privacy requirements across each market, in partnership with legal and the relevant local teams. 

Coordinate across markets and repertoire centres 

  • Act as the regional coordination point for C-POP and J-POP releases and activities, aligning timelines, asset delivery and campaign moments across Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. 
  • Consolidate requirements from local marketing teams into workable regional plans that scale while still allowing for hyper-local adaptation. 
  • Maintain visibility of the release calendar and audience plans across both repertoires so markets and the repertoire centres know what is coming and what is expected of them. 
  • Flag risks, clashes and gaps early, and keep regional stakeholders informed of progress and performance. 

Measure, report and improve 

  • Track and report on audience KPIs including listener growth, retention, market share, playlist performance, and first-party data capture, and communicate results clearly to senior stakeholders. 
  • Lead post-campaign reviews, identifying what drove audience growth and feeding those learnings into the next cycle. 
  • Work with the insights, data and analytics team to develop reporting that markets will actually use, and build data literacy across the regional teams. 
  • Stay ahead of platform, format and consumption changes across Greater China and Southeast Asia, and advise the business on what they mean for how we grow audiences.

 

Who you are:

  • 2+ years' experience in audience development, digital marketing, streaming or artist marketing at a label, DSP, artist management company or comparable media business. 
  • Demonstrable track record of growing an artist, catalogue or content audience, with the numbers to show it. 
  • Strong working knowledge of the streaming landscape across Greater China and Southeast Asia, including DSP editorial and algorithmic mechanics, playlist strategy, and platform-specific audience behaviour. 
  • Genuine fluency in C-POP and J-POP: the artists, the fandoms, the platforms they live on, and how audience behaviour differs between Taiwan, Hong Kong and the Southeast Asian markets. 
  • Comfortable with data. Able to work with streaming, social and first-party data, draw a defensible conclusion from it, and explain that conclusion to people who are not analysts. 
  • Experience with first-party data capture, CRM or direct-to-consumer fan initiatives is a strong advantage. 
  • Fluent in Mandarin (Traditional Chinese) and English. Japanese is a strong advantage given the J-POP scope.
  • Strong coordination skills across multiple markets, time zones and stakeholders, with the ability to keep several campaigns moving at once. 
  • Ability to articulate an idea or point of view succinctly, with clarity and confidence, adapting the message to different audiences, seniority levels and cultures. 
  • Responds and adapts quickly to change, maintaining a flexible attitude and using new conditions to evolve their thinking. 
  • A thorough understanding of lifestyle and cultural trends across Greater China and Southeast Asia.

 

What we give you:

  • You join a vibrant global community with the opportunity to channel your passion every day
  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community

job.title: Coordinator, Digital Production
job.description:
At Warner Music Group, we’re a global collective of music makers and music lovers, tech innovators and inspired entrepreneurs, game-changing creatives and passionate team members. Here, we turn dreams into stardom and audiences into fans. We are guided by three core values that underpin everything we do across all our diverse businesses: 

  • Curiosity: We do our best work when we’re immersing ourselves in culture and breaking through barriers. Curiosity is the driving force behind creativity and ingenuity. It fuels innovation, and innovation is the key to our future. 

  • Collaboration: Making music and bringing it to the world is all about the power of originality amplified by teamwork. A great idea, like a great song, travels globally. We ignite passions and build connections across our diverse community of artists, songwriters, partners, and fans.

  • Commitment: We pursue excellence for our team and our talent. Everything in music starts with a leap into the unknown, and we’re committed to keeping the faith, acting with integrity, and delivering on our promises.

WMG is home to a wide range of artists, musicians, and songwriters that fuel our success. That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone.  We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences.

Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.
 

Job Title: Coordinator, Digital Production


A little bit about our team:

Our team sets up, schedules, and gathers all the pieces for new digital releases to be delivered to digital service providers like Spotify, Apple, etc., and also new physical releases (Vinyl, CDs, Cassettes), to be manufactured. We ensure that all digital and physical products appear in the marketplace as intended by the label and artist.


Your role:

You will play an integral role in supporting Warner Records, Warner Records Nashville and 10K Projects. This position will handle day-to-day support on products with various digital service providers as well as operations processes. The ideal candidate will be able to work and communicate effectively with multiple stakeholders. Flexibility and the ability to prioritize various tasks in an ever-changing environment will also be key.


Here you’ll get to:

  • Run the production schedules, ensuring their accuracy and sending out to large distribution lists; you’ll also build and send the Daily Schedule Changes memo, with late-breaking changes not yet published in the schedule.
  • Assist with setting up and scheduling products to digital service providers, often making numerous changes to setup both before and after product delivery.
  • Be responsible for coordinating new album and single releases on a weekly basis for releases assigned to you. This includes verifying that audio/video, art, metadata, and scheduling, and pricing are in place and compliant with current industry standards.
  • See your projects through by completing digital bill of materials (dBOM) approval for delivery to digital service providers. 
  • Conduct weekly checks to ensure products assigned to you have successfully completed delivery to accounts and reconcile the release details back to the release intention.
  • Handle takedowns and price changes as requested by the labels.
  • Coordinate the delivery and tracking of all digital releases for your assigned projects.
  • Enter in-network video claims for video products live at YouTube.
  • Utilize automated robot to create still image audio products for delivery to YouTube.
  • Provide coverage for absent team members.

About you:

  • Creative self-starter with exceptional follow-up skills.
  • General understanding of current digital music distribution partners and industry best practices. 
  • Must be able to accept changes readily, both in job responsibilities, as well as in the work environment, and can be flexible in adapting to re-prioritized tasks.
  • Minimum one year experience in the music industry.  
  • Data analysis/research skills.
  • You have knowledge of digital retailer metadata requirements and broad knowledge of the audio production process.
  • You have great people skills, able to work with varied personalities at many levels of the company.
  • You’re extremely flexible, are extremely detail-oriented, like constant change, and are comfortable juggling multiple responsibilities and last-minute requests. 
  • You’re a problem solver with a keen deadline awareness.
  • You have excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • You have excellent computer skills, including working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets
  • You possess a genuine interest in music and the music business.
  • You have excellent time management and organizational skills.
  • You’re a team player, who can tolerate ambiguity.

We’d love it if you also had:

• Mastery of Excel, including formulas for date calculation and calendaring.

• Experience with music industry production schedules.

• Experience using and designing workflows in AirTable.



As the home to 10K Projects, Asylum, Atlantic Music Group, East West, FFRR, Fueled by Ramen, Nonesuch, Parlophone, Rhino, Roadrunner, Sire, Warner Records, Warner Classics, and several other of the world’s premier recording labels, Warner Music Group champions emerging artists and global superstars alike. And our renowned publishing company, Warner Chappell Music, represents genre-spanning songwriters and producers through a catalog of more than one million copyrights worldwide. Warner Music Group is also home to ADA, which supports the independent community, as well as artist services division WMX. In addition, WMG counts film and television storytelling powerhouse Warner Music Entertainment among its many brands.

Together, we are Warner Music Group: Independent Minds. Major Sound.

Love this job and want to apply?

Click the “Apply” link at the top of the page, or apply directly with your LinkedIn. Applying with LinkedIn will import all of the information you put in your profile, but will still allow you to upload a resume and cover letter.

 

Don’t be discouraged if you don’t hear from us right away. We’re taking our time to review all resumes, and to find the best people for WMG.

 

Thanks for your interest in working for WMG. We love it here, and think you will, too.
 

This position requires a minimum of 4 days per week in the office. job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
The big picture: Axios is a media company dedicated to delivering trustworthy news and information with efficiency, clarity, and Smart Brevity. We’re hiring a Virginia-based Executive Assistant to support our Chief Operating Officer, coordinate group meetings across her teams, and partner with her Chief of Staff on cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives.

Why it matters: As the COO’s internal and external commitments grow, thoughtful scheduling and reliable follow-through help her and her teams spend time where it matters most. Reporting to the Chief of Staff, this role divides its time roughly equally between direct support for the COO and cross-functional coordination and project support. The Chief of Staff sets priorities for strategic initiatives, projects and broader team support.

Go deeper: In this role, you will make an impact at Axios with the following responsibilities:

  • Manage the COO’s calendar strategically, aligning internal and external commitments with her priorities and proactively resolving routine scheduling conflicts.
  • Learn the COO’s priorities and working preferences, use sound judgment to resolve routine scheduling and logistical issues independently, and bring the Chief of Staff clear options when trade-offs or decisions need escalation.
  • Schedule complex group meetings across the COO’s teams, working with executive assistants and participants to bring the right people together.
  • Own meeting logistics, invitations and materials, anticipating preparation needs and coordinating changes so participants know where to be and what to prepare.
  • Coordinate the COO’s business travel end to end, maintain accurate itineraries and calendar details, and proactively manage changes with relevant partners.
  • Organize agreed follow-ups from group meetings, track owners and deadlines, and flag dependencies or outstanding items to the Chief of Staff.
  • Maintain project plans, timelines and status updates; coordinate inputs across teams, follow up with owners, and surface risks, dependencies or decisions that need the Chief of Staff’s attention.
  • Gather and synthesize information, conduct research, and draft concise briefs, presentations and updates to support planning, leadership discussions and decisions.
  • Take ownership of defined workstreams and special projects as assigned by the Chief of Staff, and identify practical ways to improve coordination, documentation and team processes.
  • Draft, edit and coordinate internal and external communications for the COO and Chief of Staff, including team updates, stakeholder correspondence and meeting follow-ups; gather input, coordinate review and approval, and ensure messages are clear, accurate and timely.
  • Handle sensitive information with discretion and keep the COO and Chief of Staff informed of changes that affect their plans.

Worthy of your time: Ideal candidates will embody an entrepreneurial spirit, a passion for Axios’ mission, and have the following skills:

  • Experience managing executive calendars and priorities, with strong scheduling and logistics skills in a fast-moving organization.
  • Excellent prioritization, time management and attention to detail, with a proactive approach to anticipating needs and adapting as priorities change.
  • Clear, concise communication and confidence coordinating across multiple executives and teams, keeping colleagues and external contacts informed as plans change.
  • Strong writing and editing skills, with experience preparing internal and external communications, adapting tone and content for different audiences, and capturing an executive’s voice with accuracy, professionalism and discretion.
  • Sound operational judgment: anticipate and solve routine problems, assess urgency, make decisions with limited guidance, and recognize when to escalate, while handling confidential information with discretion.
  • Strong coordination skills: organize meeting preparation and follow-ups, track deadlines, and collaborate with executive assistants and accountable owners.
  • Experience coordinating projects across teams, with the ability to turn broad goals into organized plans, track progress, and follow through without constant direction.
  • Ability to synthesize information and prepare clear written updates and presentations, with curiosity about business priorities and how different teams work together.
  • Comfort using Google calendar, document and collaboration tools to keep schedules and follow-ups organized.

What success looks like

  • A well-managed COO calendar that reflects her priorities and minimizes avoidable conflicts.
  • Group meetings scheduled efficiently, with clear logistics and prepared participants.
  • Accurate travel information and timely communication when plans change.
  • Visible meeting follow-ups, with owners reminded and unresolved items surfaced promptly.
  • Cross-functional projects advance against agreed milestones, with clear ownership, timely updates and risks surfaced early.
  • The Chief of Staff has reliable project support and concise, useful materials to move strategic initiatives forward.
  • Some experience and comfort using AI tools, with curiosity to learn more and apply them thoughtfully to day-to-day work.
  • A trusted partnership with the COO and Chief of Staff, with clear boundaries for broader team support.

job.title: Freelance Pitch Form
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

While the vast majority of ProPublica’s work comes from our staff, we occasionally consider supporting ambitious accountability stories or projects from independent journalists whose ideas align with the mission of our organization.

Here’s what journalists submitting proposals should know.

We’re open to investigations that are revelatory or substantially advance what is known on a subject of importance. The investigation should have the potential to trigger needed reforms by identifying a problem, who’s responsible and what should change. It should also clearly show harm. The investigation can be rooted in a place or focus on a person, but it should illuminate an issue of broader relevance.

The best proposals have a clear hypothesis, typically based on significant reporting: They don’t wonder whether something bad is happening, they know it. Please include not only a general description of the topic, but also a sense of the anecdotes/data/documents you have gathered, what you expect to find and possible accountability stories you want to tell.

In addition, applicants should detail, as much as is possible at the outset, what an investigation will require: data work, travel, obtaining public records. It’s also important for us to know what data, documents and/or source relationships the reporter already has. Finally, we’d like to hear a bit about why you are particularly suited to do this investigation.

We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, and aim to notify candidates regarding your proposals within two weeks of submission. Questions? Send an email to talent@propublica.org. No phone calls, please.

For those proposals we accept, we pay competitive freelance rates, including reporting expenses. Freelancers are independent contractors and will not be treated by ProPublica as employees for any purpose.

Independent contractors are responsible for paying any required taxes on any compensation received and for understanding the applicable tax laws. We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, and aim to notify candidates regarding your proposals within two weeks of submission. 

We know there are great candidates who may not fit into what we’ve described above or who have important skills we haven’t thought of. If that’s you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself.

All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age or any other status protected under applicable law. We are dedicated to building an inclusive newsroom and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.

job.title: Product Engineer, Membership and Front-End
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

We will stop accepting applications for this role on Monday, November 30th @ 11:59PM ET.

ProPublica is hiring a software engineer to work primarily on the systems and services that power our audience data platforms. This important role serves to advance ProPublica’s mission — publishing journalism with real-world impact — by enabling systems that bring us greater understanding of our audiences and donors.

We’re looking for an experienced engineer who believes in our mission and thrives in multifaceted roles, contributing both to the long-term product road map and to hands-on development. Your responsibilities will include shipping high-quality and resilient code and collaborating with designers, product managers, data analysts, other engineers and agency partners. You’ll write code, configure no- and low-code integrations, contribute to our documentation, share your expertise and proactively solve problems.

As a member of our expanding, crossfunctional product team, you’ll work with colleagues across ProPublica’s engineering, audience and membership operations, ensuring that our capabilities align with our principles and advance our organizational objectives. This position reports to our director of product engineering and will work closely with the audience data and insights analyst.

  • Integrate the systems behind them: messaging tools, payments and donation processing platforms, user accounts, CDP and CRM, and the data infrastructure that connect them.
  • Instrument the audience and donor journey. Set up accurate and actionable event tracking so every meaningful step is captured cleanly and becomes data we can act on.
  • Support making experimentation routine. Build the infrastructure for A/B testing and, with internal business teams, run experiments regularly so our decisions rest on evidence instead of guesswork.
  • Write front-end  services and integrations as needed. (Our site runs on Wordpress VIP.)
  • Working with our engineering leaders, protect reader privacy and keep us compliant with legal and regulatory requirements.

  • Experience interacting with audience and reader data platforms, such as Salesforce, Google Analytics, Parse.ly, Sailthru, or similar CRMs, CDPs and analytics tools.
  • Experience working on a customer data platform implementation within the last two years.
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, with experience in a highly collaborative team environment, supporting diverse stakeholders and adapting solutions to evolving business needs.

  • Knowledge of newsroom workflows and a passion for journalism.

job.title: Executive Director, Human Resources
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a strategic, consultative, and data-driven Executive Director of Human Resources to lead HR across North America. Reporting to the COO, this leader will serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership, providing insights, recommendations, and counsel that connect talent strategy to business priorities. 


The ideal candidate brings strong business acumen, sound judgment, and the ability to influence effectively at all levels. They will use workforce data, including attrition trends and employee insights, to identify organizational challenges, inform recommendations, and develop strategies that strengthen retention, leadership effectiveness, and business performance. 


This role requires a balance of strategic advisory leadership and hands-on execution, along with a commitment to developing the HR team and fostering a high-performing, accountable, and engaged workforce. 


Who You Are: 

  • You are a strategic HR leader who operates as a trusted advisor and consultant, challenging assumptions, offering thoughtful recommendations, and influencing decisions that support business outcomes. 
  • You build credibility with senior leaders by combining sound judgment, strong relationships, business acumen, and data-backed insights. 
  • You translate complex workforce trends and organizational challenges into clear, actionable recommendations and measurable strategies. 
  • You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, advising leaders through difficult decisions, and balancing employee needs with business priorities. 
  • You are a strong people leader who coaches, mentors, and develops your team while promoting accountability, continuous improvement, and a solutions-oriented approach. 
  • You work collaboratively with your colleagues globally from talent acquisition, total rewards, HRIS, legal and finance to ensure seamless support for your key business stakeholders. 

What You’ll Do: 

  • Strategic Advisory & Business Partnership: Serve as a trusted advisor to the COO and senior leaders, providing consultative guidance on organizational strategy, workforce planning, organizational design, leadership effectiveness, and talent priorities. Influence decisions through sound analysis, business context, and actionable recommendations. 
  • Data, Analytics & Workforce Insights: Lead the analysis and reporting of workforce trends, including attrition, retention, turnover drivers, engagement, headcount, and talent movement. Translate findings into clear insights and recommendations that inform leadership decisions and shape people strategies. 
  • Attrition & Retention Strategy: Produce regular attrition reporting and insights, identifying trends, patterns, and potential root causes across teams and populations. Partner with leaders to develop targeted retention strategies, monitor outcomes, and assess the effectiveness of interventions. 
  • Leadership Coaching & Influence: Advise and coach executives and managers on leadership effectiveness, team dynamics, performance, accountability, employee development, and complex people decisions. Build leaders’ capability to manage and develop their teams effectively. 
  • Performance & Talent Management: Lead performance management, talent reviews, succession planning, talent mapping, career development, and internal mobility initiatives. Use data and organizational insights to identify talent risks, capability gaps, and opportunities to strengthen performance and retention. 
  • Organizational Effectiveness & Change: Consult with leaders on organizational structure, workforce capabilities, resource allocation, and change management. Provide recommendations that improve collaboration, clarify accountability, and align people and resources with business objectives. 
  • Learning & Development: Identify leadership and workforce capability gaps and establish development strategies, training programs, and learning opportunities that support current and future business needs.

Working closely with the managing editors’ team, you will act as the Guardian’s central lead on duty of care for journalists. You will design, embed and oversee practical strategies that protect our editorial staff, in an evolving and increasingly hostile climate.

 

This role primarily supports our UK editorial operations including our network of international correspondents, while collaborating closely with colleagues across Guardian US and Guardian Australia to maintain and elevate global best practices.
