job.title: LA Kings - Sr Director Human Resources
job.description:
The LA Kings are where hockey, culture, and community come together. As one of the most iconic franchises in the NHL, the Kings deliver high‑energy games, unforgettable moments, and a game‑night experience that goes far beyond the ice.

Owned by AEG, the LA Kings are powered by teams who bring passion, precision, and pride to everything they do, from game‑day operations and fan experiences to the work that happens behind the scenes. Every role plays a part in creating nights fans remember and a culture that represents Los Angeles.   If you want to be part of a team where the work matters on and off the ice, there’s a place for you here. You’re part of what makes it happen.

Job Summary

The Sr Director Human Resources provides strategic and operational leadership for the human resources function supporting the AEG Sports properties, including the LA Kings and Ontario Reign. The role serves as a senior advisor to business leaders on organizational design, workforce planning, leadership coaching, employee relations, talent strategy, and change initiatives. The Sr Director leads the HR team and provides direction across process improvement, staff development, talent acquisition, learning and development, compliance, and employee relations. This role works across each organization and department to promote consistent, practical, and business-aligned application of human resources programs, policies, and practices while addressing the distinct needs of each property. 

Essential Functions

  • Translate business priorities into an integrated Human Resources strategy for each supported property. Advise senior leaders on workforce, organization, and people implications of business decisions. Participate in key leadership and department discussions, bringing a broad HR perspective and recommending practical solutions that support near-term operating needs and longer-term objectives.
  • Maintain current knowledge of industry trends and employment legislation and oversee the organization's compliance. Assess the impact of regulatory and policy changes, communicate requirements to leaders, and recommend updates to policies, procedures, controls, and practices to reduce risk and support consistent application.
  • Lead the Human Resources department, establish priorities, clarify accountability, coach and develop team members, and monitor goals and service delivery to ensure work is completed accurately, consistently, and in a timely manner.
  • Connect broader business strategy to HR priorities and ensure programs remain relevant to the needs of the supported organizations. Identify patterns and opportunities across properties and recommend approaches, policies, and processes that improve organizational effectiveness, productivity, and HR service delivery.
  • Provide proactive counsel on complex and sensitive people matters, serving as a trusted advisor, coach, and thought partner to senior leaders. Frame issues, assess risk and organizational impact, develop well-supported recommendations, and guide leaders toward timely and sustainable resolutions. Oversee significant employee relations matters and partner with Legal as appropriate.
  • Provide strategic direction for employee experience, recognition, training, and development initiatives. Partner with leadership and the administration team to assess organizational and employee needs, identify capability gaps, prioritize learning solutions, and evaluate whether programs support business and talent objectives.
  • Provide oversight for core HR operations supporting new hires, employee changes, payroll coordination, and benefits administration. Establish appropriate review and escalation practices, ensure regulatory and policy compliance, partner with Legal as needed, and provide leaders and employees with clear interpretation of HR policies.
  • Lead the performance review and merit increase processes for supported properties, ensure appropriate planning and governance, monitor completion and quality of performance discussions, and address exceptions with leadership and corporate partners.
  • Serve as the senior HR liaison between AEG corporate partners and the supported properties. Shape local implementation of enterprise programs and initiatives, communicate business requirements and feedback, and promote alignment while accounting for legitimate operating differences.
  • Provide governance and oversight for the integrity, security, and confidentiality of employee data and records, including documentation standards, access controls, record retention, and lawful disposition of personnel files.
  • Oversee talent acquisition strategy and execution across supported departments. Ensure recruitment, selection, and hiring decisions follow approved practices, address critical and hard-to-fill needs, strengthen candidate quality and experience, and support retention of key talent.
  • Develop and manage the Human Resources budget and workforce plan. Allocate resources against business priorities, monitor spending and capacity, and recommend adjustments that support effective and sustainable HR delivery.

Required Qualifications

  • BA/BS Degree (4-year) in Business Management, Business Administration, or Human Resources Management. Advanced degree preferred. 
  • 7+ years of Human Resources leadership experience, including direct people leadership, experience advising senior executives, and responsibility for leading a broad HR function or major client group.
  • Broad experience across Human Resources disciplines, including compensation, talent acquisition, employee relations, performance management, and talent management, with the ability to integrate these areas into practical business solutions.
  • Experience leading and developing HR teams that support multiple locations, properties, or business units.
  • Experience with Human Resource Information Systems (i.e. UltiPro; Workday; Oracle; PeopleSoft); and Applicant Tracking Systems (i.e. Greenhouse; Taleo)
  • Experience with compensation planning, job leveling, workforce planning, and organizational design and development.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and improving HR initiatives that support measurable business and organizational outcomes.
  • Experience working within entertainment or sports industry is preferred.
  • SPHR or SHRM-SCP is highly preferred.
Skills and Abilities
  • Demonstrated ability to anticipate, assess, and resolve complex and sensitive Human Resources matters using sound judgment, discretion, and an appropriate balance of business and employee considerations.
  • Executive-level verbal, written, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex or sensitive matters clearly and follow through on commitments.
  • Strong knowledge of California, Federal and local employment laws including, but not limited to, ADA, FLSA, EEOC, Title VII, Pay Transparency, etc.
  • Ability to professionally handle sensitive and confidential information
  • Ability to establish credibility and influence decisions with senior leaders while communicating effectively across all levels of the organization.
  • Ability to navigate conflict, competing priorities, and ambiguity and to recommend balanced, sustainable solutions.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to synthesize data, identify implications, and present clear recommendations.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office Products (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) and ability to learn applicable business systems.
  • HR Systems knowledge (i.e., UltiPro, applicant tracking system)
  • Ability to read, listen and communicate effectively.
  • Able to balance strategic priorities with operational requirements and respond with an appropriate sense of urgency.

Bonus: This position is eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements.

Position Summary:

The Senior Director of Production serves as AEG's on-site representative providing strategic leadership for the operational and execution of large-scale touring productions. Serving as the senior production representative on assigned tours, this role oversees daily show operations, revenue optimization, and cross-functional coordination to maximize tour performance. The Senior Director partners with artists, promoters, venue personnel, ticketing, and production teams to drive operational excellence while ensuring accurate execution throughout the tour lifecycle.

Essential Functions:

  • Lead the day-to-day operational and financial execution of assigned touring productions, serving as the senior production representative with responsibility for production delivery, show settlements, and operational decision-making.
  • Drive revenue optimization by evaluating venue configurations, production layouts, and ticket inventory opportunities to maximize sellable seating while maintaining production, safety, and guest experience standards.
  • Oversee daily financial settlements, expense management, and accounting activities, ensuring timely reconciliation and compliance with internal financial controls and contractual requirements.
  • Coordinate cross-functional tour operations by partnering with ticketing, venue management, production, catering, temporary staffing, and other internal and external stakeholders to ensure seamless show execution.
  • Provide subject matter expertise and operational leadership by developing best practices, mentoring production staff, and supporting organizational initiatives related to tour operations, financial processes, and production standards.

Required Qualifications:

  • Extensive experience managing large-scale touring productions, including live event operations and financial settlements.
  • Strong knowledge of production accounting, revenue management, and ticketing operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to make independent operational decisions in high-pressure, live event environments.
  • Experience with tour settlement systems, ticketing platforms, and production management software.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams.
  • Experience managing multiple complex projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including advanced Excel skills, and experience using budgeting, project management, and financial systems.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships with clients, venues, and co-workers
  • Excellent written, verbal and listening communication skills
  • Strong organizational skills
  • Self-motivated and takes initiative
  • May require heavy travel for long period of time of the road

job.title: Ticketing Operations Analyst - Product Ops
job.description:
AXS connects fans with the artists and teams they love. Each year we sell millions of tickets to thousands of incredible events – from concerts and festivals to sports and theater – at some of the most iconic venues in the world. Since our founding in 2011, we’ve consistently pushed the industry forward and improved experiences for fans, making it easier than ever to discover events, find the perfect seats, and enjoy unforgettable live entertainment, and we continue to lead the evolution of our industry today.

We’re passionate about improving the fan experience and providing game-changing solutions for our clients, and we’re always looking for smart, motivated people to help make it happen. Bring your enthusiasm, your big ideas, and your desire to team up with some of the best and brightest in technology and entertainment.  

The Role

The Ticketing Operations Analyst – Product Operations coordinates cross-departmental product initiatives, ensuring effective stakeholder engagement in User Acceptance Testing and managing issue tracking with product teams under the supervision of the Manager, Ticketing Operations.  The role also supports data cleansing efforts and fraud monitoring, collaborates on triage and escalation of product issues, and participates in after-hours on-call rotations as needed. 

What Will You Do?

  • Recruits, coordinates, and holds accountable the business stakeholders required to complete User Acceptance Testing (UAT) on new AXS products and features, working closely with the Product Owner and Project Managers. 
  • Assists with the evaluation and escalation of Global Triage bug tickets. Troubleshoots any reported issues and resolves or escalates as needed. 
  • Serves as overflow support to team members responsible for creating and validating fees, investigating fee variance tickets, and managing Apex user accounts. 
  • Assists with completing client and promoter requests for OTL sweeps, generating reports on problematic orders for clients, and coordinating the bulk cancellation of orders in violation of ticket limits. 
  • Participates in an on-call rotation with other department staff to assist with daily bulk refunds for rescheduled events and triaging emergency requests after hours and on weekends. 
  • Provides general and project-specific assistance as needed to the other Ticketing Operations staff under the supervision of the Manager, Ticketing Operations. 

What Will You Bring?

  • BA/BS Degree in Computer Science, Business Administration, or Marketing major preferred. 
  • 2-4 years of significant experience in live event ticketing and/or ticketing software administration may be substituted for equivalent education depending on the nature of the work experience. 
  • Ability to independently manage complex projects
  • Familiarity with software testing protocols  
  • Excel experience required, including a familiarity with data parsing and vlookup functions 
  • Strong communication skills and the ability gracefully enforce accountability standards 
  • Ability to juggle multiple pressing priorities and meet aggressive deadlines 
  • Flexibility in adapting to rules and processes that frequently evolve 

 

At AXS, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but can't "check every box" in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be the right candidate for this or other roles.

Currently, full time employees are eligible for these benefits on the first day of employment.

*Employer does not offer work visa sponsorship for this position.

 

What’s in it for You?

  • Extraordinary People – we’re not kidding!
  • Meaningful Mission– Helping revolutionize an industry and deliver better experiences for fans and clients around the world.
  • Development and Learning – Opportunities for learning and leveling up through training and education reimbursement.
  • Community & Belonging – A range of Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that foster connection, inclusion, and professional growth. Access to meaningful volunteer opportunities and community engagement programs to make a positive impact beyond the workplace.

 

 

More about AXS

AXS, a subsidiary of AEG, sells millions of tickets each year for 1600+ premier venues, sports teams, and event organizers across North America, Europe, Asia, Australia and New Zealand. Headquartered in Downtown Los Angeles, California, AXS employs more than 900 professionals in multiple locations worldwide. In each location you’ll find a team of dedicated, diverse employees (we’ve dubbed ourselves “Fanatix”) who create groundbreaking products and services in a fun, fast-paced environment. 

To learn more about our culture and values, visit: https://solutions.axs.com/careers/

AEG brings music, sports, and live entertainment together to create moments people feel, share, and remember around the world. Each year, more than 100 million fans experience over 13,000 live events across five continents, from iconic concerts and major festivals to championship-level sports and entertainment destinations.
Powered by a passion for live experiences and the people behind them, we connect artists, teams, fans, and communities through world-class venues, events, and partnerships that shape culture and bring people together.

WHO ARE WE?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide.  Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com.

 

WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on! 

 

THE JOB

The New York City Production Department is looking for a Production Manager who oversees the execution, management, and administration of production operations for all Live Nation-operated and third-party venues, including amphitheaters, arenas and stadiums in the region. Collaborating with the operations, talent management, and finance teams, the department plays a crucial role in liaising with clients, event planners, performing talent, venues, technical and site vendors, labor unions, and other key stakeholders to ensure the success of all events, both front and back of house.

 

The ideal Production Manager will have the ability to handle multiple projects and adapt to fast-paced, changing environments while maintaining quality and demonstrating exemplary leadership and teamwork. The candidate will be directly responsible for managing 75+ shows annually, and some travel within the region will be required.

 

WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO

  • Oversee all on-stage, backstage, technical, and site planning aspects of events.
  • Advance and obtain key technical information, including venue specs, production needs, rider requirements, staging, and capacity changes.
  • Develop and maintain production documents such as site drawings, on-sale layouts, timelines, schedules, and artist riders.
  • Settlement of shows would be high priorty
  • Produce events across a range of venue sizes—from clubs and theaters to amphitheaters arenas and stadiums.
  • Manage technical production elements (e.g., stage, sound, video, lighting, backline, broadcast, labor crews).
  • Support site operations (e.g., power, heavy equipment, traffic flow, crowd control, sanitation, permitting, and engineering).
  • Track and assist with budget management for assigned responsibilities.
  • Lead multiple projects from planning through execution, including on-site presence from load-in to load-out.
  • Maintain consistent communication with stakeholders and senior leadership through meetings, calls, and emails.
  • Facilitate interdepartmental coordination and follow up on action items from internal and external meetings.
  • Foster a positive, collaborative environment for planning teams.
  • Contribute to event debriefs, including financial settlement notes and recommendations for future improvements.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

 

WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING

  • 5+ years of production management experience across varied venue types and event scales
  • Proven project management and planning expertise, with the ability to manage multiple events simultaneously
  • Strong leadership and decision-making skills, especially under pressure and with limited information
  • Proficiency in both Windows and Mac OS applications (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, OneNote, SharePoint)
  • Exceptional organizational and communication skills—written, verbal, and interpersonal
  • Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and maintain composure in fast-paced environments
  • Experience procuring vendors (e.g., staging, audio, lighting, video) and managing staff, services, and budgets
  • Flexible schedule with availability for nights, weekends, holidays, and regional travel as needed
  • Skilled in diplomatic communication with clients, vendors, and artist representatives
  • Adaptability to new technologies, workflows, and evolving event environments

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting live events, entertainment, music, production, hospitality, or another project-based industry.
  • Familiarity with QuickBooks, PEX, DocuSign, Dropbox, and spreadsheet-based tracking tools.
  • Experience with accounts payable, vendor onboarding, payroll coordination, contractor agreements, or expense reconciliation.
  • Experience coordinating meetings, calendars, staffing details, and cross-functional project follow-up.
  • Familiarity with event budgets, project codes, cost allocations, or post-event closeout processes.
  • Comfort working in a collaborative environment where priorities can change quickly.

 

BENEFITS & PERKS

Our motto is ‘Taking Care of Our Own’ through 6 pillars of benefits:

 

HEALTH: Medical, vision, dental and mental health benefits for you and your family, with access to a health care concierge, and Flexible or Health Savings Accounts (FSA or HSA)

YOURSELF: Free concert tickets, generous paid time off including paid holidays, sick time, and personal days

WEALTH: 401(k) program with company match, stock reimbursement program

FAMILY: New parent programs including caregiver leave, plus fertility, adoption, foster, or surrogacy support

CAREER: Career and skill development programs with School of Live, tuition reimbursement, and student loan repayment

OTHERS: Volunteer time off, crowdfunding match

 

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

We aspire to build teams that reflect and support the fans and artists we serve. Every day we aim to promote environments where everyone can be themselves, contribute fully, and thrive within our company and at our events. As a growing business we will encourage you to develop your professional and personal aspirations, enjoy new experiences, and learn from the talented people you will be working with. 


Live Nation strongly supports equal employment opportunity for all applicants regardless of age (40 and over), ancestry, color, religious creed (including religious dress and grooming practices), family and medical care leave or the denial of family and medical care leave, mental or physical disability (including HIV and AIDS), marital status, domestic partner status, medical condition (including cancer and genetic characteristics), genetic information, military and veteran status, political affiliation, national origin (including language use restrictions), citizenship, race, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding), gender, gender identity, and gender expression, sexual orientation, intersectionality, or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state or local law, rule, ordinance or regulation. 

 

We will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the Los Angeles Fair Chance Ordinance, San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act and consistent with other similar and / or applicable laws in other areas.

 

We also afford equal employment opportunities to qualified individuals with a disability. For this reason, Live Nation will make reasonable accommodations for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified individual with a disability who is an applicant consistent with its legal obligations to do so, including reasonable accommodations related to pregnancy in accordance with applicable local, state and / or federal law. As part of its commitment to make reasonable accommodations, Live Nation also wishes to participate in a timely, good faith, interactive process with a disabled applicant to determine effective reasonable accommodations, if any, which can be made in response to a request for accommodations. Applicants are invited to identify reasonable accommodations that can be made to assist them to perform the essential functions of the position they seek. Any applicant who requires an accommodation in order to perform the essential functions of the job should contact a Human Resources Representative to request the opportunity to participate in a timely interactive process.  Live Nation will also provide reasonable religious accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

 

HIRING PRACTICES

job.title: Acting Lex Columnist
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to inclusion and fairness
We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

The role

This is an opportunity for a UK-based financial journalist to cover a period of parental leave at the FT’s award-winning Lex opinion column.

At Lex we write views on companies and markets. No hot takes — only concise, deeply informed, analytical notes on big business, public and private markets and what makes finance tick.

We are looking for a numerate, naturally curious writer who wants to provoke debate with well-reported insights. The Lex column is central to the FT’s premium subscription strategy, and reaches an influential, engaged global audience.

Sector expertise is welcome, but we'll also want to see that you are an all-rounder. We’ll help you hone your ability to write punchy, directional and entertaining opinion.

 

What you will bring to the role

Analytical rigor: A strong grasp of corporate reporting, accounting, and the mechanics of M&A and earnings.

Conviction: The ability to generate clear, directional, and deeply reported views, backed up with numbers.

Intellectual agility: A fearless approach to untangling complex, unfamiliar topics.

Source management: A knack for conducting difficult, probing and diplomatic conversations with high-level sources.

Ambition: A drive to make a tangible impact, both in the market and within the FT newsroom.

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Thursday 19th November 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

FT Newsroom staff are expected to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, subject to role requirements and regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for Editorial roles.

 

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

job.title: Product Manager
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Together, we help audiences stay better informed and deepen their understanding of the world around them.

Our Product & Tech teams drive us forward in an ever-evolving digital landscape, delivering cutting-edge products to over one million digital subscribers daily. Our growth relies on a diverse, dedicated and dynamic group of product, tech, delivery and data specialists.

With a supportive culture, entrepreneurial spirit and opportunities at every turn, there are no limits to where your FT career can take you.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

About the role

The FT app is an important part of how subscribers engage with FT journalism, and we believe there is a significant opportunity to go further. We're looking for an experienced Product Manager with a strong background in native and/or cross-platform mobile apps to play a central role in this transformation.

You'll join at a pivotal moment, working alongside our Principal Product Manager, engineering and design colleagues to turn our app strategy into reality, delivering improvements to the app experience and building the capabilities that will support its continued evolution.

This is an opportunity to shape a product used by a highly engaged global audience, while helping establish a stronger mobile product discipline within the FT.

What you'll be doing

Help shape the future of the FT app

  • Work with the Principal Product Manager to translate our long-term app strategy into clear product requirements, priorities and a deliverable roadmap.
  • Bring specialist mobile product knowledge and experience to decisions about the future app experience, challenging assumptions and finding opportunities to make better use of native device capabilities.
  • Develop a deep understanding of our customers, their behaviours and the moments in which they turn to the FT, using research, analytics and experimentation to see opportunities.
  • Champion a mobile-first approach to product development, ensuring we're designing around the needs of app customers and complementing their web experience.
  • Work across product teams to ensure the app delivers a coherent, premium experience that delivers meaningful value for the business, while making effective use of shared FT capabilities.

Deliver a distinctive, premium mobile experience

  • Own and prioritise defined areas of the app roadmap, balancing customer value, strategic impact, technical dependencies and commercial outcomes.
  • Work day-to-day with engineering, design, data and editorial colleagues to take initiatives from discovery through development, release and iteration.
  • Help deliver experiences that make the FT more essential to customers' daily routines, including better navigation, discovery, personalisation, notifications, offline experiences and continuity across devices.
  • Explore opportunities to make FT journalism more engaging and useful through native mobile interactions and seamless experiences across text, audio, video, data and other formats.
  • Collaborate with teams responsible for identity, subscriptions and customer lifecycle to make the app a more effective platform for acquisition, engagement, retention and subscriber growth.
  • Establish clear success measures, use experimentation and customer feedback to inform decisions, and continuously optimise the experience.
  • Ensure that performance, accessibility, reliability and usability are treated as fundamental parts of the product experience.

Build mobile product expertise within the FT

  • Act as a source of specialist mobile product knowledge for colleagues across product, design and engineering.
  • Share best practices in app product management, including platform conventions, app store requirements, release management, mobile analytics and experimentation.
  • Help establish effective ways of working for developing and maintaining high-quality iOS and Android experiences.
  • Stay informed about developments in mobile technology, customer expectations and emerging product capabilities, identifying opportunities relevant to the FT.

About you

Essential experience and skills

  • Proven mobile app product management experience: You have owned and delivered meaningful improvements to consumer-facing iOS and/or Android apps, ideally within products with significant scale, frequent usage or complex customer journeys.
  • Understanding of mobile technologies: You have practical experience working with native and/or cross-platform development teams and understand the differences, opportunities and trade-offs between architectures. You don't need to be an engineer, but you can engage in technical discussions and understand the product implications of architectural decisions.
  • Knowledge of the mobile ecosystem: You're familiar with Apple and Google's platform conventions, app store policies, submission and release processes, in-app purchases, push notifications, device capabilities and the considerations involved in delivering consistently high-quality app experiences.
  • Strong product management fundamentals: You're experienced in customer discovery, defining problems and opportunities, prioritisation, roadmap management, experimentation and measuring product outcomes.
  • Proven delivery experience: You've worked closely with cross-functional engineering and design teams to deliver products iteratively, navigate technical complexity and balance short-term improvements with longer-term investment.
  • Customer and commercial focus: You use qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand customer needs, make decisions and evaluate success. You understand how product experience contributes to engagement, retention and commercial performance.
  • Collaborative and influential: You're comfortable working across organisational boundaries, bringing different disciplines together and influencing decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: You can operate effectively while technology choices, team structures and delivery approaches are evolving, helping turn strategic ambition into practical action.

Desirable experience

  • Experience working on subscription-based digital products, particularly in publishing, media, content or other habit-forming consumer services.
  • Experience developing products that combine native and web-based capabilities.
  • Experience with personalisation, content discovery, notifications, offline functionality or other features that drive regular app engagement.
  • Experience working with external development partners while retaining internal product ownership.
  • Experience helping organisations establish or mature their mobile product development practices.

 

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location, but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available on the FT Careers website.

We’ve embraced a 50% hybrid working model (averaging two to three days onsite) that fosters trust and remote adaptability while encouraging in-person camaraderie and peer learning. Additionally, we are open to accommodating specific flexible working pattern requests for all roles where feasible.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of the team will be happy to help.

Further information

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may leverage AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience and qualifications.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

You’ll play a key role in shaping and evolving Origami, the FT’s design system, helping teams across the business create coherent, accessible and high-quality digital experiences.

Working closely with designers, engineers and product managers, you’ll develop shared foundations, components and guidance that make it easier for teams to design and build products that feel distinctly FT.

The role spans web and mobile, requiring thoughtful decisions about where shared patterns create consistency and where platform-specific approaches deliver better experiences.

You’ll also explore how AI can support the future of design systems. From accelerating component development and documentation to helping teams prototype and build using Origami, you’ll test emerging approaches and identify opportunities to improve how we work.

Combining strong design craft with hands-on technical skills, you’ll help ensure Origami remains dependable, accessible and relevant as our products and technologies evolve.

  • A portfolio demonstrating high-quality product design and design systems work, clearly explaining your contribution and impact.

  • Advanced experience using Figma, including component libraries, variables and design tokens.

  • Experience building interactive prototypes using code, with a working knowledge of HTML and CSS.

  • Strong technical understanding and confidence collaborating with engineers on feasibility, implementation and design trade-offs.

  • Experience designing for web and mobile, with an understanding of platform conventions and when different approaches are appropriate.

  • Knowledge of accessibility principles and experience applying them to components, patterns and digital experiences.

  • Experience using or exploring AI-assisted design and development tools, with sound judgement about their opportunities and limitations.

  • Experience leading cross-functional design work, navigating ambiguity and influencing decisions without formal authority.

  • Strong communication and documentation skills, with the ability to explain design decisions and build relationships across teams.

  • A collaborative, systems-oriented approach and the ability to help others understand and adopt shared design practices.

Desirable

  • Experience supporting the adoption of a design system across multiple product teams.

  • Experience exploring how AI tools can use design system guidance, components or code to support product development.

  • Experience evaluating the effectiveness of design systems through feedback, usage evidence or measures of quality and adoption.

We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning. job.title: VP, Ad Operations & Campaign Management
job.description:
About the Daily Beast

The Daily Beast delivers award-winning original reporting and sharp opinions from big personalities in the arenas of politics, pop culture, world news, and more. Fiercely independent and armed with irreverent intelligence, The Daily Beast now reaches more than 20 million readers per month.

Job Description

The Daily Beast is seeking a dynamic and dedicated VP, Ad Operations & Campaign Management to join our news team.

About the Role

We're hiring an analytical, hands-on and detail-oriented leader to run our ad business across our audience of nearly 50 million. You'll lead a small team, manage ad tech and inventory performance, and make sure every campaign delivers and every client comes back.

What You'll Do

  • Lead, coach and grow a small team across ad operations, media planning and campaign management, including full-time contractor resources
  • Partner with Sales and Marketing on RFPs, media plans and avails that win business and are built to deliver
  • Bring fresh thinking to how we manage and package our wide range of inventory, including web, in-app, podcasts, newsletters, social and more, and partner with Sales and Product to develop new ad products across these and emerging channels
  • Set the standard for flawless campaign execution, from launch, trafficking and QA through pacing, delivery and post-sale reporting, and turn results into renewals
  • Drive ad tech and performance across all inventory: viewability, fill, ad load, page speed and discrepancies
  • Lead the ad tech stack strategy and operations (GAM, header bidding, SSP integrations, ads.txt, CMP), plus verification and measurement vendors
  • Partner with EPD (Engineering, Product & Design) and Programmatic as a key stakeholder on all things ad product
  • Work with the Programmatic team on new partner integrations and A/B tests of new products and solutions, balancing revenue growth with page experience
  • Build the workflows and reporting that give leadership a clear view of campaign and delivery health
  • Serve as the senior escalation point for priority clients

What You Bring

  • 10+ years in digital ad operations or campaign management, ideally at a publisher; 5+ years leading teams
  • Expert in ad tech platforms (GAM, SSPs, OMS) and programmatic
  • Cross-channel campaign experience beyond web display
  • Full sales cycle experience: RFPs, media planning, execution, reporting and renewals
  • Hands-on with Boostr (or similar), DoubleVerify/IAS, Comscore and Google Analytics
  • Track record of improving delivery, efficiency and retention, with the numbers to show it
  • Analytical, detail-oriented and hands-on with data; calm and decisive in a fast-paced environment

Pay Range Salary

The pay range for this position is $140,000 - $175,000.

The base salary range represents the anticipated low and high ends of the salary range for this position. Actual salaries may vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors, including but not limited to work location, experience, performance, and other factors.

Additional Information

Don’t meet every single requirement listed here? If you’re interested in joining the Beast but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with this job description, we encourage you to give it a shot all the same. It might turn out that you’re just the right candidate for this or other roles. See more about our commitment to diversity at https://www.thedailybeast.com/company/diversity

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

job.title: Intern, Membership Accounts
job.description:
INTERNSHIP DETAILS 

 

SPRING INTERNSHIP 

APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR STUDENTS: 11/20/2026 

SPRING INTERNSHIP PROGRAM DATES: 1/11/2027 – 4/16/2027  

*The Membership Accounts Intern position pays county/state minimum wage rates, based on work location. 

 

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

 

The Recording Academy Membership Accounts team is seeking a “rock star” student for a spring 2027 Internship with our team. 


Celebrating music through the Grammy® Awards, The Recording Academy continues its legacy as the premier national organization for honoring achievements in the recording arts and supporting the music community. As a membership organization, we represent the most talented music professionals in the world. Our members include recording artists, producers, engineers, attorneys, music supervisors, composers/arrangers, managers, agents, social media and record label executives and many others. 


Our paid Internship Program offers a unique opportunity for full-time college students (juniors or seniors) to gain on-site training in office administration, events management and artist relations, in exchange for college credit. Candidates should be energetic, hard-working and have aspirations of a career in the music industry.



WHAT YOU'LL DO


  • Internship duration is for a semester (12 weeks or equivalent).
  • Hours are part-time (20-24 hours a week).
  • Intern will work in support of the membership outreach team that works on membership recruitment strategy.  
  • Internship will provide in-depth exposure to professional recording industry.
  • Projects may include research across genres for prospective members, data entry, correspondence, database management and general administrative support. 



SKILLS & EXPERIENCE


  • Currently enrolled in a college/university. One year of course work towards degree in related field is preferred.
  • Letter from school stating that intern will receive college credit for the Recording Academy internship.
  • Display an interest in music and commitment to a career in the recording industry.
  • Possess strong verbal, written and analytical skills.
  • Exhibit proficient computer skills.
  • Be a junior, senior or graduate student.
  • Salesforce experience a plus.



PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES:   

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.   


While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time. The employee will be required to lift and/or move up to 60 pounds.   

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES 

 

RECORDING ACADEMY 

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators. 

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY 

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. Edelman is a voice synonymous with trust, reimagining a future where the currency of communication is action. Our culture thrives on three promises: boldness is possibility, empathy is progress, and curiosity is momentum.

  • Relentless Pursuit of Excellence
  • Courage to Do the Right Thing

Edelman is looking for a Senior Account Manager to play a major role within our Reputation team.


We need a strategic, confident and detail-oriented senior manager who can help clients navigate complex business and reputational challenges, strengthen stakeholder trust and communicate effectively across earned, digital and integrated channels.

  • A collaborative mindset, with the ability to partner with creative, digital, social, paid media and insights specialists to develop integrated programs spanning corporate positioning, executive profiling, thought leadership and issues management; build strong client and colleague relationships; and demonstrate behaviours consistent with Edelman’s values and Code of Ethics and Business Conduct

This is an existing opportunity to join our team as a Corporate Affairs Intern – someone curious, creative, proactive, and genuinely excited about the intersection of business, reputation and current affairs.

In this paid internship role, you’ll work alongside experienced corporate communications and advisory professionals supporting clients across a variety of industries, including financial and professional services, energy and technology. From monitoring and analysis and media relations to stakeholder engagement and thought leadership, you'll gain hands-on experience helping organizations tell their stories and build trust with their audiences.

job.title: Executive, Digital Strategy
job.description:
Opportunity

Brunswick Group is seeking a curious, resourceful, and ambitious Executive to join our U.S. Digital practice.

At Brunswick, we work on the issues that define industries and shape the future of business. Our Digital team helps some of the world's most influential organizations navigate complex communications challenges, build and protect their reputations, and engage the audiences that matter most in an increasingly digital world.

This is a role for a self-starter who is eager to learn, thrives in a fast-paced environment, brings intellectual curiosity and creativity to complex challenges, and is driven to deliver outstanding results. If you want to help some of the world's leading organizations navigate their most consequential challenges – from M&A and crisis to corporate positioning and reputation – Brunswick offers a platform unlike any other in our industry.

About the Role

As an Executive, you will work alongside experienced advisers to support a diverse portfolio of clients and high-stakes issues. You will contribute to research, strategic recommendations and hands-on execution, developing the skills to become a trusted digital adviser.

  • Client Contribution & Handling
    • Support the development and execution of digital communications strategies across a range of high-stakes issues, including corporate reputation, financial situations, litigation, crisis, and public affairs.
    • Draft high-quality client materials, including strategy presentations, research reports, messaging, campaign plans, and performance updates.
    • Analyze online conversations, media coverage, platform activity, and other sources of intelligence, translating findings into clear, actionable insights.
    • Support the planning, implementation, and evaluation of digital campaigns across paid, owned, and earned channels.
    • Leverage digital analytics, social listening, AI, and other research tools to support client work and uncover emerging risks and opportunities.
    • Contribute creative ideas and practical recommendations to client discussions, brainstorms, and new business pitches.
    • Leverage in-house AI tools and other resources to manage workload and keep deliverables on track, on time, and of the highest quality.
  • Teamwork and Collaborative Approach
    • Collaborate with colleagues across Brunswick, bringing digital expertise to integrated client teams.
    • Proactively share relevant digital developments, emerging trends, platform changes, and new technologies with colleagues.
    • Take ownership of assigned responsibilities, anticipate team needs, and contribute solutions without waiting to be asked.
    • Develop strong working relationships with colleagues and clients, demonstrating professionalism, responsiveness, and discretion.
    • Participate in and contribute to training sessions where appropriate and take advantage of the learning and engagement opportunities Brunswick provides.

What We're Looking For

At Brunswick, we seek smart and curious individuals dedicated to learning and growth. We value potential, strong work ethic, sound judgement, and excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Standout Executive candidates demonstrate:

  • 1-3 years of relevant professional experience; experience in strategic communications, campaigns, digital marketing, or an agency environment a strong plus.
  • Experience working on paid digital campaigns, social media management, and digital content development.
  • Working familiarity with digital analytics, social listening, or audience research tools (such as Google analytics, Sprinklr, Brandwatch).
  • Experience using AI and large language models to support research and analysis.
  • A strong understanding of the digital media landscape, including major social and LLM platforms, online communities, the creator economy, and emerging technologies, and familiarity with online formats, features, and content conventions.
  • An interest in business, current affairs, and the issues affecting major corporations and their leaders.
  • Excellent research, analytical, writing, and verbal communication skills.
  • Resourcefulness and proactivity, with the curiosity and agility to tackle unfamiliar challenges, learn quickly, and find creative, practical solutions.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced environment.
  • A collaborative, entrepreneurial mindset.
  • Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive or confidential information.

Why Join Us

Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of exceptional employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.

The successful applicant will be eligible for the following compensation and benefits package: 

Base Pay: The annual base compensation range for this role is $70,000 - $80,000. The base pay offered will be determined by factors including experience, skills, training, office location, certifications, and education.

Bonus Eligibility: Annual discretionary bonus contingent upon individual and firm-wide performance.

Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance. Disability insurance. Employee assistance program. Flexible spending account. Health savings account. Life insurance. Commuter Benefits. Generous Paid Time Off: 25 vacation days and 10 days sick leave, as well as 11 paid company holidays. Firm-sponsored 401(k) Plan with 3% automatic company contribution of base and bonus with an additional 1.5% profit share– immediate vesting. Career training and development opportunities. Employee discounts.

Office Policy: At Brunswick, our work is a craft that thrives in teaching environments – whether in our offices or on-site with clients – through real-time observation, collaboration, human connection, clear guidance and by challenging one another to keep getting better. Our policy is that our team members are in person – either in the office or on-site with clients – at least four days each week.

The firm will provide reasonable accommodation to qualified applicants or employees, as defined by applicable law. In addition to the application, the process may include virtual and in-person interviews, as well as an assessment, which may be timed. To request an accommodation during our application and hiring process, email americasaccommodations@brunswickgroup.com.

About Brunswick

Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes. 

Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. We operate as a “one-firm firm” with no individual profit centers. This allows us to assemble fully integrated, bespoke teams for each client, able to draw on the full resources of Brunswick anywhere in the world. 

 

Brunswick is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. Please read our Global Privacy Notice to understand how your data is managed.

  • Backend language and craft. You are an expert in TypeScript with Node.js or in Python, and a practitioner in the other. You set our backend and frontend coding patterns, framework choices and upgrade path, and you are a practitioner in at least two other crafts. • React and frontend. You set our full-stack conventions across teams: where logic lives, how APIs serve user interfaces, and how shared components are built and maintained.
  • APIs and data formats. You design REST APIs with OpenAPI from first principles: resource modelling, HTTP semantics, pagination, consistent error formats, versioning, idempotency and rate limiting. You know when to use JSON and when to use Protocol Buffers, and how to evolve both without breaking consumers. You set our API and serialisation standards and decide on exceptions.
  • Data. You are fluent in PostgreSQL, including schema design, indexing, query plans, transactions and zero-downtime migrations with Prisma, TypeORM or SQLAlchemy. You design DynamoDB and MongoDB models around access patterns, use Redis for caching, and choose the right store for each workload. You own our data-architecture standards, including how datastores are introduced and retired.
  • Asynchronous systems and reliability. You design event-driven systems on queues and streams such as SQS, Kafka and BullMQ or Celery, using retries, dead-letter queues and idempotent consumers so that at-least-once delivery is safe. You know the outbox and saga patterns and when orchestration is better than choreography. You own our reference architecture for reliability.
  • Cloud and platform. You have built and run production services on AWS or GCP, both as Lambda functions and as Kubernetes workloads, and you understand the trade-offs between them: cold starts, concurrency, cost, capacity and deployment risk. You define infrastructure as code with Terraform or AWS CDK and release safely with canary and blue/green deployments. With Platform Engineering, you decide when we use serverless and when we use Kubernetes, and you set the reference architectures for both.
  • Testing and quality. You practise test-driven development and expect every team to do the same. You build balanced test suites: unit tests with Jest, Vitest or pytest, integration tests with Testcontainers, contract tests with Pact, and Playwright end-to-end tests that gate releases. You set our quality standard and approve any exceptions to it.
  • Observability and performance. You instrument services with OpenTelemetry and use Datadog and CloudWatch to find problems before users do. You profile with flame graphs, measure p95 and p99 latency, and fix causes rather than symptoms. You set our standards for SLOs, dashboards, alerting and performance budgets, and you lead the hardest incidents to their root cause.
  • Security and identity. You write secure code by default and apply the OWASP Top 10 and API Security Top 10 in practice. You design authentication and authorisation with OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, secure service-to-service traffic with mTLS and workload identity, and integrate identity providers such as Okta, Keycloak and Cognito. You set our identity and security standards and own security reviews with the Security team
  • Architecture and design. You design systems that span many services and teams, and you write architecture decision records that make the trade-offs explicit. You own our technical roadmap and style guide, act as the arbiter on standards, and decide on evidence rather than authority. You are able to trace many symptoms back to a single root cause and fix it once.
  • Engineering practices. You work trunk-based with GitHub Flow, small changes and feature flags, and you know CI/CD pipelines inside out. You have led deprecations and migrations all the way to switching the old system off. You set our Git, CI/CD and dependency policies, and you make large-scale change routine rather than exceptional.
  • AI-first engineering and LLMs. You use Claude Code every day and understand how large language models work: tokens, context windows, cost, structured output, embeddings and retrieval. You have built production features with the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs, including tool calling and evaluations, and designed agentic services with clear guardrails and human review. You set our AI-first operating model, covering approved models and frameworks, Claude Code conventions, evaluation and release gates, and governance.
  • Communication, collaboration and initiative. You communicate clearly and concisely in writing and in conversation, and you adapt your message for engineers, product leaders and executives. You understand complex problems quickly, ask the right questions and confirm shared understanding before acting. You collaborate well across locations and cultures, working asynchronously and handing over cleanly between time zones. You are proactive: you spot problems and opportunities before you are asked, propose solutions and innovations of your own, and drive them through without waiting for instructions.
  • Leadership and behaviours. You lead without authority and influence engineering heads and teams across the organisation. You define the hiring bar for each level, calibrate interviewers and give Talent Acquisition clear screening criteria. You mentor senior engineers into technical leaders, build an engineering practice that does not depend on you, and hold the bar under commercial pressure. You say "I don't know" when you don't, and you dig in until you do.

Preferred qualifications:

  • B.Tech or B.E. in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field.
  • Experience maintaining a widely used open-source library.
  • Experience with multi-region and disaster-recovery architecture.
  • Experience mapping engineering controls to SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

  • Experience running an engineering-productivity measurement programme.

job.description:

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 11 years of professional software development in Python, including 5 years of architecture across multiple systems.
  • 3 years of experience owning engineering standards adopted beyond your own team, and mentoring senior engineers.
  • Experience working in globally distributed teams across time zones, with engineering, product and business stakeholders in other regions.
  • Language and craft. You are an expert in Python. You write idiomatic, fully typed Python, understand asyncio and the GIL in depth, and can diagnose concurrency, CPU and memory problems in production. You set our Python version strategy, dependency policy, framework choices (FastAPI or Django) and coding patterns, and you are a practitioner in at least two other crafts.
  • APIs and data formats. You design REST APIs with OpenAPI from first principles: resource modelling, HTTP semantics, pagination, consistent error formats, versioning, idempotency and rate limiting. You know when to use JSON and when to use Protocol Buffers, and how to evolve both without breaking consumers. You set our API and serialisation standards and decide on exceptions.
  • Data. You are fluent in PostgreSQL, including schema design, indexing, query plans, transactions and zero-downtime migrations with SQLAlchemy and Alembic. You design DynamoDB and MongoDB models around access patterns, use Redis for caching, and choose the right store for each workload. You own our data-architecture standards, including how datastores are introduced and retired.
  • Asynchronous systems and reliability. You design event-driven systems on queues and streams such as SQS, Kafka and Celery or Arq, using retries, dead-letter queues and idempotent consumers so that at least-once delivery is safe. You know the outbox and saga patterns and when orchestration is better than choreography. You own our reference architecture for reliability.
  • Cloud and platform. You have built and run production services on AWS or GCP, both as Lambda functions and as Kubernetes workloads, and you understand the trade-offs between them: cold starts, concurrency, cost, capacity and deployment risk. You define infrastructure as code with Terraform or AWS CDK and release safely with canary and blue/green deployments. With Platform Engineering, you decide when we use serverless and when we use Kubernetes, and you set the reference architectures for both.
  • Testing and quality. You practise test-driven development and expect every team to do the same. You build balanced test suites: unit tests with pytest, integration tests with Testcontainers, contract tests with Pact, and Playwright end-to-end tests that gate releases. You set our quality standard and approve any exceptions to it.
  • Observability and performance. You instrument services with OpenTelemetry and use Datadog and CloudWatch to find problems before users do. You profile with flame graphs, measure p95 and p99 latency, and fix causes rather than symptoms. You set our standards for SLOs, dashboards, alerting and performance budgets, and you lead the hardest incidents to their root cause.
  • Security and identity. You write secure code by default and apply the OWASP Top 10 and API Security Top 10 in practice. You design authentication and authorisation with OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, secure service-to-service traffic with mTLS and workload identity, and integrate identity providers such as Okta, Keycloak and Cognito. You set our identity and security standards and own security reviews with the Security team.
  • Architecture and design. You design systems that span many services and teams, and you write architecture decision records that make the trade-offs explicit. You own our technical roadmap and style guide, act as the arbiter on standards, and decide on evidence rather than authority. You are able to trace many symptoms back to a single root cause and fix it once.
  • Engineering practices. You work trunk-based with GitHub Flow, small changes and feature flags, and you know CI/CD pipelines inside out. You have led deprecations and migrations all the way to switching the old system off. You set our Git, CI/CD and dependency policies, and you make large-scale change routine rather than exceptional.
  • AI-first engineering and LLMs. You use Claude Code every day and understand how large language models work: tokens, context windows, cost, structured output, embeddings and retrieval. You have built production features with the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs, including tool calling and evaluations, and designed agentic services with clear guardrails and human review. You set our AI-first operating model, covering approved models and frameworks, Claude Code conventions, evaluation and release gates, and governance.
  • Communication, collaboration and initiative. You communicate clearly and concisely in writing and in conversation, and you adapt your message for engineers, product leaders and executives. You understand complex problems quickly, ask the right questions and confirm shared understanding before acting. You collaborate well across locations and cultures, working asynchronously and handing over cleanly between time zones. You are proactive: you spot problems and opportunities before you are asked, propose solutions and innovations of your own, and drive them through without waiting for instructions.
  • Leadership and behaviours. You lead without authority and influence engineering heads and teams across the organisation. You define the hiring bar for each level, calibrate interviewers and give Talent Acquisition clear screening criteria. You mentor senior engineers into technical leaders, build an engineering practice that does not depend on you, and hold the bar under commercial pressure. You say "I don't know" when you don't, and you dig in until you do.

  • Experience maintaining a widely used open-source library.
  • Experience with multi-region and disaster-recovery architecture.
  • Experience mapping engineering controls to SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

  • Backend language and craft. You are an expert in TypeScript with Node.js or in Python, and a practitioner in the other. You set our backend and frontend coding patterns, framework choices and upgrade path, and you are a practitioner in at least two other crafts. • React and frontend. You set our full-stack conventions across teams: where logic lives, how APIs serve user interfaces, and how shared components are built and maintained.
  • APIs and data formats. You design REST APIs with OpenAPI from first principles: resource modelling, HTTP semantics, pagination, consistent error formats, versioning, idempotency and rate limiting. You know when to use JSON and when to use Protocol Buffers, and how to evolve both without breaking consumers. You set our API and serialisation standards and decide on exceptions.
  • Data. You are fluent in PostgreSQL, including schema design, indexing, query plans, transactions and zero-downtime migrations with Prisma, TypeORM or SQLAlchemy. You design DynamoDB and MongoDB models around access patterns, use Redis for caching, and choose the right store for each workload. You own our data-architecture standards, including how datastores are introduced and retired.
  • Asynchronous systems and reliability. You design event-driven systems on queues and streams such as SQS, Kafka and BullMQ or Celery, using retries, dead-letter queues and idempotent consumers so that at-least-once delivery is safe. You know the outbox and saga patterns and when orchestration is better than choreography. You own our reference architecture for reliability.
  • Cloud and platform. You have built and run production services on AWS or GCP, both as Lambda functions and as Kubernetes workloads, and you understand the trade-offs between them: cold starts, concurrency, cost, capacity and deployment risk. You define infrastructure as code with Terraform or AWS CDK and release safely with canary and blue/green deployments. With Platform Engineering, you decide when we use serverless and when we use Kubernetes, and you set the reference architectures for both.
  • Testing and quality. You practise test-driven development and expect every team to do the same. You build balanced test suites: unit tests with Jest, Vitest or pytest, integration tests with Testcontainers, contract tests with Pact, and Playwright end-to-end tests that gate releases. You set our quality standard and approve any exceptions to it.
  • Observability and performance. You instrument services with OpenTelemetry and use Datadog and CloudWatch to find problems before users do. You profile with flame graphs, measure p95 and p99 latency, and fix causes rather than symptoms. You set our standards for SLOs, dashboards, alerting and performance budgets, and you lead the hardest incidents to their root cause.
  • Security and identity. You write secure code by default and apply the OWASP Top 10 and API Security Top 10 in practice. You design authentication and authorisation with OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, secure service-to-service traffic with mTLS and workload identity, and integrate identity providers such as Okta, Keycloak and Cognito. You set our identity and security standards and own security reviews with the Security team
  • Architecture and design. You design systems that span many services and teams, and you write architecture decision records that make the trade-offs explicit. You own our technical roadmap and style guide, act as the arbiter on standards, and decide on evidence rather than authority. You are able to trace many symptoms back to a single root cause and fix it once.
  • Engineering practices. You work trunk-based with GitHub Flow, small changes and feature flags, and you know CI/CD pipelines inside out. You have led deprecations and migrations all the way to switching the old system off. You set our Git, CI/CD and dependency policies, and you make large-scale change routine rather than exceptional.
  • AI-first engineering and LLMs. You use Claude Code every day and understand how large language models work: tokens, context windows, cost, structured output, embeddings and retrieval. You have built production features with the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs, including tool calling and evaluations, and designed agentic services with clear guardrails and human review. You set our AI-first operating model, covering approved models and frameworks, Claude Code conventions, evaluation and release gates, and governance.
  • Communication, collaboration and initiative. You communicate clearly and concisely in writing and in conversation, and you adapt your message for engineers, product leaders and executives. You understand complex problems quickly, ask the right questions and confirm shared understanding before acting. You collaborate well across locations and cultures, working asynchronously and handing over cleanly between time zones. You are proactive: you spot problems and opportunities before you are asked, propose solutions and innovations of your own, and drive them through without waiting for instructions.
  • Leadership and behaviours. You lead without authority and influence engineering heads and teams across the organisation. You define the hiring bar for each level, calibrate interviewers and give Talent Acquisition clear screening criteria. You mentor senior engineers into technical leaders, build an engineering practice that does not depend on you, and hold the bar under commercial pressure. You say "I don't know" when you don't, and you dig in until you do.

Preferred qualifications:

  • B.Tech or B.E. in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field.
  • Experience maintaining a widely used open-source library.
  • Experience with multi-region and disaster-recovery architecture.
  • Experience mapping engineering controls to SOC 2 or ISO 27001.
  • Experience with multi-agent systems and agentic frameworks such as LangGraph, Google ADK or the Anthropic Agent SDK.
  • Experience running an engineering-productivity measurement programme.
  • Experience in the second backend language.

About the job:

WPP Open is WPP's AI-enabled marketing operating system, used by brands and agencies around the world. Our engineering teams in India build and run it alongside colleagues in the UK and Europe. As a Principal Engineer you own architecture and engineering standards for full-stack engineering across teams. You stay hands-on and set the bar for hiring.   • Review designs and architecture decision records across teams, challenge assumptions, and make sure decisions are made on evidence and recorded with their trade-offs.
