job.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Recommendations (Core)
job.description:
We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join ML Core, the team that builds the shared ML models behind SoundCloud’s recommendations, search and content understanding. New sounds start on SoundCloud. Our job is to connect artists with the communities that will care about their music, and help listeners discover the gems and emerging scenes they’d never find on their own. Recommendations are our largest area, but you’ll work across problems that share the same foundations: representing users, tracks and creators, and ranking them well. We’re also in the middle of modernizing our stack, moving from classical approaches to deep learning on GPU, and you’ll play a big part in that.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, train and ship models for recommendations (candidate generation, user/item modeling, ranking) and related problems in search and content understanding.
  • Lead the move of key models from classical approaches (e.g., word2vec-style embeddings) to PyTorch-based models trained and served on GPU.
  • Adapt, fine-tune and evaluate open-source embedding and ranking models for our catalog and use cases.
  • Own evaluation end to end: offline metrics, A/B experiments, and making sure offline gains show up online.
  • Work with ML, data and backend engineers to get models into production and keep them healthy, and help set modeling standards across the team.

What we’re looking for:

  • 3+ years building ML systems in production, with end-to-end ownership of at least one ranking, retrieval or recommendation model.
  • Strong deep learning skills in PyTorch (or similar frameworks), and a good grasp of recommendation and retrieval fundamentals (embeddings, two-tower models, learning to rank, multi-objective ranking) and their trade-offs.
  • Solid experience with evaluation and experimentation for ranking systems, including biases in implicit feedback such as clicks and plays.
  • Strong Python; comfortable with large-scale data processing (e.g., Spark/BigQuery) and with getting models to production on a cloud platform (GCP preferred).
  • M.Sc. in a quantitative field or equivalent experience.

Nice to have:

  • Fine-tuning or serving transformer-based embedding/ranking models.
  • Applying LLMs or foundation models to recommendations (content understanding, semantic IDs, generative retrieval, feature generation).
  • Audio or music ML, or multimodal representations.
  • Contextual bandits, RL or causal methods for long-term value.
  • Publications at RecSys, KDD, SIGIR, WSDM, NeurIPS or similar.
  • Experience with ANN/vector search and GPU training or serving at scale.

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification. Research suggests that some applicants may doubt their candidacy, so please submit an application if you are interested.

job.title: Insomniac - Manager, Production HR
job.description:
Job Summary:

WHO ARE YOU?

Do you thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume operating environment where great HR work directly shapes the employee experience? Are you an experienced people leader who can build strong teams, develop scalable systems, and credibly support employees and leaders in the field? If you are passionate about dance culture, people, and operational Human Resources, read on.


WHO ARE WE?

Insomniac produces some of the most innovative, immersive music festivals and events in the world. Enhanced by state-of-the-art lighting, pyrotechnics and sound design, large-scale art installations, theatrical performers and next generation special effects, our events captivate the senses and inspire a unique level of fan interaction.  The quality of the Headliner experience is our top priority.


Insomniac produces 10,000 concerts, club nights and festivals for seven million attendees annually across the globe. Since its inception, Insomniac's events have taken place in 13 countries across five continents. The company's premiere annual event, Electric Daisy Carnival Las Vegas, is the world’s largest dance music festival and attracts more than 525,000 fans over three days. The company was founded by Pasquale Rotella and has been based in Los Angeles since it was formed in 1993.


THE ROLE

Insomniac Events is seeking an experienced Manager, Production HR to lead the HR team supporting high-volume, seasonal, event-based workforces across festivals, concerts, venues, and assigned adjacent business lines. This role leads the Production HR operating model, from annual workforce planning and event coverage through on-site support, employee relations, payroll readiness, and post-show closeout.


The Manager, Production HR leads and develops a team of four full-time and a few HR seasonals. The team supports approximately 5,000 seasonal employees annually. The Manager is accountable for the quality, consistency, and strategic impact of Production HR partnership across a complex calendar of concurrent festivals, concerts, venues, and related workforce programs. This role translates business priorities into scalable workforce strategies, talent plans, employee relations approaches, and HR operating practices that support organizational effectiveness, legal compliance, and an exceptional employee experience. The Manager serves as a senior advisor to Production and operational leaders while building a collaborative, accountable, and sustainable field-HR model.


This position is based in Las Vegas, with a mix of in-office and on-site event work. Travel is expected to be approximately 20-30% annually, with concentrated on-site support during major event periods.


RESPONSIBILITIES

HR Team Leadership and Development

  • Lead, coach, develop, and manage a team of HRBPs, HR Generalists, Coordinators, and assigned operational support roles supporting event operations, production, and related business functions.
  • Establish clear team priorities, service standards, operating rhythms, and performance expectations; ensure consistent, high-quality HR consultation and execution across client groups.
  • Conduct regular performance discussions, provide actionable feedback, support development planning, and address performance concerns for direct reports.
  • Establish annual Production HR goals and individual development objectives aligned to business priorities; review progress at least quarterly, address gaps, and adjust plans as business needs evolve.
  • Assess Production HR team capacity, capability, and coverage; make recommendations regarding staffing, structure, development, and resource allocation.
  • Support recruiting, selection, onboarding, and development of Production HR team members and seasonal HR personnel.
  • Build a collaborative, accountable, inclusive team culture grounded in sound judgment, partnership, continuous improvement, and exceptional service.

Workforce Planning, Event Coverage, and Strategic Partnership

  • Lead the development and execution of people strategies for operational, production, and event-based workforces in alignment with business plans, event calendars, workforce demand, and organizational priorities.
  • Own the annual Production HR event-coverage strategy, including pod assignments, service tiers, on-site deployment decisions, backup coverage, and capacity planning for concurrent events.
  • Ensure each event has a named accountable HR owner, on-site representative when required, and clear escalation path.
  • Partner with senior business leaders to assess workforce effectiveness, staffing needs, talent risks, succession requirements, and opportunities to strengthen team capability and performance.
  • Guide HRBPs and Generalists in translating business needs into practical workforce plans, staffing models, employee engagement strategies, talent development plans, and retention approaches.
  • Serve as a senior HR advisor for complex, sensitive, or high-impact business matters; provide clear recommendations that balance business objectives, employee experience, consistency, and risk.
  • Use workforce analytics, employee feedback, turnover trends, staffing data, and operational insights to identify risks and recommend strategic action.

Employee Relations, Compliance, and Risk Management

  • Oversee complex employee relations matters managed by the Production HR team, including investigations, performance management, corrective action, workers' compensation, accommodations, and terminations.
  • Coach HRBPs and Generalists through complex employee relations, investigations, workers' compensation, wage-and-hour, and corrective-action matters; personally lead only the most sensitive, high-risk, or enterprise-impacting cases.
  • Partner with HR leadership, Legal, Employee Relations, Payroll, Talent Acquisition, and other stakeholders to ensure timely, consistent, and compliant resolution of sensitive matters.
  • Ensure the Production HR team appropriately interprets and applies applicable federal, state, and local employment laws, company policies, and standards.
  • Identify systemic employee relations, compliance, payroll, timekeeping, classification, or organizational risks and develop proactive mitigation plans.
  • Review and recommend enhancements to policies, practices, documentation, and processes to improve consistency, reduce risk, and support evolving business needs.

Operational Excellence and Event Closeout

  • Oversee HRBP and HR Generalist support for the end-to-end seasonal employee lifecycle.
  • Establish event-readiness and post-show closeout standards for seasonal onboarding, employee relations, workers' compensation, payroll exceptions, and compliance items.
  • Maintain a centralized case and closeout tracking process; ensure open items have clear owners, due dates, escalation paths, and documented resolution.
  • Define when HR support is remote, high-touch remote, on-site, or all-hands based on workforce size, event complexity, market novelty, employee relations risk, and historical issue trends.
  • Partner with Talent Acquisition, HR Operations, HRIS, and Payroll teams to ensure workforce readiness, reliable processes, data integrity, and a consistent employee experience across events.
  • Establish scalable tools, templates, training, reporting, and operating procedures that improve the Production HR team's effectiveness and reduce administrative burden.
  • Own the Production HR shared-inbox operating model, including intake, triage, routing, service-level expectations, coverage, escalation, and continuous improvement; identify and resolve bottlenecks that create delayed or inconsistent responses.
  • Partner with corporate Training and Development to assess capability needs and design effective learning plans, development programs, and training resources that strengthen manager effectiveness, employee growth, and operational readiness across event-based teams.
  • Build and maintain an operating dashboard and provide regular reporting to the VP, People Operations on workforce readiness, staffing and onboarding progress, shared-inbox performance, payroll exceptions, employee relations and workers' compensation trends, event closeout status, material risks, and decisions requiring leadership support.
  • Oversee HR-related budgets within the scope of the role and identify opportunities to improve service quality, operational efficiency, and cost effectiveness.
  • Lead cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives that advance HR and business priorities.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • 7-10+ years of progressively responsible HR experience supporting operational leaders.
  • 3-5+ years of demonstrated experience directly leading, coaching, developing, and managing the performance of HR professionals, including establishing priorities, providing feedback, and supporting growth.
  • Demonstrated experience developing people strategies, workforce plans, talent approaches, and organizational solutions for complex, high-volume, seasonal, distributed, or event-based workforces.
  • Strong experience managing complex employee relations matters, investigations, performance management, corrective action, and terminations in partnership with senior leadership and Legal.
  • Strong working knowledge of federal, state, and local employment laws, HR best practices, risk-management principles, and wage-and-hour considerations.
  • Experience supporting live events, production, entertainment, hospitality, retail, or similarly complex operational environments strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders, navigate ambiguity, and translate workforce data and business needs into actionable recommendations.
  • Experience with Workday or a comparable HRIS platform, ADP or comparable payroll systems, time and attendance systems, HR reporting, and workforce analytics.
  • Strong leadership, consultation, communication, project-management, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills.
  • High degree of integrity, discretion, sound judgment, and accountability.
  • Willingness and ability to travel domestically and work nontraditional hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays, during event periods.

WORK ENVIRONMENT


  • Must be able to tolerate loud noise levels & busy environments
  • May work in drastic temperature climates when traveling to event locations
  • Must be willing to travel to work during evening and weekend hours, as required, to meet deadlines 

Applicants for employment in the U.S. must possess work authorization, which does not require sponsorship by Insomniac for a visa.

job.title: Application Security Engineer
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide. At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world. In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing. Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere. Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role Overview

We’re looking for a Cyber Security Engineer to help improve application security across the FT’s cloud-native technology estate. This is a hands-on role focused on making secure engineering easier for product, platform and software engineering teams.

Application security experience is essential for this role. You’ll help improve developer-friendly security guardrails across GitHub-based CI/CD pipelines, application repositories and engineering workflows. This includes working with SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning, vulnerability management and secure coding guidance so that security findings are clear, actionable and owned by the right teams.

You’ll work closely with engineers to support practical threat modelling, triage application vulnerabilities, improve security playbooks and help teams remediate issues in a pragmatic way. You do not need to be a deep AWS or cloud security specialist, but some exposure to AWS, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security would be useful.

We’re looking for someone with practical AppSec experience who wants to grow their impact - someone who enjoys working with engineers, improving tooling and helping security become part of normal delivery rather than a last-minute checkpoint.

What you’ll bring to the role

Application security experience: practical experience identifying, explaining and helping remediate application security risks in modern engineering environments.

Developer-friendly security mindset: you enjoy working with engineers, explaining risks clearly and helping teams adopt secure practices without unnecessary friction.

Vulnerability management experience: experience triaging and tracking application vulnerabilities from sources such as SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, penetration tests, bug bounty reports or third-party advisories.

CI/CD and code security awareness: familiarity with security tooling in development workflows, such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or repository security controls.

Threat modelling awareness: experience participating in, supporting or facilitating lightweight threat-modelling sessions for applications, services or new features.

Automation mindset: ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to reduce manual effort, improve visibility or make security workflows easier.

Cloud security awareness: Some exposure to AWS, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security would be useful, but is not essential.

Growth mindset: willingness to keep developing across application security, cloud security, secure development and modern engineering practices.

Required Experience, Essential

  • Practical experience in application security.
  • Experience working with software engineers to explain and remediate security issues.
  • Familiarity with common web application security risks and secure coding practices.
  • Experience with vulnerability triage, prioritisation and remediation tracking.
  • Experience using or interpreting findings from tools such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or similar.
  • Experience participating in or supporting threat-modelling activities.
  • Ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to automate tasks or improve visibility.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Familiarity with Agile or Scrum ways of working.

Desirable

  • Exposure to AWS security, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security.
  • Experience with Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • Experience with container or Kubernetes security.
  • Experience with bug bounty, penetration testing or security testing programmes.
  • Experience with Splunk or similar logging/SIEM platforms.
  • Exposure to AI security, such as LLM-enabled applications, AI-assisted development workflows or prompt/data leakage risks.
  • Experience building dashboards, metrics or reports to support vulnerability management.
  • Relevant security certifications or training, such as AWS security training, secure coding training, GIAC, ISC2, CREST or equivalent practical experience.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. job.title: Senior Cyber Security Engineer
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide. At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world. In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere. Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role Overview

We’re looking for a Senior Cyber Security Engineer to help mature application and cloud security across the FT’s cloud-native, AWS-hosted technology estate. This role has an approximate 50/50 focus across application security and cloud security, working closely with product, platform and engineering teams to make secure delivery easier by default.

You’ll shape and improve developer-friendly guardrails across GitHub-based CI/CD pipelines, AWS environments and infrastructure-as-code workflows. This includes improving SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning, IaC scanning, vulnerability management and AWS misconfiguration management so that findings are actionable, low-noise and owned by the right teams.

Day to day, you’ll run practical threat-modelling sessions, review application and cloud designs, improve security playbooks, support vulnerability and misconfiguration remediation, and build automation that reduces toil. We’re looking for someone who has demonstrably improved security outcomes in real engineering environments, not just someone with theoretical knowledge of tools or frameworks.

Depending on team structure, you may also mentor or line-manage one or two security engineers, while remaining hands-on and close to the technical work.

What you’ll bring to the role

Application and cloud security experience: practical experience across both application security and cloud security, ideally in AWS-hosted, cloud-native environments.

Developer-friendly security mindset: you know how to work with engineers, explain risk clearly and design controls that help teams move securely without unnecessary friction.

Vulnerability management at scale: experience improving how application vulnerabilities, dependency risks, bug bounty findings, penetration test findings and advisories are identified, prioritised, owned and remediated across engineering teams.

Cloud misconfiguration & vulnerability management: experience identifying and reducing infrastructure-as-code and AWS vulnerabilities & misconfigurations at scale through pragmatic guardrails, tooling and clear remediation paths.

Threat modelling: confidence running lightweight, practical threat-modelling sessions that lead to useful engineering decisions and risk reduction.

CI/CD and code security: hands-on experience with security tooling such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning and IaC scanning.

Automation mindset: ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to reduce toil, improve visibility and surface meaningful risk.

Security leadership: ability to mentor other security engineers and influence engineers across the wider organisation. Depending on team structure, this may include line management.

AI security awareness: experience of leveraging AI to improve and scale appsec and cloud sec controls would be useful, but is not essential.

Key Responsibilities

Improve application security guardrails
 Tune and evolve SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning and related controls so they are actionable, low-noise and useful to engineering teams.

Improve cloud and IaC security guardrails
 Help identify, prioritise and reduce AWS and infrastructure-as-code misconfigurations and vulnerabilities at scale.

Drive vulnerability management
 Improve how application vulnerabilities, dependency risks, bug bounty findings, penetration test findings and third-party advisories are triaged, prioritised and remediated.

Drive cloud misconfiguration management
 Help teams understand, own and remediate cloud security issues using pragmatic, developer-friendly workflows.

Run practical threat modelling
 Facilitate lightweight threat-modelling sessions for new products, features, services and architectural changes.

Build automation and tooling
 Create or improve scripts, integrations, dashboards and workflows that reduce manual effort and make risk easier to understand.

Support secure architecture decisions
 Provide application and cloud security input into design reviews, AWS architecture decisions and larger technical changes.

Partner with engineering teams
 Work closely with product, platform and software engineering teams to embed security into design, delivery and operational practices.

Support incidents and lessons learned
 Provide application and cloud security expertise during incidents and feed lessons learned back into patterns, tooling and guidance.

Mentor others
 Coach security engineers and engineering teams on practical security approaches. Depending on team structure, this may include line management of one or two security engineers.

Required Experience, Essential: 

  • Strong practical experience in application security and cloud security, ideally with a balanced focus across both.
  • Hands-on AWS security experience, including common misconfiguration patterns and practical remediation approaches.
  • Experience improving vulnerability management across engineering teams, including prioritisation, ownership, remediation tracking and noise reduction.
  • Experience in improving cloud or IaC misconfiguration management at scale in a developer-friendly way.
  • Experience integrating, tuning or improving security tooling in CI/CD workflows, such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or IaC scanning.
  • Experience running practical threat-modelling sessions that influence design, delivery or remediation decisions.
  • Ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to automate security workflows or improve visibility.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence engineers and technical leaders without relying on gatekeeping.
  • Evidence of improving application security, cloud security or vulnerability management practices in a real engineering environment.
  • Familiarity with Agile or Scrum ways of working.

Desirable

  • Experience with leveraging AI for AppSec and CloudSec.
  • AWS Certified Security – Speciality or equivalent practical AWS security experience.
  • Terraform or CloudFormation expertise.
  • Incident-management or incident-response experience.
  • Experience with Splunk or similar logging/SIEM platforms.
  • Experience with security metrics, dashboards or reporting that helped drive measurable risk reduction.
  • Experience mentoring or line-managing security engineers.

 

What’s in it for You?

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning.  We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams.

job.title: Operations Coordinator, Nashville Chapter
job.description:
This is a hybrid position requiring a minimum of three days per week in the Nashville, TN office.

 

 

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Recording Academy’s mission is to recognize musical excellence, advocate for the well-being of music makers and ensure music remains an indelible part of our culture. The Academy is a professional membership organization of musicians, producers, engineers, and recording professionals that is dedicated to improving the cultural condition and quality of life for music and its makers.

 

We’re looking for a highly motivated, idea-generating self-starter who will coordinate office operations, high-quality initiatives, programs, and content with professionalism for the Nashville Chapter. As part of the Nashville Chapter team, you will be responsible for developing and managing programs to ensure member retention, working with local outreach committees, and building coalitions in our Chapter city as well as the surrounding Chapter region. You will also be responsible for the day-to-day logistics of the Nashville Chapter office. You are a team player ready to roll up your sleeves with impeccable follow-through.

 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 

Work with the Senior Executive Director to coordinate operations for the Nashville Chapter office:

  • Liaison with the property manager and the Recording Academy’s Facilities Operations department.
  • Manage the schedule for shared meeting rooms including communicating with various stakeholders.
  • Liaison with service vendors including researching best companies, scheduling services, discussing prices, and managing invoicing.
  • Know the building systems including security, internet, fire safety, etc.
  • Coordinate in-office artist visits with Academy staff.
  • Handle all office supplies and needs including general office supplies, postage, kitchen supplies, mail, UPS, FedEx, etc.

 

Facilitate the Chapter’s Grammy U Program, interns, and temps:

  • Recruit and facilitate interviews and the hiring process for Chapter Grammy U Reps.
  • In coordination with the Grammy U Program lead, work with the Grammy U Rep in training on programming, membership presentations and outreach, program Invitations and RSVP process, and copy writing.
  • In coordination with the Chapter Manager, structure a regular meeting schedule to monitor university and membership outreach and set yearly goals for Grammy U membership growth.
  • Facilitate the recruitment, interview, and hiring process for temps and interns.

 

Serve as the staff liaison for a variety of Chapter committees:

  • Work with committee chairs to schedule meetings and minutes.
  • Implement follow-up materials including collaborating with the Chapter Manager on related program initiatives.

 

Execute the Chapter’s social media marketing initiatives and strategy:

  • Work closely with the Chapter Manager on each program’s social media needs, creating the social plan strategy in partnership with the Academy’s social media team and set timeline.
  • Manage the day-to-day administration of the Chapter’s Facebook Group and work to grow followers including best practices to utilize the platform.
  • Manage Chapter’s social media calendar.

 

Legal Agreements:

  • Facilitate all vendor and performance agreements and releases pertaining to Chapter programs and initiatives.
  • Work closely with the Academy’s Legal Affairs and Executive Director department on agreements.
  • Ensure timely delivery and receipt of signatures from vendors and program participants.

 

Programming:

  • Attend all Chapter programs and Board meetings.
  • Work closely with the Academy’s Communications department to book and manage Getty photographers and security guards as it pertains to Chapter programs.
  • Ensure contracts for all security and catering/bartender requests are reviewed with the Academy’s Legal Affairs Department, signed promptly, and paid according to each vendor’s desired schedule, and event confirmation details are appropriately relayed ahead of each event.
  • Coordinate with the Chapter Manager in liaising with the social media and editorial teams, coordinating support and activations for Chapter events.
  • Track RSVPs and coordinate check-in/registration at programs.
  • Other programming duties as needed.

 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s Degree required, preferably in music business or related.
  • 3+ years of executive level administration experience in the music industry.
  • Proficiency in Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and various Microsoft applications.
  • Strong marketing skills through social media.
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain composure under pressure and make decisions/problem solve in high-stress situations.
  • Outstanding organizational, time management, and multitasking skills.
  • Adaptability to change and openness to innovative ideas.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Proven ability to foster teamwork and contribute positively to team dynamics.
  • Must be proactive with the ability to manage upwards.
  • Ability to uphold the highest levels of integrity and ethics.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAN ROLES

 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time.

 

The employee will be required to lift and/or move up to 60 pounds.

 

 

SALARY AND BENEFITS

 

The starting rate for this position is $21.70 to $23.50 per hour, benchmarked against industry standards. Rates for positions required to be in specific geographic locations reflect the corresponding labor market. 
 
The actual offer extended will depend on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and the role's requirements. Positions working 20+ hours per week also receive our comprehensive benefits package (with medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, generous paid time off, and more). Click here for an overview of our company benefits.


Explore our career opportunities to join a team that values creativity, innovation, and diversity. 

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

 

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

 

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination, access to benefits and training, recruitment, hiring, transfer, and social and recreational programs.

job.title: Senior Account Executive, Associate Practice (Health)
job.description:
We are in relentless pursuit of an equitable and inspiring workplace that is respectful of all, reflects and represents the world in which we live, and fosters trust, collaboration and belonging. Consistent with this approach, we hire the best qualified candidates for all positions.

About the Edelman Associate Practice

The Edelman Associate Practice is the foundation of our client service talent and the launchpad for early-career professionals who want to shape the future of communications. Bringing together emerging talent across communications, public affairs, and advisory disciplines, the practice is designed to develop well-rounded, integrated practitioners from day one. Associates contribute meaningfully to client work across industries and sectors—building strong fundamentals in research, writing, project management, and media engagement—while gaining exposure to diverse clients and capabilities. Rather than being confined to a single track at the start of their careers, Associates are empowered to explore, collaborate across teams, and discover where their interests and strengths can make the greatest impact.


Rooted in community and driven by growth, the Associate Practice combines hands-on client experience with structured development, peer connection, and dedicated leadership support. As the industry evolves, so does the role—blending operational excellence with increasing strategic contribution and AI-enabled innovation. Associates learn not only how to execute exceptional work, but how to think critically, solve complex problems, and build the judgment and confidence that define Edelman excellence. This is more than a first step in your career—it’s an opportunity to grow alongside a connected cohort, contribute to transformative client work, and help redefine what modern communications looks like. 


About the Role

Senior Account Executives (SAEs) are strong communicators who serve as trusted connectors between clients, teams, and media or stakeholder networks. They show emerging leadership by anticipating needs, solving problems proactively, and influencing both internal and external stakeholders with clarity and confidence.  SAEs demonstrate supportive ownership of workstreams, contribute to strategic planning and execution, and engage with senior leadership and clients. As they continue to build their expertise, SAEs may begin to specialize in a particular practice area based on their skills, experience, and professional goals. 


In this role, you will primarily support work across Health clients with U.S. and global footprints. These clients are in regulated industries, specifically and such as medical technology, health services, animal health, and more.  Your day-to-day work may include: 

  • Media landscape research, engagement, and materials development
  • Social media campaigns and content creation
  • Executive visibility and thought leadership initiatives
  • Proactively researching and analyzing industry trends
  • Administrative reporting, tracking, and operational management

Key Responsibilities  

Client & Account Support  

  • Actively support senior team members in day-to-day client interactions around assigned projects, helping to manage deliverables and ensure alignment with objectives.  
  • Actively support senior team members in client calls, providing tactical counsel, and proactively flagging issues, risks, or opportunities.  
  • Build strong relationships rooted in reliability, responsiveness, and trust, focused on internal audiences and stakeholders in addition to client interactions

Strategic Planning & Program Management  

  • Support senior leads around client strategy development, message framing, and campaign planning through research, trends analysis, operational activation, presentation creation, etc.
  • Assist with integrated program execution across functions, ensuring alignment with goals, timelines, and budgets.  
  • Collaborate internally and throughout the firm with creative, digital, and analytics partners, for example, to deliver seamless, multi-channel campaigns.  

Content & Storytelling  

  • Write and/or edit high-quality materials such as press releases, op-eds, briefing documents, messaging, talking points, stakeholder materials, or other client-facing content.  
  • Translate complex scientific, technical, and business information into clear, compelling, and accessible narratives that connect to business and reputation outcomes.  
  • Review and refine content to ensure quality and consistency in client deliverables.  
  • Show eagerness, interest, and willingness to learn, as well as developing a strong understanding and/or curiosity to help distill and understand  complex, evolving healthcare topics and issues for varying stakeholder groups
  • Review and refine content with a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail, ensuring client deliverables are clear, consistent, polished, and aligned with approved messaging, key stats and facts, and with consideration to overarching operational priorities. 

Media & Stakeholder Relations  

  • Support proactive outreach to journalists, influencers, and conference organizers; secure earned media and stakeholder engagement results; do so under the guidance of senior external engagement team members.  
  • Monitor trends and provide recommendations that shape client strategy, response, and day-to-day real time opportunity potential.  
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships across media, industry, and relevant stakeholder networks.  

Executive Visibility and Thought Leadership

  • Conduct research and provide clear recommendations for conferences, awards, and media engagements for executives.
  • Conduct both company-level and peer-level competitor audits.
  • Draft messaging framework and/or platform development for executives.
  • Manage logistics for media and event engagements, including preparation of talking points, briefing materials, etc.

Leadership & Team Development  

  • Provide and seek guidance and feedback with colleagues both junior and senior to foster their growth and development.  
  • Model professionalism, collaboration, and inclusion; support performance and actively support team performance and development conversations.  
  • Contribute to new business initiatives through research, insights, idea development, or presentation design refinement. 

  

Basic Qualifications:

  • 2 years of professional experience in communications, public relations, or a related discipline. 
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven ability to manage multiple small or medium-sized projects simultaneously  
  • Clear understanding of the clients’ businesses and their missions, as well as their key stakeholders that could include but are not limited to consumers, patients, clinicians, employees, investors, regulators, media, vendors, partners, other businesses/organizations, etc.
  • Ability to functionally and successfully work in a dedicated time zone, but with day-to-day team members internally who dispersed throughout multiple time zones and office locations.
  • Demonstrated ability to help develop communication programming and plans, implement integrated tactics and impart knowledge to junior account team members and peers.
  • Able to perform well under pressure and be a team player.
  • Strong research, writing and editing skills, as well as the ability to interact with clients professionally and show active engagement internally as well.
  • Demonstrate strong intellectual curiosity and the ability to quickly absorb new information, ask thoughtful questions, and rapidly build an understanding of clients, their businesses, and the broader industry landscape.
  • Operate with a proactive, self-starting mindset and a strong sense of urgency, anticipating needs and moving work forward without requiring significant direction.
  • Thrive in a fast-moving environment, adapting quickly to shifting priorities and balancing speed with sound judgment and attention to detail.

$60,000 - $80,000 a year

job.title: Senior Account Supervisor, Special Situations & Investor Relations Communications
job.description:
We are in relentless pursuit of an equitable and inspiring workplace that is respectful of all, reflects and represents the world in which we live, and fosters trust, collaboration and belonging. Consistent with this approach, we hire the best qualified candidates for all positions.

About Our Team

Edelman Smithfield advises companies when the stakes are highest. We sit at the intersection of capital markets, reputation and strategy, helping leadership teams earn trust, command attention and win support from investors when it matters most.

 

Backed by the scale of the world’s largest independent communications firm, our team brings deep capital markets expertise. We are a team of experienced advisors and former in-house IROs, sell-side analysts and investment bankers who partner directly with Boards and C-suites on IPOs, transformational M&A, activist campaigns, restructurings, earnings inflection points and market-moving moments of change.


The Opportunity

The Senior Account Supervisor, Special Situations & Investor Relations (SSIR), will be responsible for developing and executing IR and financial communications programs of our clients. Ideal candidates will come from former investment and research analyst roles and/or will have direct investor relations experience, either with an agency or in-house IR position. Financial communications experience is preferred. The candidate must be fluent in the capital markets and possess a strong comfort level in counseling senior executives and investor relations teams of publicly traded companies on matters including disclosure, earnings and guidance, governance, marketing, investor targeting and relationship building, M&A, capital raises and crisis situations.

Manage and participate hands on in team development of messaging and positioning of company business model and corporate developments.

  • Ensure team is proactive and highly responsive to client needs, anticipating upcoming deliverables and taking accountability for proper execution. Ensure junior staff is trained, supportive of team efforts and paying sufficient attention to detail.
  • Participate with senior partners in new business preparation and participate in new business activity to ultimately serve those accounts.

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • At least 6 years of relevant experience within the capital markets, including either with a sell-or buy-side firm, investor relations agency or in an IR role at a public company
  • A bachelor’s degree in business, finance, accounting or related discipline or equivalent work experience

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong comfort level in counseling senior executives of publicly traded companies on IR related and financial communications matters.

job.title: 21GRAMS- Account Director
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Job Summary:

Real Chemistry is looking for a Account Director to join our growing team!

21GRAMS, a Real Chemistry subsidiary is an advertising agency born to make healthcare more human. Not just in our work, but in the way we conduct business, approach client relationships, and treat each other. It’s a place where people subscribe to the adage, “Be good to each other, but hard on the work.” A place where people are not just in it for the paycheck, but to make a dent in the universe. Sound like you?

21GRAMS is in search of an Account Director. In addition to being the diplomatic face of the brand, both internally and externally, they accept the role of manager, liaison, thinker, and problem-solver. The Account Director leads broad-based, complex work-streams, is critical to the smooth running of Accounts, is a credible advisor and has very strong marketing communications experience.

The Account Director has mastered communications, project management, and has a strong point of view on the pharmaceutical side. This person should be able to confidently lead client projects and internal teams, encouraging smart, effective and integrated solutions, and always deliver results and client satisfaction. This position offers the opportunity to become an internal leader while developing strong relationships with clients.

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, Lambertville or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What you'll do:

  • Establish and maintain productive working relationships to drive agency success
  • Demonstrate understanding and knowledge of key messages/message platform, data, and promotional story for brand and competition
  • Develop and align on key agency/client documents that drive success (e.g., Project and Creative Briefs)
  • Read and interpret analytics around programming, tactics, and overall brand performance (e.g., metrics, KPIs, goals)
  • Negotiate, when necessary, to meet and deliver on client needs while managing agency resources and projects effectively
  • Continuously identify new opportunities to make recommendations based on customers, markets, and competitive environments, including corresponding rationales
  • Lead by example: exhibit professional conduct while providing ongoing leadership as a role model for the team
  • Demonstrate a solutions-oriented approach and collaborate across teams to drive success
  • Pursue business objectives, while developing talent and preserving the 21GRAMS culture
  • Supervise, train, and mentor team members to develop the skills and careers of others by providing guidance

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values, Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I", genuinely resonate with how you work and lead.
  • You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

What you should have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing or a related field or equivalent
    experience is required
  • 5-7 years marketing experience, agency environment preferred.
  • Strong ability to multi-task and manage multiple projects with strong organizational
    skills.
  • Excellent business communication skills
  • Strong written and oral communication and presentations skills
  • Experience working on Therapeutic brands a plus
  • Previous experience managing junior staff preferred

Pay Range: $135,000.00-$155,000.00

The anticipated salary range for this position is listed above. Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and internal parity.

In addition to base salary, Real Chemistry offers a comprehensive benefits package and a variety of programs designed to support our employees' well-being, growth, and success.

Real Chemistry reserves the right to update compensation and benefits programs at any time.

 

Real Chemistry is proud to be Great Place to Work® certified; check out what our people shared about our culture and workplace on our Great Places to Work Profile here.

Real Chemistry offers a comprehensive benefit program and perks, tailored to your region. Globally, this includes offices in our key markets with free snacks to keep you running all day long, generous holiday and paid time off, options for private medical, dental, and vison plans, and support in saving for the future. job.title: AI Engineer
job.description:
Opportunity

Brunswick is on an exciting journey to harness the power of artificial intelligence and data science to enhance the way we work and the advice we provide to clients. As we continue to expand our AI capabilities, we are looking for an AI Engineer to join our growing team.

In this role, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining AI-powered applications that deliver real value across the business. Working closely with our existing AI team, you will help build innovative solutions using modern AI technologies, with a particular focus on large language models (LLMs).

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with hands-on experience developing and deploying AI applications who enjoys solving complex problems, working with a high degree of autonomy, and turning emerging technologies into practical, high-quality products.

You will thrive in this role if you are curious, creative, and passionate about applying AI to solve real-world business challenges. You take pride in writing robust, maintainable code and enjoy collaborating with colleagues to continuously improve and expand our AI capabilities.

About the Role

Your main responsibilities will include:

  • Support, run, and iterate existing AI applications.
  • Design, develop, deploy, and maintain new AI applications which can be scaled across multiple business use cases, driving operational and commercial outcomes.
  • Trial and test solutions with end users to iterate and optimise them.
  • Research and analyse data sets using a variety of statistical and machine learning techniques.
  • Track and understand the evolving AI landscape.

What We’re Looking For

The successful candidate will be a highly professional, well-rounded individual with strong problem-solving skills, engineering expertise, strategic thinking, and excellent interpersonal skills. They will have a strong academic background complemented by an outstanding career to date. Standout candidates will demonstrate:

  • Experience building solutions with large language models (LLMs) and a deep understanding of the broader generative AI landscape.
  • Experience designing datasets, conducting model evaluations, and fine-tuning foundation models to improve task-specific performance.
  • Strong Python development skills, including experience writing production-quality code.
  • Experience with front-end technologies such as JavaScript, React, HTML, and CSS.
  • A solid understanding of statistics and machine learning fundamentals.
  • An undergraduate degree in a quantitative discipline, such as Mathematics or Computer Science, or equivalent relevant industry experience.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • The ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with changing priorities and an iterative, user-focused approach to development.
  • Curiosity, a strong sense of ownership, and the ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
  • Previous experience in professional services would be advantageous.
  • Experience developing cloud applications on Microsoft Azure would be advantageous.
  • Experience with DevOps practices and tools (e.g. CI/CD, Git) would be desirable.
  • Knowledge of, or experience with, secure software development practices would be advantageous.

Why Join Us

Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.

About Brunswick

Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes. 

Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. APAC AI Media Orchestration Senior Director – Japan

This newly created leadership role within Media Futures Group (WPP Media's bespoke agency for Google) brings together media expertise, practical AI delivery and organizational transformation. Based in Japan, you will help pioneer agentic workflows at scale for Google, connecting regional and global capabilities with the needs of the local market. Your remit is to turn AI ambition into everyday practice: identifying high-impact opportunities, piloting and deploying AI agents across live campaigns, developing solutions for Japan-specific needs, and helping teams adopt new ways of working. You will partner with senior client and agency stakeholders, cross-functional media teams, and APAC AI specialists to move successful experiments into repeatable, measurable solutions. We are looking for someone who understands how media works, brings strong practical fluency in generative AI, and can lead change from initial use case through deployment and sustained adoption.

What you’ll do
  • Lead AI adoption in Japan. Own the execution of the Japan market AI agenda, aligning local priorities with regional and global capabilities.
  • Deploy AI into live media workflows. Partner with strategy, planning and activation teams to identify opportunities, pilot verified agents, and embed successful workflows into campaign delivery.
  • Build and localize solutions. Architect, localize, test, deploy and maintain custom AI tools and agents that address Japan-specific business and workflow needs.
  • Enable teams and lead change. Deliver practical workshops, training and onboarding, while working with cross-functional leaders to overcome adoption barriers and embed new ways of working.
  • Advise senior stakeholders. Translate business challenges into actionable AI initiatives, clearly communicating opportunities, trade-offs and results to client and agency leadership.
  • Measure, govern and scale. Track adoption, quality, productivity and business impact; uphold enterprise standards for responsible AI; and share successful local innovations across the wider APAC network.
What we’re looking for
  • Substantial relevant experience across media strategy, marketing transformation, consulting, marketing technology or adjacent disciplines, with demonstrated leadership of complex initiatives.
  • Business-level or native Japanese and professional English—both essential.
  • Strong understanding of the media ecosystem, including how campaigns are planned, activated, optimized and measured.
  • Deep understanding of Japan’s media landscape, audiences and cultural context.
  • A track record of driving AI adoption across teams, with hands-on experience piloting or deploying AI workflows or custom agents.
  • Strong practical fluency in generative AI and AI agents, including familiarity with GenAI tools and large language models.
  • Working knowledge of prompt and context engineering, agent testing and evaluation, and responsible AI practices.
  • Proven success leading large-scale change or technology adoption across cross-functional teams.
  • Experience working with major global brands and influencing senior stakeholders.
  • Strong strategic and analytical judgment, with the ability to translate complex business needs into practical solutions and measurable outcomes.
  • Confidence working across local, regional and global teams in a fast-evolving environment.
Why this role is different This is an opportunity to help define how agentic AI becomes part of everyday media delivery for Google, one of the world’s most influential technology brands. You will help build the playbook for Japan: shaping priorities, piloting new workflows, developing local capabilities and turning successful use cases into solutions that can scale. The impact spans both the work and the people delivering it—improving how campaigns run while equipping teams to achieve more with AI. With dedicated Japan ownership and connections across APAC, you will have the opportunity to influence local delivery and contribute to a broader transformation.

job.description:

Role Purpose

The Governance & Assurance Analyst supports WPP's governance, certification, assurance, and digital risk management activities.

The role helps maintain governance documentation, support certification and audit readiness activities, coordinate evidence collection, and contribute

to client assurance requests and governance reporting.

Working closely with Strategy & Risk, Technical Security Governance, Assurance, Privacy, Legal, Enterprise Technology, and business stakeholders,

the Governance & Assurance Analyst helps ensure governance processes remain effective, documentation remains current, and evidence required

for certifications, audits, and client assurance activities is readily available.

A key focus of the role is supporting the day-to-day operation of WPP's Information Security Management System (ISMS), maintaining certification

readiness, and coordinating governance and assurance activities across the organisation.

Key Responsibilities

Governance & Policy Support

Maintain governance frameworks, policies, standards, procedures, and related documentation.

Support periodic reviews and updates of governance artefacts.

Maintain mappings between policies, standards, controls, and certification requirements.

Assist with governance forums, working groups, and documentation reviews.

Support the preparation of governance materials, meeting outputs, and action tracking.

Provide research and analysis to support governance activities and decision-making.

Digital Risk Governance Support

Support governance reporting activities related to digital risk management.

Assist with the collection and analysis of governance-related metrics and indicators.

Maintain governance dashboards, scorecards, and reporting materials.

Track governance actions and follow-up activities.

Support reviews of governance processes and documentation.

ISO 27001 & Certification Support

Support the operation of the Information Security Management System (ISMS).

Coordinate activities required to support ISO 27001 certification and surveillance audits.

Maintain certification-related records, registers, and supporting documentation.

Coordinate evidence collection and stakeholder engagement activities required for audits.

Track audit findings, corrective actions, and improvement activities through to closure.

Support management review preparation and governance reporting.

Help maintain ongoing audit and certification readiness.

Client Assurance Support

Coordinate responses to client security, governance, risk, and compliance due diligence requests.

Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to gather information required for assurance activities.

Maintain reusable assurance content, responses, and supporting evidence.

Track assurance requests and response status.

Support the continuous improvement of assurance documentation and response quality.

Evidence Management & Audit Readiness

Maintain repositories used to support governance, certification, audit, and assurance activities.

Coordinate evidence collection across relevant business functions.

Ensure evidence is current, appropriately classified, and available for authorised use.

Maintain evidence ownership information, review dates, and supporting metadata.

Identify missing, outdated, or incomplete evidence and coordinate remediation activities.

Support internal, external, certification, client, and regulatory reviews through effective evidence coordination.

Reporting & Operational Improvement

Support the development of governance dashboards, scorecards, metrics, and reporting packs.

Analyse governance and assurance data to identify trends and reporting insights.

Support the standardisation of governance documentation, evidence collection, and reporting practices.

Identify opportunities for process improvements and raise recommendations to management.

Contribute to the continuous improvement of governance operational processes and reporting effectiveness.

Skills & Experience Required

Must-Haves

Fluent English, written and verbal.

Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Risk Management, Audit, Compliance, Business Administration, or a related discipline, or

equivalent relevant experience.

2-4 years of experience in governance, information security, compliance, audit, risk management, assurance, or a related discipline.

Experience supporting an ISO 27001-based management system, audit programme, or certification activity.

Understanding of governance frameworks, controls, audit principles, and certification requirements.

Experience supporting audits, assurance reviews, or certification activities.

Experience coordinating evidence collection and documentation activities.

Strong reporting, documentation, and organisational skills.

Ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Strong communication and stakeholder coordination skills.

Ability to manage multiple priorities in a global environment.

Nice-to-Have

ISO 27001 Foundation, Lead Implementer, Lead Auditor, or similar qualification.

CISA, CISM, CRISC, CISSP, or equivalent certification.

Exposure to frameworks such as SOC 2, GDPR, NIS2, or similar.

Experience supporting client assurance or security questionnaire activities.

Experience using GRC, audit, compliance, or certification management platforms.

Experience within a large multinational organisation.

Key Behaviours & Competencies

Governance Awareness

Understands the importance of governance, accountability, and effective documentation in supporting organisational objectives.

Analytical Thinking

Uses structured analysis and evidence-based reasoning to support governance activities and reporting.

Quality Focus

Maintains attention to detail and supports high-quality governance and assurance outcomes.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Works effectively with stakeholders across business and technical teams.

Communication

Communicates clearly and professionally with a range of audiences.

Organisation & Planning

Demonstrates a structured approach to documentation, coordination, reporting, and action tracking.

Continuous Learning

Seeks opportunities to improve processes, skills, and ways of working.

Professional Integrity

Acts with objectivity, accountability, professionalism, and discretion.

What This Role Explicitly Does Not Do

This role does not:

Own governance frameworks, policies, or standards.

Own cyber security strategy.

Own enterprise risk management processes or risk registers.

Own Digital Risk Governance frameworks.

Make risk acceptance or risk treatment decisions.

Own technical security controls, security architecture, engineering, or operational security functions.

Perform incident response, vulnerability management, monitoring, or security operations activities.

Act as Internal Audit or provide independent assurance.

Own regulatory compliance programmes.

Serve as the accountable owner for ISO 27001 or certification outcomes.

Own the ISMS.

Design governance operating models or policy architectures.

Approve policies, standards, exceptions, or governance decisions unless formally authorised.

Replace the accountability of risk owners, control owners, policy owners, or business stakeholders.

 

Who you are:

You're open: We are inclusive and collaborative; we encourage the free exchange of ideas; we respect and celebrate diverse views. We are open-minded: to new ideas, new partnerships, new ways of working.

You're optimistic: We believe in the power of creativity, technology and talent to create brighter futures or our people, our clients and our communities. We approach all that we do with conviction: to try the new and to seek the unexpected.

You're extraordinary: we are stronger together: through collaboration we achieve the amazing. We are creative leaders and pioneers of our industry; we provide extraordinary every day.

 

What we'll give you:

Passionate, inspired people – We aim to create a culture in which people can do extraordinary work.

Scale and opportunity – We offer the opportunity to create, influence and complete projects at a scale that is unparalleled in the industry.

Challenging and stimulating work – Unique work and the opportunity to join a group of creative problem solvers. Are you up for the challenge?

This is a hands-on editing role requiring extensive tape-cutting experience, along with exceptional editorial judgment and sophisticated audio storytelling instincts. The successful candidate will be an accomplished audio editor who can shape raw improvised material into polished, compelling programming under intense deadline pressure.


Main responsibilities

  • Edits each weekly episode to an exceptional standard, bringing a well-trained ear for tape, sharp editorial instincts and masterful editing skills. Works quickly and efficiently to craft tight, compelling listening experiences and versions across radio and podcast.
  • Quickly identifies the strongest moments, cuts what doesn’t work and makes decisive editorial choices that preserve the spontaneity, comedic timing and energy of the live recording  under demanding production deadlines. 
  • Mixes audio bumpers and stings to brand the programme with pod-safe music and taglines. 
  • Demonstrates excellent asset management skills and a thorough understanding of audio specifications across CBC publishing platforms, including file compression, formatting and audio optimization to ensure the highest possible sound quality. 
  • Researches news stories, current events and cultural developments to identify material with strong comedic and editorial potential.
  • Develops, pitches, researches, and writes compelling scripts (quiz rounds), and other program elements, demonstrating extensive writing experience and exceptional writing, editing, and proofreading abilities, with an advanced command of grammar, vocabulary, and language. 
  • Contributes to daily editorial meetings, helping shape the program’s coverage of the news and identify opportunities for satire, parody and commentary.
  • Exercises sound journalistic judgment in evaluating stories, sources, facts and comedic material.
  • Fact-checks scripts and research, verifies information.  
  • Edits and re-writes scripts for the host and contributors, responding to editorial changes and troubleshooting under deadline.
  • Participates in control room operations and live broadcasts, helping coordinate timing, technical elements and communication among the host, guests and production team.
  • Contributes ideas and material for the program’s social media, digital platforms and established TikTok channel, adapting content for different audiences and formats.
  • Identifies emerging comedic voices and perspectives, contributing to a program that reflects the diversity of the communities CBC serves.
  • Supports the executive producer in preparing production plans, coordinating resources and tracking production requirements.
  • Liaises with the in-person audience, welcoming them into the Toronto Broadcast Centre each week. 
  • Keeps abreast of Canadian comedy and talent, competing programming, cultural developments, broadcasting trends and current affairs.
  • Contributes to a positive, respectful and collaborative workplace culture in a team that writes together for much of the week. 
  • Performs other related production duties as required.



Your profile

  • University degree or equivalent combination of education, training and relevant experience, including internships, job shadowing, workshops or other learning opportunities.
  • Experience in journalism, radio broadcasting, podcasting, digital media or a related production environment.
  • Exceptional audio editing skills, with a proven track record of excellence in cutting and shaping broadcast and podcast programming. 
  • Strong journalistic instincts and demonstrated news judgment, including the ability to assess stories quickly and accurately under deadline.
  • Demonstrated ability to write with clarity, precision, creativity and personality, adapting tone and style for comedic contexts.
  • Outstanding research and editorial skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information, identify compelling angles and translate current events into engaging, intelligent content.
  • A strong interest in comedy, satire and current affairs, with an instinct for identifying the comedic potential in news and cultural stories.
  • Extensive experience in live broadcast or live event production, with the ability to manage competing priorities, adapt quickly to changing circumstances, and remain calm and decisive under pressure.
  • Strong organizational skills  and the ability to manage competing priorities while meeting tight deadlines.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work constructively with hosts, performers, writers and colleagues.
  • An interest in discovering and developing new talent and bringing a range of voices and perspectives to the program.
  • A distinctive perspective, lived experience or area of expertise that can enrich the program’s content.
  • Flexibility to adapt to changing production needs, work patterns and hours, including one evening a week (Thursday.) 

Relevant knowledge and skills

  • Advanced knowledge of audio editing software and digital production tools.
  • Significant experience writing and editing material for live performance and broadcast.
  • Excellent command of Canadian English, spelling, grammar and editorial conventions.
  • Experience developing content for social media and digital platforms, with an understanding of audience engagement and platform-specific storytelling is an asset. 
  • Exceptional digital video editing skills are an asset.
  • Familiarity with CBC journalistic standards, policies and practices, particularly as they apply to satire, parody, opinion and commentary.
  • Awareness of the editorial considerations involved in producing comedy based on real people, events and current affairs.
  • Knowledge of radio and podcast production workflows, studio operations and live broadcast techniques.
  • Familiarity with social media publishing, content moderation and digital audience development.
  • Knowledge of Canadian comedy, performers, writers and the broader cultural landscape.
  • Familiarity with relevant union agreements, including those involving the Writers Guild of Canada (WGC) and the Canadian Media Guild (CMG), is an asset.

The ideal candidate combines a journalist’s curiosity with a comedy producer’s imagination. They understand that great comedy begins with great research, thrive on collaboration and can move confidently between developing an idea, writing a script, editing others’ scripts, checking the facts, editing audio and helping bring a live program to air. They will bring sound judgment, creative energy and a collaborative approach to finding the balance between being funny, being fair and being accurate.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
